# Changelog

All notable changes to Agent Farm. Detailed release notes live in the built-in guide (`Agent Farm: Open Guide` → Release Notes / Sürüm Notları).

## 3.654.0 - OpenCode's start-up lock race is retried once (X-329) (2026-09-24)

- **Two OpenCode starts in the same second no longer lose one of them
  (X-329).** On a fresh data home the two race OpenCode's first-use migration
  and one used to die within ~1.5 s with `database is locked` or
  `Failed query: CREATE TABLE …` — the task row simply failed. A run that dies
  that way in its first seconds is now started once more after 2 s; a second
  failure is shown as it is. Both doors do it: a headless task (its output
  file keeps the first attempt and says why it ran again) and the Console's
  shared OpenCode process (a card opened during the wait joins the retry).

## 3.653.0 - A panel kept open across a redraw is drawn solid, not re-faded (U-146) (2026-09-24)

- **The ⏳ background-task panel on the Console strip is no longer
  see-through (U-146).** The strip redraws every 120ms while a turn runs, and
  the component that keeps a panel open across a redraw first asked the page
  what was under the pointer — which computed the new panel closed — and then
  opened it with the ordinary 80ms fade. So the panel spent most of its life
  fading in from nothing. A panel held open this way now appears at once, with
  no fade; the same goes for a free-floating panel re-opened after a redraw
  (the Console's session list, the Live Timeline, Toolbox and Missions rows).

## 3.652.0 - Live Timeline dots and bars open their panel at once, even under a redraw (U-149) (2026-09-24)

- **A dot or a bar opens its panel in 200ms (U-149).** Every lane box carries a
  button role, so the tooltip component gave it the 700ms wait meant for
  pressable controls — and the page redraws itself every few seconds, so the
  wait often never ended. Lane dots and bars now open in 200ms; the row's own
  toggle boxes keep the slower open.
- **A redraw during the wait no longer kills it.** The free-panel open timer
  gave up silently when the page replaced its trigger under a still pointer;
  it now opens the trigger standing at the same point, and nothing when there
  is none.
- **The ⏱ subject picker left the paragraph.** It sits beside the Swim lanes
  heading as `⏱ tests as [...]`, and the explanation under it is shorter.

## 3.651.0 - A card in a baton relay wears its leg in the session list (S-91) (2026-09-23)

- **The relay leg is on the card, not only on the open session (S-91).** The
  `⑂ N` chip used to live on the status row under the conversation, so the
  list on the left could not tell a relay run from any other. Every live card
  in a chain now carries it on its second line, right after the sign-in pill
  (first on the line when there is none), in the same small size so the card
  keeps its height; hovering it opens the same chain panel — the chain, the
  predecessor, the successor and the brake. A card no baton touched draws
  nothing new.

## 3.650.0 - A re-indexed session keeps the search shards it was re-indexed into (X-356) (2026-09-23)

- **The search index stopped deleting its own fresh work (X-356).** When a
  transcript changed, its search shards were rebuilt under the same file names
  — but the old ones were cleared by a delete that was never waited for, so it
  was still in flight when the new ones were written, and removed them. The
  answer stayed right (a missing shard is rebuilt on the spot), but every
  changed session was re-read from its transcript again on the next search, and
  the next, instead of once. Measured: five changed transcripts, 20 shards
  before, 5 left once the deletes landed. The old shards are now cleared before
  the new ones are written, so a live session is parsed once per change. This
  was also the test suite's long-standing intermittent red in
  `test_search_speed.js` (load decided whether a delete landed before or after
  the write).

## 3.649.0 - The phone opens a real Console session: /new <agent> [prompt] (U-138) (2026-09-23)

- **An eleventh launch door (U-138).** `/agent <name> <prompt>` stays what it
  was — a headless run that answers once in the thread. `/new <agent> [prompt]`
  opens a real **Console session** instead: numbered in `/sessions`, its turn
  cards sent to this chat, steerable from the phone, and a message written
  while it works waits in the queue for the turn to end. It starts like every
  other door — seeded from what that agent was last run with and recorded
  afterwards — in the agent's own folder, under the window's active project.
  A bare `/new` means the agent the chat is bound to; a name nobody has is
  refused rather than run on the bound agent.
- **Budgeted for its whole life.** A spent daily cap refuses the door before
  anything spawns, and every turn the session takes — from the phone or from
  the window — is billed against `agentFarm.telegram.maxDailyUSD`. A session
  that cannot start (a missing CLI, a sign-in that is not on this machine) now
  says why on the phone, not only in the window.

## 3.648.0 - A wiki category is renamed, or merged into another, in all three places it lives (U-125) (2026-09-23)

- **One rename, three places (U-125).** A category is a folder under the wiki
  root, a `## <Category>` section in `index.md`, and the topic of every mark
  the next compile files under it. Renamed by hand in Obsidian, only the folder
  moved: the index kept the old heading and the next compile, reading a pending
  mark's old topic, opened the old folder again. The Wiki page's new
  **✏ Rename category** button (and `wiki.category.rename {from, to}` on the
  bridge) moves all three together — including the page paths a compiled mark
  keeps as provenance — appends a line to `log.md`, and answers with the lint.
  With exactly one topic in the filter, that one is offered first, and the
  filter follows the new name.
- **A name that exists is a merge.** Typed in any spelling, it merges into that
  spelling: every entry of the source folder moves in, the two index sections
  become one sorted list (a page linked from both is listed once), and the
  empty source goes. The box warns as you type and a modal asks before
  anything moves. **A page name present in both stops the merge before a single
  file leaves**, with the list; a move that fails half-way puts back what it
  moved. A case-only rename (`ai` → `AI`) really renames on Windows. The rules
  a new category name follows — no separators, no `_` prefix, no device name —
  are the same ones starting a category already followed.

## 3.647.0 - A headless OpenCode task can pick its model's own reasoning variant (X-330) (2026-09-23)

- **The variant is the model's, and only a headless run carries it (X-330).**
  OpenCode's reasoning level is `--variant`, and `opencode models --verbose`
  publishes it per model — some models none, some low · medium · high, some
  minimal … xhigh. The launcher already said "a headless task can pick one",
  but no task could: the Effort box was hidden for OpenCode and any level was
  refused at launch. Now the New-task form offers the chosen model exactly the
  variants it publishes (and no box at all for a model that publishes none), a
  headless run sends it as `--variant`, and a level the model does not publish
  is refused before anything spawns, with the model's own list. A terminal (the
  TUI has no `--variant`) and a Console card (ACP declares only model and mode)
  still take none, and a task set to run there is refused by name; a catalog
  that has not answered yet refuses nothing. The rule is one pure module,
  `core/opencodeVariant.ts`, asked by the form, the bridge, the task launcher
  and the mission preview alike.

## 3.646.0 - A notice that becomes a work item carries the whole notice, and goes back to the agent that raised it (N-10) (2026-09-23)

- **The item carries its notice (N-10).** Converting a notice — "Add to queue",
  or answering a question — deletes the notice by default, and the item kept
  only its title: who asked, what kind of message it was, its words, its
  sections and its report were gone. Now the item keeps all of it
  (`sourceNoticeAgent` · `Type` · `Body` · `Sections` · `ReportPath`, and the
  notice's project), copied once at the moment of conversion. Both doors — the
  Notices page and `queue.fromNotice` — build the item through one pure
  function (`core/noticeToQueue.ts`), so they cannot disagree about what
  travels.
- **Back to the agent that asked.** The item's target is the notice's agent
  when that is an agent that takes work; a notice raised by Agent Farm itself
  stays unrouted. `queue.list` gains `sourceNoticeAgent`, which is how an agent
  finds the answers to its own questions after they left Notices — every
  agent's answered-questions duty now watches both boards.
- **The queue card shows it.** The badge says what the notice was and who sent
  it (`❓ Question: <title> · from developer`), and **▸ Original** opens the
  notice as it read when it became this item — body, sections and a button for
  its report — even after the notice itself is gone. Items converted before
  this still draw their title, as before.

## 3.645.0 - A backlog line typed straight into the file is dated from the moment it appears (X-357) (2026-09-23)

- **Born in the file, dated in the file (X-357).** An item written or pasted
  straight into `Backlog.md` passed no door that records `opened`, so it had no
  date and both time orderings sank the newest thing in the file to the
  bottom (X-339…X-343 sat at 731–735). The outside reconciler now records a
  birth for a code that was not in the file the last time it was read —
  dated by the file's own last save when that is earlier than the moment it was
  noticed, and never on a first read, so old undated lines are not all "new
  today". `summarizeCode` keeps a noticed birth in the dates (a noticed closing
  is still kept out, X-135), and a pass that appended records refreshes an open
  Projects page.
- **The ones already undated can be dated from git.** `projects.tracks.backfill`
  (and the Track tab's ⚕) now has a second clue besides the transcripts: when
  the project folder is under git, an item with no `opened` of its own gets one
  at the first commit whose backlog diff adds its line — earlier than anything
  its ledger holds, or not at all — stamped `backfill` / `guess`, counted as
  `births`. One `git log` per run (measured: 1 s, 193 commits on the vault).

## 3.644.0 - A turn waiting on its own background command is no longer "your turn" (U-148), and the test suite stops calling a real model (X-361) (2026-09-23)

- **Waiting on background is its own state (U-148).** When a turn ends while a
  command it started is still running, the CLI wakes the session by itself once
  the command ends — nothing waits on you. The Console card said "your turn" in
  green and counted it in "N waiting for you"; the Live Timeline showed YOUR
  TURN. Now the card is purple with a slow, deep breath and reads "waiting on
  background", the strip says the same instead of "your turn now", the green
  nudge leaves it out, and Send becomes **Steer** — the box stays open, because
  a message then is a deliberate interruption, not an answer. The live monitor
  has a `waiting-task` status for it (decided in `core/liveWait.ts` from the
  Console's own background list, the way a parked question is), so the Live
  Timeline, the phone page, the Agents tree, Portfolio and Missions all show
  BACKGROUND in purple, the "your turn" alert and the idle reminder do not fire
  for it, and it becomes your turn again only when the list drains with no new
  turn behind it. A parked question still wins; terminal sessions are unchanged.
- **The suite no longer spends a model call (X-361).** `test_activation.js`
  turns every switch on, the weekly summary among them, and activation ran the
  real `claude` with the account slot's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` — every full run
  since 2026-09-20 left a real haiku conversation in the transcript pool (93 of
  them). The sandbox now puts stub engine CLIs first on PATH and removes the
  engines' configuration variables, and asserts both.

## 3.643.0 - A relay leg keeps its setup across a restart, and one that cannot pass is still carried on (S-89, S-90) (2026-09-23)

- **A revived card is the same run (S-89).** A `resume=true` restart brought each
  Console conversation back in a new card without its launch id, so a relay leg
  that loaded a new build on arrival could no longer pass the baton ("carries no
  launch id, so its setup is unknown"). The launch id now travels with the
  revive, and a relay leg whose launch record is missing anyway passes on its
  chain's own setup — the one it was opened on and the one the failsafe's rescue
  uses — and says so in `setupFromChain`.
- **A leg told to hand over is never left idle for ever (S-90).** A Console card
  does not end by itself, so a leg that got its QUOTA/CONTEXT HANDOVER order and
  came to rest WITHOUT passing sat there, and the failsafe — which judges an END
  — never ran. Agent Farm now closes such a card after 30 s at rest; the failsafe
  then opens the next leg from its handover note. A card the user spoke to after
  the order is left alone, and a terminal leg is never killed on this evidence.

## 3.642.0 - A Console task follows its conversation across a restart (S-88) (2026-09-23)

- **The row stays with the run.** A restart that takes the Console's
  conversations up again (`farm.restartExtensionHost resume=true`) reopens each
  one in a NEW card — but its task row went back to the queue, lost its card,
  and said the session "did not survive" while it was still working. Every
  relay leg that loads a new build on arrival hit this: its row sat parked
  beside the running leg, and ▶ on it would have opened a second one. Now the
  row is hooked onto the new card by the conversation's own id, goes back to
  running, keeps its start time, and its timeline says what happened. A row
  whose conversation was not taken up stays parked, as before.

## 3.641.0 - The baton relay no longer stalls on a Console leg (S-85, S-86, S-87) (2026-09-23)

The first real relay stopped after one hand-off. Three causes, all fixed:

- **The leg that passed is ended for it (S-86).** A Console card — and a
  terminal session — does not end when its turn does; it waits for the next
  message. The successor waits for the predecessor to END, so the chain sat
  still for as long as nobody closed the card. Now, once the turn that passed
  the baton has been at rest for ten seconds (nothing queued, no question
  open), Agent Farm ends that session itself: the card is closed with the
  reason written on it, or the terminal's process is stopped, together with
  any background command it left running. The successor opens right after.
  The passing turn itself is never cut.
- **A Console successor stays in its chain (S-85).** Its baton recorded the
  Console card's id instead of the conversation's, so nothing could find it:
  its own pass opened a NEW chain at hop 1 (the leg ceiling started over), its
  card showed no relay badge, ⑂ Attach on it sealed a second chain, and its
  handover whisper said "write a note" instead of "pass the baton". The baton
  now holds the engine's session id, and batons written the old way are
  repaired on the next sweep while their task row is still around.
- **The successor's header counts legs (S-87).** It said `hop 1/6` on the
  second leg — the same "1" the first leg's card showed. It now reads
  `leg 2/6`, the number the card and the status bar use; handover templates
  get a `{leg}` variable.

## 3.640.0 - The Dashboard and Farm Settings say which build is running (U-147) (2026-09-23)

- **`v3.640.0`, top right.** The Dashboard and Farm Settings headers carry the
  running Agent Farm version on the title's own line, flush right, small and
  quiet — no trip to the Extensions view to find out which build you are on.
- **The running one, not the installed one.** The number is read from the
  extension's own manifest when it activates and handed to the page, so after
  installing a new VSIX the stamp keeps showing the OLD version until the
  window is reloaded — which is exactly the question it answers. Every other
  page is unchanged.

## 3.639.0 - A hover panel is never seen through a dimmed row (U-146) (2026-09-23)

- **Opaque, everywhere.** A panel opened inside a faded block — a closed A2A
  card, a done task, a muted account line, a dimmed table header, a quiet
  session row — was drawn at that block's opacity: half-transparent, with the
  text behind it showing through and the next row painting over it. Measured
  on the page renders: about 640 panels on 14 pages sat under such a block.
  Now the faded block is lifted to full opacity for exactly as long as its
  panel is open — the row you are reading comes forward with it — and fades
  back when the panel closes. A pointer merely passing over a list flashes
  nothing: the lift waits the same short delay the panel does.
- The code that decides where a panel opens (K-18's side, K-44's fit, and this
  lift) now lives in its own file, `media/afTipEdge.js`, so the panel component
  itself stops growing.

## 3.638.0 - A hover panel never opens off the window, or under the column beside it (K-44) (2026-09-23)

- **A third answer when neither side fits.** A panel used to choose between
  its trigger's left edge and its right edge; when it was wider than the room
  on both sides, both choices ran off the page — measured on the Console: a
  760px panel off `📥 Queue` started 21px past the left edge at 1400px, and at
  744px four kinds of panel ran 26–42px off the right. Now, after picking a
  side, the panel is measured against the box that really clips it — the
  window, narrowed by any scrolling area it sits in — and slid inside it,
  narrowed only when even that box is too small. Every page gets this; the
  Console is where it showed.
- **The Console reads at a reading width.** Its ordinary panels are capped at
  520px (about 75 characters) instead of the full-page 760px: a
  one-paragraph explanation is no longer drawn as a single line that neither
  side of its button had room for. Panels placed against a row (`tip-block`)
  and the session list's floating panels keep their own widths.

## 3.637.0 - The web view gets a cockpit: can my phone read this farm right now? (U-85) (2026-09-23)

- **A card that answers the one question.** Toolbox → Services has a Mobile
  Web Dashboard card: start/stop, the port badge, a local ↔ LAN select, the
  whole link with a copy button, and a new token. Turning LAN on and minting a
  new token (which revokes every bookmark) are both asked about every time.
- ‼️ **`local` is amber, not green.** Enabled, token set, server bound — and
  the only link is `http://127.0.0.1:…`, which the phone on the desk cannot
  open. The card says so instead of painting its three booleans green.
- ‼️ **A QR code only where a phone can use it.** Drawn by our own encoder (a
  link carrying a token is not handed to a website to draw), and only when the
  link is reachable from the network; otherwise the card says why there is none.
  With the view off the address is struck through and there is no copy button —
  a URL that refuses every request is not something to put on a clipboard.
- **A door on the Dashboard.** `📱 Web` in the top bar runs the same command as
  the palette: it asks local or LAN if the view is off, then opens it.
- **The phone page stops polling when nobody is looking.** A phone left open on
  it no longer wakes its radio every 15 s behind a locked screen; showing it
  again fetches at once. It also pads for the notch and the home bar
  (`safe-area-inset-*`), which `viewport-fit=cover` had promised and never done.
- New bridge ops: `web.status` (the card's own verdict, the code on request) ·
  `web.stop` · `web.bind` · `web.token.new`. The link has ONE formula
  (`webUrl()`), used by the card, the command, the QR, the server and the ops.

## 3.636.0 - A relay leaves its handover on the A2A board, and the board keeps itself clean (S-84) (2026-09-22)

- **The words go where you already look.** Every baton pass now hangs a card
  on the A2A Notes board — the successor's own first message as the body, the
  chain id as its topic, `⑂` as its category. `baton.status` names the card
  (`a2aNoteId`). The failsafe's rescue hop (S-83) gets one too: it is a
  handover as well, just written by a session that has already gone.
- **A card's life is its chain's.** It is marked resolved the moment the
  successor is running — the words have reached the run they were written for
  — and when the chain ends (`done`, `failed`, or a baton you stop) every card
  of that race is given 24 hours before the board sweeps it.
- **The board sweeps itself.** A note resolved more than 48 hours ago goes,
  an expired relay card goes whether or not anybody resolved it, and
  **a pinned note (📌) is never swept by any rule** — only deleting it by hand
  takes it off. `a2a.notes.sweep` says exactly that.
- **One switch for the races.** `⑂ Batons: all → hidden → only` on the filter
  row: a busy relay writes a card per leg, and this is how it stops burying
  the fleet's ordinary notes.
- **One race, read as a story.** On a relay card the topic chip IS the chain
  (`⑂ chn_…`). Click it and the page locks to that race: every leg, **oldest
  first**, with the other filters off — a chain with its resolved legs hidden
  is not the story. A bar says what is locked, how many legs handed on, and
  unlocks.
- **A hand that deletes.** ✕ Delete on a card; a checkbox per row with `all`
  and 🗑 Delete taking the selected rows — or every row shown when nothing is
  checked, never the whole board behind the filter; ● Clear resolved for the
  closed half only. Pinned notes are spared by everything automatic.
- New bridge ops: `a2a.notes.pin` · `a2a.notes.delete` ·
  `a2a.notes.deleteMany` · `a2a.notes.clear`.
- ‼️ A relay card is **addressed, not broadcast** (`hard`, to the agent that
  passed it), so a race never lands on another agent's `a2a.status`; the page
  draws the whole board, so a person still sees every chain.

## 3.635.0 - The relay's failsafe: a leg that ends without passing is judged, not lost (S-83) (2026-09-22)

- **A cut-off leg is rescued.** A run in a baton relay that ends WITHOUT
  passing is now looked at. If it was cut off — a QUOTA/CONTEXT HANDOVER had
  reached it, it wrote a handover note in its last two minutes, it exited with
  an error, or it left uncommitted work — Agent Farm opens the next leg itself,
  through the same door and the same brakes as `baton.pass`. The new run wakes
  up under an `EMERGENCY HANDOVER` header: why it was rescued, the note's
  Durum / Kalan / İlk 5 dakika sections (or the folder's `git status`), the
  predecessor's full session id and the command that reads its LAST turns.
- **A finished leg is not.** A leg that ended cleanly — the chain's natural
  end — or one you ended yourself closes the chain as `done` (a routine line
  on Notices); nothing is opened.
- **Crash-loop guard.** A successor that dies within 30 seconds without a
  tool call stops the chain as `failed` and says so on Notices, instead of
  opening another that would die the same way.
- **Your own emergency header.** `agentFarm.batonEmergencyTemplate`
  (Settings ▸ Handover Discipline ▸ When a leg ends without passing), with
  `{fromSessionId}` `{agentId}` `{chain}` `{hop}` `{maxHops}` `{why}`
  `{evidence}` `{userDirective}`; the evidence is never dropped.
- `baton.status` shows a chain's end (`done` / `failed`) and marks a rescued
  hop with `rescue`; the card's relay panel says how the chain ended.

## 3.634.0 - The Console status row's icons are legible, and every hover panel on it opens on a title (2026-09-22)

- **Frameless icon chips.** The relay and handover hands on a card's status row
  (↪ Continue from handover, ✕⑂ Stop chain, ⑂→ Pass now, ⑂+ Attach relay) were
  10px glyphs inside a bordered box — the frame took the room and the ⑂ could
  not be read. They are now frameless chips with a 15px glyph (a hover tint
  shows they can be pressed), and 📎 Attach files joins them. `⑂ n` on the
  strip is larger too.
- **A title before the paragraph.** Every hover panel on the strip now reads:
  the small state line, then a bold title saying what the thing is (Pass now,
  Stop chain, Context window, 5-hour quota signal, Bridge guard…), then the
  explanation — you know the subject before you read a word of it. 📎's panel
  follows the attached count as it changes.

## 3.633.0 - The Console status row's hover panels are solid (U-81) (2026-09-22)

- **No more reading the page through a panel.** The status row under the
  composer was dimmed with `opacity`, and every hover panel on it is drawn
  inside that row — so each panel came out 60% see-through. The row is now
  dimmed with a colour (`tip-host`, the rule the Live Timeline cards already
  follow), its buttons dim themselves, and the panels are opaque.

## 3.632.0 - The Console status row is one quiet line again (2026-09-22)

- **Signals are dots, hands are chips.** 3.631.0 put full-size buttons and
  words on a card's status row — "Continue from handover", "⑂ Attach relay",
  "CONVERGE ✓", "guard 1" — and squeezed its figures into three lines. The
  context, quota and bridge-guard signals are now a 6px dot in their colour,
  with the words one hover away; Continue from handover (↪), Stop chain (✕⑂),
  Pass now (⑂→) and Attach relay (⑂+) are small chips, each named first in its
  hover.

## 3.631.0 - A baton relay you start yourself: from the New-task form, the Console composer and a running card, with your own header on every leg (S-81, S-82) (2026-09-22)

- **The run that opens a relay is leg 1 from its first turn (S-81).** A task
  started with `baton:true` is sealed as leg 1 the moment its session is
  known, so at its quota or context line it is told to pass the baton rather
  than to write a note. The chain keeps the pool its first leg named on every
  later leg — a rule (`@…`) is the pool, a single slot or nothing means
  `@emptiest` — and a pass that asks for another account is answered with
  `poolKept`.
- **Start a relay from the New-task form (S-82).** A `⑂ Relay` row beside
  Budget: the tick, and while it is on a pool picker (the Account box
  narrowed to rules) and a max-legs box whose empty value is the fleet
  setting. The relay travels with the run's other dimensions, so schedules,
  triggers, templates and every retry carry it.
- **…from the Console composer.** `⑂ Relay` beside Superpowers, before Send:
  the pool is the rule in the Account box, and a max-legs box appears while
  it is on. `console.start baton=true maxHops=N` is the same door for an
  agent.
- **…or on a session that is already running.** A live card outside any relay
  offers `⑂ Attach relay`: a strip under the status row picks the pool and the
  ceiling, and the run becomes leg 1 at once, without a restart — the same
  body as the new `baton.attach` op. A card that is in a relay offers
  `⑂ Pass now` beside `✕ Stop chain`: the handover order its context line
  would have sent is said into the run now.
- **A chain can carry its own leg ceiling.** Set from any of the three doors
  (0 = none); empty means `agentFarm.batonMaxHops`. The successor's header
  now says `hop n/N`.
- **Your own header on every leg.** `agentFarm.batonHandoverTemplate` replaces
  the built-in "=== BATON RELAY ===" header — `{fromSessionId}`, `{agentId}`,
  `{chain}`, `{hop}`, `{maxHops}`, `{why}`, `{userDirective}`,
  `{agentPrompt}` — and `agentFarm.batonInjectedDirective` is a standing rule
  said to every leg. The predecessor's words are never dropped, even by a
  template that forgets them. Both are text boxes on Settings ▸ Handover
  Discipline.
- **The Console cards were missing three things they had been designed to
  show.** "Continue from handover", the `⑂ n` relay chip, `✕ Stop chain` and
  the bridge-guard chip are drawn from views the Console page had never been
  sent — only the `console.sessions` op built them. The page now gets the
  same views from the same builder, and repaints when a baton changes.

## 3.630.0 - The lean project brief, a backlog icon that takes only its own value, and Tasks toolbars that break as two blocks (X-352, U-145) (2026-09-22)

- **The project brief is lean.** A session started inside a project is no
  longer handed the people list, the open plan, the next backlog items, the
  recent worklog or the recent decisions — they change mid-session and have
  ops of their own. It carries the status, the code roots, which file holds
  which role, and the charter's four constitution sections (Scope &
  Anti-Scope, Code Architecture, Verification Gate, Project Invariants)
  inlined. The charter is read once per brief instead of seven times inside
  the budget loop, and headings match by word stem: `## Research` is no
  longer taken for architecture, `## Latest` no longer for verification, and
  a second "Kapsam dışı" heading adds to the first instead of replacing it.
- **A backlog metadata icon takes only its own value (X-352).** Each valued
  icon is stripped only together with a value of its own form — the date
  icons with YYYY-MM-DD, 🆔 with an id, ⛔ with a code list, 🏁 with
  delete|keep. An icon without such a value stays in the text
  (`⏳ Yanıt bekleniyor` keeps its words), and a bare ⛔ is a flag on its own
  instead of eating the next word.
- **The Tasks toolbars break between two blocks (U-145).** The Runs and Plan
  toolbars are a filters block and an actions block: on a slight narrowing
  the filters give ground and the row stays one line; narrower, the actions
  move down together, never a button at a time; under 620px each block wraps
  inside itself.

## 3.629.0 - The parity gate reaches zero: every door and its op meet at one function (B-16, B-26) (2026-09-22)

- **Zero open parity gaps.** The last eighteen user doors that either had
  no op or had an op doing the same act by a second road now meet their op
  at one shared function, and the gate’s budget is 0 — a new gap can no
  longer be added, only a new op or a reasoned exemption.
- **New ops.** `airtable.folders.add` / `.remove` — one folder at a time,
  the way the page’s + Add and remove do it, instead of overwriting the whole
  list; a folder already listed (either case, either slash) is not doubled,
  and an engine folder with no instance needs `anyway:true`, the question the
  page asks you. `terminal.render.get` / `.apply` — the “Fix Terminal
  Rendering” repair (`fix` · `external` · `persist` · `restore`), the only
  op allowed to write `terminal.integrated`, and only its three keys.
  `examples.setup` — the three working examples (inbox trigger, morning
  briefing, two-agent chain); the chain is created, not run, unless
  `run:true`. `studio.export` gains `format:"both"`: the XML with the EDL
  beside it, which is what the Studio’s export card writes.
- **One function where there were copies.** Settling a mission round’s
  approval was written out five times (the op, the page, the tree’s Approve
  and Reject, cancelling the run) — now `settleMissionApproval`. The
  Studio’s export card and `studio.export` both write through
  `core/sequenceExport`; the palette’s terminal repair and its op through
  `core/terminalRender`; the example walk-through and its op build from
  `core/examples`; the doc-open default refreshes its three readers through
  one `docOpenChanged`, from the palette and from `docopen.set` alike. Also
  (earlier in B-16): `removeToolboxItem`, `setServerDisabled`,
  `answerMissionQuestion` with `skip`.
- **The gate sees further, so it stops reporting parity that is there.** A
  fall-through `case` arm carries the code it falls into; a command run from
  inside a deps value is followed; an op reaching a deps object by its own
  name (`portfolioDeps.importPack`) is expanded; and a command that hands off
  to a host function is read through to it. Three gap notes had named the
  wrong op (filing sessions is `projects.suggest.apply`, removing a project
  is `projects.set delete:true`, the Studio’s re-run is `studio.rerun`).

## 3.628.0 - B-21 closed: the Tasks page’s ⬇ MD is back, and a session exports from an op (2026-09-21)

- **The Tasks page’s Runs toolbar carries ⬇ MD again.** The handler had
  outlived its button since the page was rewritten (v6.31); asked on
  Notices, the answer was to put the door back. It exports the rows you can
  see — this search, these filters, this order, the archive month you are
  reading — as a Markdown table whose cells are the text the screen shows
  (a status with its hold reason, `you` for a run you pressed, the engine’s
  own name, a full clock instead of “2h ago”). The page sends title,
  columns and rows; the host builds with `core/mdTable`, the same function
  `tasks.export` uses.
- **`sessions.export` — one conversation as a document.** The session page’s
  own Export MD, built where an op can build it: header (session, folder,
  span, totals with the ⚖ figure and its mark), then every step under its
  `## Turn n` heading — speaker named by your `speakerLabel` settings, the
  shared step kind, clock, model, tokens, cost — with tool calls and results
  fenced. Everything by default; name `roles`, `filter`, `excludeTurns` or
  `foldedTurns` and only that view is written, with an `Export:` line
  stating exactly what was applied. `file` writes atomically, `save` lands
  it in the report folder.
- **The builder left the webview (`core/sessionExport`).** The document used
  to be assembled inside the page out of its view state — visible steps,
  folded and unticked turns, the replay position — and the host only filed
  it. The page now sends that view with the click; the host asks its two
  questions and builds from the same parse the page was drawn from, so the
  button and the op cannot describe one conversation two ways. The reader’s
  speaker settings come from one place (`speakerSettings()`), read by the
  page shell and by the builder alike.
- **Parity: 21 → 18 open gaps.** `tasksPanel#export-md → tasks.export`,
  `sessionViewer#exportChoose → sessions.export`; the `exportMd` message no
  longer exists, so its gap is gone with it.

## 3.627.0 - Five pages’ Export MD stops being a button and becomes an op (B-21) (2026-09-21)

- **The board, the turns table, the analytics page and the runs board can
  now be exported without a person in front of them.** `notices.export`,
  `turns.export`, `tasks.analytics.export` and `tasks.export` each hand back
  the document the page writes — content by default, an atomic write when
  you pass `file`, the report folder on `save:true`, and the path always
  named in the answer. Each selects exactly like its page’s list op through
  one shared selector, so rows and document can never drift apart.
- **The builders moved out of the webview.** A page that assembled its own
  Markdown was reachable from a button and from nowhere else; that is the
  whole of B-21’s complaint. The Task Analytics page now posts its title,
  its columns and the rows it is showing, and the host builds with
  `core/mdTable` — the same function the op uses. Pipes and newlines are
  escaped, a short row is padded rather than ragged, and `0` and `false`
  print as values instead of blanking into what reads as missing data.
- **A cap is named, never silent.** Turn content is heavy, so `turns.export`
  defaults to 50 turns — and always answers with `matched` and `truncated`,
  because a caller handed 50 of 900 with no word about it has been given a
  file that simply stops.
- **‼️ The Tasks page’s own ⬇ MD has had no door since the page was
  rewritten.** The handler is still there and still works; nothing reaches
  it. `tasks.export` covers the bridge side; whether the control comes back
  or the dead handler goes is asked on Notices rather than decided here.

## 3.626.0 - The relay proven live, and its hand-off stops posting "Task parked" on every leg (S-79 · X-355) (2026-09-21)

- **The baton relay, run for real (S-79).** A three-leg haiku chain over two
  accounts: the pass answered with the right sentence; each successor opened
  only after its predecessor's run had ended (20:27:24 ended → 20:27:25
  started, and the same on the next leg); the successor's first message
  opened with `=== BATON RELAY — chain … · hop 1 ===`; and the relay's
  converge whisper reached leg 2 — `CONTEXT CONVERGE 39% … then pass the
  baton (baton relay — chain …, hop 2)` — which passed on it. With every
  account made full by a test-only policy, the pass said beforehand that
  the successor would park, the baton parked until the first reset plus the
  safety buffer, Notices said so once, and `baton.now` woke it.
- **‼️ The hand-off was posting a "Task parked" line on every leg (X-355).**
  Found by that run: a successor row is added the moment its predecessor's
  session ends, a beat before that run's own row closes, so it meets the
  per-agent lock for a second or two — and the farm-news scan announced it,
  "Task parked — Baton — hop N of chain …", once per leg. That is the door
  working, not news; the relay speaks for its rows (a park, a brake). A
  successor row held by anything else still speaks.

## 3.625.0 - The baton relay gets its surfaces and its brakes: ✕ Stop chain on the card, one ⑂ item on the status bar, a ⑂ column in every sessions table (S-77) — and a leg ceiling and a barren-chain brake decided at the pass (S-78) (2026-09-21)

- **✕ Stop chain, beside Continue from handover — never instead of it.** A
  relay leg whose chain still has a baton waiting or parked carries the
  brake on its Console card. It runs the one body `baton.stop chain=` runs
  (`stopBatons`), so the button and the op cannot drift: every live baton of
  the chain is kept as `stopped`, nothing is deleted, and a run a baton
  already opened keeps running. Its panel opens with the relay's state and
  ends with the agent's spelling of the same brake.
- **One status-bar item for the relay running now** — `⑂ 3/6`, `· 14:37`
  when that leg is parked, `+N` when more chains run, hidden while none
  does. The tooltip has a line per chain, the ceiling and the brake; a click
  opens the Console on the running leg.
- **A ⑂ column in every sessions table** (Dashboard, Sessions, agent and
  project pages), right after the origin strip: `⑂ n` on a relay leg with
  the chain in its panel — the Console card's own words — and a blank cell
  on every other row.
- **Two brakes, decided at the pass.** `agentFarm.batonMaxHops` (default 6
  legs, the run that started the chain being leg 1; 0 = none) is the
  ceiling. And every pass now records the folder's git HEAD: two legs in a
  row that end on the HEAD they were opened on stop the chain — a third run
  would only spend another window the same way. A braked pass is answered,
  not refused: the baton is kept as stopped with the reason, the answer says
  `braked`, the runner is told to write a handover note instead, and Notices
  says it once. The setting has its own group under Settings ▸ Handover
  Discipline. Notices speaks about a relay exactly twice: a park and a brake.

## 3.624.0 - The handover whisper becomes a setting — the two lines AND the words they deliver (S-80) — and it stops reading the week and calling it the five-hour window (X-353) (2026-09-21)

- **‼️ The quota line was reading the wrong window (X-353).** Measured on this
  machine, on the session that was doing the work: `five_hour 34% ·
  seven_day 90%`, and the live hook answered `QUOTA HANDOVER 90% — your
  account's 5-hour window is 90% used` and ordered the run to end. The guard
  was handed `SlotUsage.percent`, which is the **binding** bar — whichever of
  the five-hour window and the week is fuller (X-309). That is right where it
  was built, choosing an account to start a session on, and wrong here twice:
  the handover law names the 5-hour window as its trigger and says in the same
  breath that the weekly figure is never one, and the sentence the guard
  delivers *names* the five-hour window. `fiveHourOf` now reads that row and
  nothing else, and the chip's reset clock is that window's reset. An engine
  whose only window is the week (Codex) gets no quota line at all — which is
  what the law asks for.
- **The order the whisper delivers is yours to write (S-80).** The thresholds
  were already settings; the sentence they deliver was not, and a percentage
  nobody can retune is half a rule. `agentFarm.disciplineOrders` holds six
  branches — converge · handover, and the relay pair plus the
  already-passed pair, because a run carrying a baton is told to pass it
  rather than to write a note. It ships **empty**: a blank branch keeps its
  built-in sentence, so nothing changes until you change it. `{chain}` is
  replaced by the relay's own chain and hop.
- **‼️ The lead words are NOT settable.** `CONTEXT HANDOVER`, `QUOTA CONVERGE`
  and the reading in front of them are what the handover law waits for — they
  are the protocol; what you edit is the instruction that follows them.
- **Settings ▸ Handover Discipline** is a section of its own, in two groups:
  *When a run is spoken to* (the four percentages, moved out of Live
  Monitoring, where they read as a monitor's sensitivity rather than as the
  law a run is held to) and *What it is told* (the six boxes).
  `agentFarm.contextWindowTokens` stays where it was on purpose — it is the
  ceiling every context figure is drawn against, not a line anybody is held
  to.
- Two page fixes the section exposed, both derived from the schema rather than
  from a list of keys, so they reach the next long-text setting for free: a
  form field whose own declared default is a *sentence* gets a textarea
  instead of a 170px box, and the flex basis that lines a form up moved onto
  the AFTip wrapper — it had been set on the span one level down, so a long
  field name pushed its own box to the right and a form's boxes never lined
  up.
- **Bridge:** `sessions.contextGuard` answers `orders` and a `sample` of the
  sentence as it actually arrives; `sessions.contextGuard.set orders=` writes
  them, refuses an unknown branch by name, and treats `""` as *remove this
  override* rather than as a blank order.
- **‼️ The allowance block on an account card stops being prose (U-144).**
  Reported as "the numbers that should catch my eye never do — I have to pick
  them out of a line of prose every time", and it was two faults in one block.
  The percentage was 11px of the card's ordinary grey beside a track that was
  already red, so the loudest thing on a card at 91% was a 7px bar; it is
  bigger and bolder now and wears the **same three steps its track has**
  (plain · warn at 75 · hot at 90), from one expression, so the number and the
  bar can never disagree. And both windows' reset times were ONE sentence under
  both bars — `5h: 37m left (02:17) · wk: 4d left (14 Ağu 2026, 01:40)` — so
  reading how long the five-hour window had left meant reading past the weekly
  window's date; each window's clock is on that window's own row now, the span
  at full strength and the time of day quietly behind it, and the line
  underneath is gone rather than restyled. **A window that has already turned
  over strikes its own figure through** — that percentage belongs to the window
  before this one, and the clause that used to say so sat at the tail of a
  sentence nobody read to the end. The Engines page draws this same section, so
  it is fixed in both places at once.

## 3.623.0 - The relay leg on the Console card: ⑂ n, the chain in its own panel (S-77, part 1) (2026-09-21)

- **A card that is a leg of a baton relay says so.** `⑂ 2` sits beside the
  context figure; its panel names the chain and how many legs it has had,
  the predecessor that passed the baton to this run, and what the successor
  is doing right now — waiting for this session to end, parked until a
  named time because every account is full, running as a named session, or
  stopped / refused with the reason — plus the brake to use while anything
  in the chain is live. The words are derived once in core
  (`batonCardView`) and ride on `console.sessions` as `batonView`.
- Still to come in S-77: the ✕ stop-chain button beside Continue, the
  status-bar item, the sessions-table chain column and the two Notices
  events.

## 3.622.0 - The whisper gets a quota line — a run is told when its own account's 5-hour window reaches 90% — and a relay runner is told to pass the baton (S-75 · S-76) (2026-09-21)

- **‼️ The discipline signal is two-dimensional now (S-75).** The handover
  law has two triggers — the context window and the 5-hour quota — and until
  now Agent Farm only whispered the first. The guard reads the session's
  **own** account window (its Console card's slot, else the slot its sealed
  launch manifest names) and, on the same PostToolUse / UserPromptSubmit
  hook, tells the run `QUOTA HANDOVER 90%` (stop and hand over) — once,
  re-armed when the window resets, recorded as undelivered on an engine with
  no channel. **There is no quota converge line by default:** the handover
  law has none — below 90% a run works at full capacity — so
  `QUOTA CONVERGE` is said only if you set a figure for it.
  **A session whose slot is not known is never told a figure** — a number
  from the home folder's sign-in is worse than none (measured: home 95%,
  the session's own window 23%). Both lines crossing in one hook are one
  answer: the window's sentence first, the quota's under it.
- **Settings:** `agentFarm.quotaConvergePct` (0 = off) and
  `agentFarm.quotaHandoverPct` (90); 0 switches a line off.
  `sessions.contextGuard.set` takes all four thresholds.
- **Surfaces.** The Console card draws a `5h 91% HANDOVER` chip beside the
  context figure with its **own** panel — the account, the reading, the reset
  clock, what was delivered when, and the law — never mixed into the context
  panel; `✕` when the sentence could not reach the run. The session's own
  page draws the same line under the context gauge. A card told QUOTA
  HANDOVER offers **Continue from handover** exactly as a context handover
  does, and counts as handover evidence everywhere a run would otherwise be
  resumed.
- **Bridge:** `sessions.contextGuard id=` also answers `quotaReading`
  {pct, account, resetsAt, level} read now from the session's own sign-in,
  and `view.quota` — the words the card and the page are showing.
- **‼️ In a baton relay the order is "pass the baton" (S-76).** A session a
  baton opened — or one that has passed a baton still live — is told, at the
  handover line of either dimension, to pass the baton instead of writing a
  handover note: the chain and hop, and the recipe (`Write` the prompt to a
  file, `node af.js baton.pass "@<file>"`, end the run). One that already
  passed is only told to end. Outside a relay the sentences are exactly what
  they were; a chain the user braked after the runner opened falls back to
  the note; a baton store that cannot be read is no relay, never a broken
  hook. `_REF/handover.md` gains the relay step; the vault has the human-side
  definition beside the handover system.

## 3.621.0 - The baton is released when its session ends, and the successor opens through the task board; the user has a brake and a go (S-70 · S-71 · S-74) (2026-09-21)

- **‼️ The relay now runs on its own (S-66).** A baton left with `baton.pass`
  is released the moment its session ENDS — the hook's `SessionEnd`, the
  Console host's exit and a terminal's close all arrive on one channel — and
  a 60-second sweep is the backup for a run that died with no hook. The
  verdict is evidence, never silence: a session with a **registered CLI
  process** is alive whatever else is known (two agents in one repo, never
  — an agent that passed the baton and kept working keeps its repo); the
  watcher's own end is an end; a claude session with no registry record is
  gone; an engine without a registry is believed dead only once the watcher
  has forgotten it. Evidence that cannot be read is a wait that says so.
- **The successor opens through `tasks.add` — the one door every run uses**
  — so the park, the budget brake, the concurrency lock and the automation
  gate are all already on it, and the row is visible on the board
  (`Baton — hop n of chain …`). Surface by surface: headless → headless;
  console → an interactive row hosted by the Console that stays open;
  terminal → the VS Code terminal; external-terminal → an external window;
  `inherit` = whatever the predecessor used. The sealed setup rides on the
  row, the account is the want (`@emptiest` by default), the project travels
  from the manifest and is stated even when absent, a run outside the
  agent's folder says so. Always a fresh session, never a resume.
- **The header is the system's.** The successor's first message names the
  chain, the hop and the predecessor (session · agent · engine/model ·
  project), says the words below are its own, and teaches it to pass the
  baton itself by the file recipe when its own run is ending — then the
  predecessor's prompt, untouched. The chain carries itself.
- **What the door did is the baton's state:** a session opened → `started`
  (task + successor); a row the pump holds → `parked` on that row with the
  hold in `why`, then `started` when the row names its session; a row that
  ended without a session, or a door that refused (no such agent, an engine
  not installed) → `refused`, told once on Notices, nothing started.
- **`baton.stop`** — by baton, chain or session; each record stays as
  `stopped` with your reason, nothing is deleted. **`baton.now`** — a
  waiting baton goes through the door at once; a baton parked on a queued
  row asks the pump again (what a hand that just freed an account wants).

- **The quota brake reads the row's own account (S-72).** The pump's
  `quota:5h` hold read one figure — the machine-wide transcript window —
  whichever account the row would run on, so a row bound for a slot at 10%
  was held because the home account stood at 95%. Now a row that states an
  account (a slot or a rule) is judged by the 5-hour figure of the slot it
  resolves to, from that plan's own published usage, and the hold names the
  slot; a row that states none keeps the machine figure it always had.
- **Every account full at the release → the successor waits until the first
  reset (S-73).** The row is written with the first reset plus the safety
  buffer as its start moment, so it waits visibly on the board and the pump
  starts it then — no second timer; the baton is `parked` with its wake time
  and the person is told once on Notices (the moment, `baton.now` to go
  sooner once room is made, `baton.stop` to drop it). Quiet hours and the
  main switch defer the row, never drop it.
- **A session with a live Console card is alive** for the release, whatever
  the registry says at that second — the host owns that process (or is
  reclaiming it after a reload) and says SessionEnd itself when it goes.

## 3.620.0 - `baton.pass` / `baton.status`: a run can leave its successor's first words, and nothing starts until it has ended (S-69) (2026-09-21)

- **‼️ The door of the baton relay (S-66) is open — and it opens nothing yet.**
  `baton.pass` records the words a run leaves for the session that will
  continue its work, against the calling session (found the way
  `sessions.whoami` finds it, never from the folder), with the successor's
  whole setup read off that session's **sealed launch manifest** (engine,
  model, effort, permission, provider, superpowers, folder, project). It
  answers with one sentence saying what will happen when the session ENDS
  — which account rule, which slot it would land on now (a preview: the
  round-robin cursor does not move), or that every account is full and it
  would park until the first reset. A second pass replaces the first; both
  stay on record. Opening the successor is the next step (S-70/S-71).
- **Refusals are data** naming the step: no caller evidence, no launch id or
  manifest for the session (its setup would be a guess), an empty prompt, an
  unknown surface.
- **`baton.status`** lists the live batons and their chains hop by hop:
  who passed, who was started, what each waits for, the sentence of its last
  change. Filter by `chain` or `session`.
- The prompt is prose, so the op's own description teaches the file recipe
  (`node af.js baton.pass "@baton.json"`) rather than an inline string.

## 3.619.0 - `sessions.whoami`: a caller can ask which session it is, and the answer is evidence, never the folder (S-68) (2026-09-21)

- **‼️ "Which session am I?" had no answer anywhere.** An agent calling the
  bridge runs several processes below the CLI that holds its conversation
  (claude → shell → node af.js), and the only way to name that conversation
  was the engine's own environment variable — which not every engine sets.
  `sessions.whoami` answers in a fixed order: the `session` you pass; the
  variable af.js forwards; otherwise **af.js's parent pid, walked up the
  process tree until a pid the CLI itself registered**
  (`<config-dir>/sessions/<pid>.json`) — the nearest one is the conversation.
  With none of those it refuses, and says it will not guess from the folder:
  two sessions in one folder is the ordinary case. The answer carries the
  Console card holding the session (agent, engine, account, `launchId`,
  project); `verify:true` walks the tree even when the variable answered and
  says whether the two agree. This is how the baton (S-66) will find its owner.
- **af.js now puts its parent pid on every request**, beside the session it
  already forwarded; the envelope keeps it (a positive integer, or nothing) and
  it never mixes with an op's own args. A caller with no session still arrives
  with no session — only its pid.
- **The process tree is read without blocking the extension host**
  (`readProcessTableAsync`): the host is one thread, and the synchronous read
  froze every panel for the second and a half it takes. The direct parent is
  tried against the registry first, so a caller that IS the CLI costs no tree.

## 3.618.1 - the bridge can read what a Console question asked and what it was answered (K-43) (2026-09-21)

- **`console.sessions` no longer shows a question row as empty.** A row that
  asked or answered keeps its words in the question or the answer, not in
  `text`, and the projection read `text` alone — so an agent reading a card
  saw `role: ask, text: null` for both. Measured on the K-43 live run: the
  auto-answer fired on time, the agent was told, and the one row that says
  `⏱️ Zaman aşımı: önerilen seçenekler seçildi — …` came back as null. The row
  now carries its answer, or the question it asked.
- **K-43 seen live on 3.618.0.** A haiku Console card asked one question with
  `Mavi (Recommended)`; with the wait at 15 s the card reported `armed` with
  that pick, the answer went out 3 ms after `dueAt`, and the agent replied that
  Agent Farm had chosen the recommended option for the user.

## 3.618.0 - a question nobody answers no longer holds the turn for ever: the recommended option is chosen on a timer (K-43) (2026-09-21)

- **‼️ A Console session parked on `AskUserQuestion` is answered for you when
  nobody is there.** An unattended card — a night shift, a queued run, a fleet
  working while you sleep — used to sit on a question indefinitely: alive,
  spending nothing, doing nothing, and reporting none of it. Now the wait is
  bounded (`agentFarm.console.autoAnswer.timeoutSeconds`, default **300**,
  clamped to 5–7200) and at the end of it the option the agent itself marked
  **(Recommended)** / **(Önerilen)** is chosen — or its first option, which the
  tool's own contract makes the same thing. Off with
  `agentFarm.console.autoAnswer.enabled`.
- **The clock lives in the host, not the page.** The unattended case is exactly
  the one with no panel open, so a countdown drawn in the webview would stop
  the moment nobody was looking. It is measured from when the question was
  **asked**: reopening the window does not buy the question another wait, and
  changing the setting re-arms the questions already waiting.
- **Three things it will not do, each on purpose.** A **permission** request is
  never answered on a timer (that would hand an unattended machine to whatever
  asked). A question whose text, headers, labels or descriptions read as
  destructive — delete, force push, `reset --hard`, drop table, sil, kaldır… —
  is left for a person, and the card **says which word** stopped the clock. A
  question with no options gets no invented answer.
- **The card counts down, and a person in the room wins.** Under the question:
  `⏳ 4:31 left — then "…" is chosen for you` with a **Stop timer** button;
  picking an option or typing an answer stops it too, so a half-made choice is
  never overwritten. A stop belongs to one question — the next one gets its own
  clock. Folded, the card keeps the countdown on its header line.
- **‼️ The agent is told the user did not choose.** The answer goes out on the
  same wire as a click, with the picks folded into the response the CLI always
  delivers (X-166) and one sentence saying Agent Farm chose them. The
  transcript row reads `⏱️ Zaman aşımı: önerilen seçenekler seçildi — <question> → <pick>`.
- **Bridge.** `console.autoAnswer.hold { id }` is the Stop button;
  `console.sessions` → `asking.autoAnswer` says whether a timer will answer,
  when (`dueAt`) and with what (`picks`), or why not (`reason`, `why`).

## 3.617.0 - the revive nudge reaches the armed path, and a silent revived card stops saying `starting` (X-349) (2026-09-21)

- **‼️ The session that ASKED for a restart is spoken to again — on the path it
  actually uses.** The nudge was sent only when the asker was *also* cut
  mid-turn, and those two conditions can only both be true on the `now` path,
  where the restart fires inside the asking turn. On the `armed` path it waits
  for somebody else's turn to end, and by the time it fires the asker is
  between turns — so the nudge was **never** sent there, not once. The
  contract that "the last thing you say before a restart is what your resumed
  copy acts on" was therefore broken on the path the fleet is built around.
- **What changed.** Consent is the whole test now: the seat that asked is
  nudged in a turn or between turns. `midTurn` decides only what is *true*
  about the gap — a cut turn lost a reply and is told so, an idle one lost
  nothing and is told that instead. **X-310 is untouched**: a seat cut without
  asking is still brought back whole, told on its own card that nothing was
  said into it, and left for the user.
- **‼️ And a revived card nobody speaks into no longer sits at `starting` for
  ever.** The persistent CLI announces itself on its first *turn*, not on
  boot, so a seat deliberately left alone never left that state — measured at
  thirteen minutes on two cards. That is not cosmetic: `starting` counts as a
  turn in flight, so a silent revived card **blocked every later restart** —
  the farm's own door held shut by a session doing nothing at all. The card
  now settles to `idle` when the CLI's own live registry says its process is
  up, which is the engine stating it exists rather than Agent Farm assuming
  it; a process that never registers is given up on rather than invented.
- **What that `idle` rests on is said out loud.** `farm.health` gains
  `sessions.revived`: the cards a restart took up again that nobody has spoken
  into yet. They read `idle` because the registry says so, not because the
  engine has announced itself — and the flag clears the moment it does.
- **‼️ And the armed answer now says what will happen to your own seat.**
  `armed` means the restart fires later, out of your hands, so whether your
  last words are an instruction to your resumed self or are simply lost is the
  one fact that changes what you write next — and it was not in the answer at
  all. `reviveIntent` names the seat, says whether it will be spoken into, and
  says why not when it will not be (no `resume`, no named asker, a caller that
  is not a Console card, a session the engine never named).

## 3.616.0 - the binding resolution is kept; a live write asks about itself alone (X-348) (2026-09-21)

- **‼️ A transcript growing by a few hundred bytes no longer re-judges every
  session the farm has ever indexed.** `reconcileBindings` is wired to
  `onDidUpdate` — which fires on every live append — and it read
  `resolvedBindings()`, which walked every session against every binding on
  every call, and then asked `byId` (itself a scan) for each resolved run's
  progress figures. The trigger was the live write; the cost was the whole
  history, which is the exact shape X-127 exists to end.
- **What changed.** `SessionIndex` now KEEPS the resolution (task → the
  session that holds it, with the two run-progress figures riding along) and
  re-asks only the records that moved: a session marks itself when it is
  admitted, dropped or replaced, and a binding change marks the sessions
  X-345's `ReachIndex` already says that change reaches. Nothing else is
  touched. The rules the full walk had are kept: the first session to claim a
  task keeps it, and a task whose holder lets it go — a withdrawn binding, a
  session that left the index — is offered to whoever else can hold it rather
  than being lost with its holder.
- **The figures ride with the resolution** (`ResolvedBinding`), so the caller
  no longer scans for a session by id: one O(N) per binding, on the hottest
  path in the index, simply disappears.
- **Measured** (`test_launch_binding.js`, a year of sessions): the map is
  built once (1 000 walked at 1 000 sessions, 10 000 at 10 000); a call with
  nothing changed walks **0**; one transcript growing walks **1** at either
  size, in **0.14 ms at 10 000** against 0.82 ms at 1 000 — the cost no
  longer moves with the archive. The kept answer is compared against a forced
  full walk on the same index, task by task and figure by figure.
  `SessionIndex.lastBindingResolve` reports what each call really cost.

## 3.615.0 - a binding change sweeps what it reaches, not every session (X-345) (2026-09-21)

- **‼️ The launch-binding sweep is now the size of the change, not of the
  history.** X-128 made each comparison cheap and left the sweep alone: every
  task change still re-asked every session the farm had ever indexed, so its
  cost grew with the history (X-127's shared criterion: proportional to what
  CHANGED, never to what is stored). `setLaunchBindings` now works out which
  bindings came and went (`bindingDelta`, by a signature that carries every
  field a binding decides with or hands over — so a run that ends, declares
  its session, reports its transcript or changes mode is a change, and the
  same list in another order is not) and re-asks only the sessions one of
  those could reach: by declared id, declared file or lifespan window, out of
  a `firstTs`-ordered index kept in step with the session maps (`ReachIndex`,
  new `core/bindingReach.ts`). A removed binding reaches too — the session it
  was one of two candidates for may now have one. A change that alters no
  binding asks nobody.
- **Measured** (`test_launch_binding.js`, a year of sessions, 15 one-hour
  runs): publishing all 15 touches 2 sessions at 1 000 and 8 at 10 000; one
  run finishing touches 0–1 session in ~0.4 ms at either size — where the
  X-128 sweep cost ~23 ms per task change at 10 000 and grew with every
  session. **Reach is a superset of what the matcher decides with**, proven
  by brute force over 3 600 random sessions and 12 random changes: every
  session whose answer moved is reached, and the set is far narrower than the
  crowd. `SessionIndex.lastBindingSweep` reports what each change cost.

## 3.614.0 - a queued task no longer holds its account's token refresh (X-347) (2026-09-21)

- **‼️ A task waiting in the queue was counted as work running on its
  account**, and the account's OAuth refresh was deferred for as long as it
  waited — the busy guard (X-204) exists so a refresh never revokes the token
  a live CLI is holding, but a queued task has no process and holds nothing.
  A run parked on quota, concurrency or a budget for hours kept its slot's
  grant from ever being refreshed while nothing on that slot could be hurt.
  `accountIsBusy` now counts a console session and a **running** task only.
  Safe because `launch` marks the task running before anything is spawned, so
  `running` already covers a CLI's first read of the credentials file
  (`test_account_usage.js` pins both halves).

## 3.613.0 - four services on the bridge: forecast, web view, pack gallery, meaning index (B-19 closed) (2026-09-21)

- **New op `schedules.forecast`** — what the schedules will fire, when, and
  how busy that keeps the farm: the same forecast "Open Forecast" renders as a
  markdown page, as data (`upcoming` with each firing's median duration and
  success rate where there is a history, `queued`, `running`,
  `totalScheduledRuns`, `estBusyMs`). `days?` narrows the window,
  `markdown:true` also returns the page's own text.
- **New op `web.enable`** — turn on the read-only web view and answer the link
  a phone opens: mints the token if there is none, records the binding,
  switches `agentFarm.web.enabled` on and starts the server. **It opens a
  port**, so `confirm:true` is required and `bind:lan` (anyone on the network
  with the link can read the dashboard) only when the user asked for their
  phone. Already on → nothing is rewritten, `alreadyOn:true`, current link.
- **New op `packs.gallery`** — the agent packs on offer in every configured
  gallery (`agentFarm.packGalleryRepos`, git URLs or local folders, three
  folders deep); a source that cannot be reached is named in `errors`.
  Install one with the existing `agents.pack.import` and the pack's `file`.
- **New op `search.index.build`** — build or catch up the transcript
  meaning index behind the Search page's "Meaning" mode (`memory.semantic.build`
  is the other index). Refused when `agentFarm.embeddingsProvider` is off;
  `maxSessions?` caps one call; a build already running now answers
  `busy:true` instead of a silent zero (the command had the same blind spot).
- Each of the four commands and its op go through ONE closure (`forecastNow`,
  `enableWebView` + `webViewUrl`, `galleryPacks`, `buildSemanticNow`), so an
  agent gets what the person gets. Parity: 379 ops on the bridge, 25 open gaps
  (was 29). B-19 is closed.

## 3.612.0 - parallel.run: the parallel worktree launch on the bridge (B-17 closed) (2026-09-21)

- **New op `parallel.run`** — fan prompts out over git worktrees, one isolated
  headless run each: the same launch the "Agent Farm: Run Parallel…" command
  makes from its input box. Each prompt gets its own `git worktree` on an
  `af/` branch beside the agent's repo and its own task (`⑂ <name>`, workDir =
  the worktree), started at once; `agentFarm.maxConcurrentPerAgent` decides
  whether they really run side by side or in turn (`serial`). **`dryRun` is
  the default** — the answer is the plan (repo, `gitRepo`, `worktreeBase`,
  each run's worktree name, `serial`) and nothing is created; `dryRun:false`
  launches, and only when the user asked for the runs (N headless sessions,
  each spending quota). Prompts past 6 are never launched and come back in
  `dropped`; a folder that is not a git repository is a plan with
  `gitRepo:false` and a refused launch.
- **The launch lives in `core/parallelRuns`** (`parallelPrompts` ·
  `planParallel` · `launchParallel`), not in `extension.ts`: the command and
  the op go through the same two closures (`parallelPlanFor`,
  `runParallelFor`), so the op's dry run IS the plan the command warns about.
  The command now reports how many runs actually launched, not how many
  prompts were typed, and a task's `workDir` arrives with the task instead of
  being patched on afterwards.
- Parity: 375 ops on the bridge, 29 open gaps (was 30). B-17 is closed.

## 3.611.0 - dispatch.test: the dispatcher's answer on the bridge (B-17, first half) (2026-09-21)

- **New op `dispatch.test`** — ask the dispatcher where a piece of work would
  be routed without sending it anywhere: the text goes through
  `agentFarm.dispatchRules` (first match wins) and then, when
  `agentFarm.dispatchClassifier` is on and no rule matched, through the judge
  model against every agent's CLAUDE.md hint. Answer `{ agent, method: rule |
  model | none, reason }`. The command palette's "Test Dispatch" and the op now
  go through ONE closure (`dispatchFor`), so an agent gets exactly the answer a
  person gets. Parity: 374 ops on the bridge, 30 open gaps (was 31).
- B-17's second half — `runParallel` (fan one prompt out over N git
  worktrees) — is still an open gap; it is the next session's first item.

## 3.610.0 - "I search for a word I know is there and it says nothing": three measured causes, all closed (X-147) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ The Turkish i was never case-folded.** JavaScript's `/i` folds by
  Unicode SIMPLE case folding, in which İ (U+0130) and ı (U+0131) fold to
  nothing but themselves — so a query typed in lowercase never matched the
  word at the start of a sentence or in a heading written in capitals.
  Measured on the live corpus of 977 sessions: "istanbul" found 1 session and
  "İstanbul" was in 3; "ilk" found 1.412 matches and the 556 written "İlk"
  were not among them; "iki" missed 1.120, "için" 402, "işte" 207. Under
  case-insensitive matching i/İ/ı/I are now one letter (`media/afQuery.js`,
  so every filter box in the extension gets it, not only the Search page).
  Folding only the case pairs is not expressible under `/i` — the class
  `[ıI]` already admits `i` because I ≡ i — and joining the four openly is the
  better answer for a search: "kirmizi" typed on an English keyboard finds
  "kırmızı", and the case-sensitive mode is still letter-exact. ripgrep's `-i`
  does not fold these, so the candidate prefilter cuts a literal at the
  letter exactly as it does at `*` — a plan may never exclude a file the
  matcher would hit.
- **‼️ The session title was never searched.** `title` was metadata on a hit;
  the matcher ran over the messages and nothing else, so a session NAMED
  after the word and not containing it could not be found on the Search page
  — while `sessions.find` matched titles on another surface. The title is
  judged in the one reducer both engines share, first, as its own hit
  (`kind: 'title'`, `role: 'title'`, dated by the session's activity, under
  the same date window), whenever any conversation role is in scope; a
  memory-only / events-only search (`roles: []`) leaves titles alone. In the
  corpus a session the ripgrep candidate pass excludes is still put to the
  reducer for its name. The page draws it with a `title` badge; the bridge
  op's hits carry the same `kind`.
- **‼️ A session whose every match fell past the preview cap was not on the
  page.** The page built its session groups from the hits, and a fleet query
  for a common word fills the 250 previews out of the newest sessions alone —
  the bar said "1.412 matches · 472 sessions" and the list drew forty; the
  other four hundred, every one a real match, were nowhere. `sessionMatches`
  rows now carry the header (agent, title, id, engine, activity, author), and
  such a session is drawn as its header — "7 matches · none previewed (the
  250 previews went to newer sessions)" — sorts with the others and opens
  like any other.
- **The ripgrep battery had never spawned ripgrep.** The candidate pass
  starts at twelve million characters and the test fixture is thirty
  kilobytes, so every "ripgrep:" assertion passed without one process — the
  fallbacks were never exercised and nothing was ever narrowed. The threshold
  is overridable for tests (`CorpusDeps.rgMinChars`), the battery runs on the
  real binary beside VS Code, and a guard reads the spawn.

## 3.609.0 - the search corpus is bounded by ageing the tool trail, not by keeping fewer sessions (X-131) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ The corpus grew 1:1 with the transcripts and nothing ever pruned it.**
  Measured 253.7 MB over 977 sessions (doubled in under a month), 2.6 GB
  projected at 10 000, 0 entries prunable — the only rule dropped a session
  whose transcript was deleted, and transcripts never are. A size cap was
  measured NOT to be the fix: `orderSessions` caps nothing, a fleet query asks
  for every session, and anything evicted below that working set is rebuilt on
  the next query — the 7.5 s full re-parse the corpus exists to have ended,
  paid on every search.
- **So the bound makes each session cost less instead.** The tool trail
  (`tool` + `toolResult`) is 92.5% of the bytes and only an Everything search
  reads it; the default You+Agent search never does. Past a horizon after the
  transcript's last write, a session keeps its dialogue shards and loses its
  trail shards. The default search never rebuilds anything for it — cold or
  warm, measured by a guard that counts transcript reads. An Everything search
  that reaches an aged session re-parses that transcript on the spot, keeps
  the trail for the rest of the window, and the results say how many it
  re-read and why (`trailRebuilt`, in the Coverage note) rather than just being
  slow. A session past the horizon is built without its trail in the first
  place — nothing is written today to be unlinked tomorrow.
- **New setting `agentFarm.searchToolTrailDays`** (default 60, 0 = keep every
  trail for ever), category Search, read live and applied on the first search
  of each window. The age is the transcript mtime the manifest already stores
  (`signatureMtime`), so ageing rides the existing per-entry pass with no stat
  of its own, and `tools/measure_search_corpus.js --days N` names exactly the
  sessions the extension will age. Steady state: the trail of the last N days'
  sessions plus the dialogue of all of them — a bound set by activity, not by
  history.
- Chosen over a hard size cap (exact bound, seconds on every search) and over
  "measure and wait" (the corpus doubles monthly) — the user's own pick among
  the three, recorded as a decision in the project.

## 3.608.0 - one budget per token, not one per reader: why a single account of four kept hitting the rate limit (X-240) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ The account that got rate limited was the only one with TWO readers, and
  that was the whole defect.** Anthropic limits the usage endpoint per account
  token, and on this machine a token IS the credentials file it lives in.
  `AccountUsageService` walks every captured sign-in; `PlanUsageService` watches
  whichever one is STANDING. Both resolve that path through the same
  `slotCredentialsFile`, so whenever an account is standing the two are reading
  one token — and each kept its own floor and its own 429 curve for it. Two
  requests could leave milliseconds apart, and a refusal one reader took never
  held the other, so the hold meant to END a rate limit was walked through by
  the other door and renewed itself. There is one ledger now
  (`src/core/usageGate.ts`), keyed by the file; the two readers recognise each
  other without either having to know the other exists.
- **New setting `agentFarm.planUsageMinIntervalSeconds`** (default 10, floor 5)
  — the shortest gap between two requests for ONE sign-in, counted across the
  beat, the indicator, the turn-boundary read, a card's ⟳ and the bridge. It is
  a spacing rule, not a beat: it never causes a read, it only makes one that
  arrives too early wait its turn.
- **Four ways a hold was being walked through, all shut.** `refreshSlot` never
  checked the account's own backoff and its callers are not all people — the
  worst fires on exactly the account that has just hit a wall, so every
  automatic "re-read the figure that let it start" pushed the penalty further
  out; it now takes a `reason` and only a person spends through a hold. The
  bridge's `usage.engines refresh=true` claimed the person's privilege that
  `usage.plan` beside it deliberately refuses an agent. `accounts.status` —
  the op whose own description names an unattended runner as its caller —
  refreshed as a person too, so the caller most likely to ask over and over
  held the one reason allowed past a 429. And every guard in
  `PlanUsageService.read` sat inside `if (this.snap)`, so a service holding no
  cached snapshot obeyed neither its floor nor its backoff — which is not a rare
  state, because the snapshot is dropped whenever the standing account moves,
  the one moment something also force-reads.
- **A turn-boundary read that arrives too early is now deferred, not dropped.**
  The moment a turn ends is the moment the figures settle and also the moment
  the beat drops to the slow idle window, so a refused edge read used to leave
  the settled number unread for the whole idle interval. The indicator arms one
  catch-up instead — nothing waits, and turn boundaries arriving in bursts are
  absorbed by the one pending read rather than re-arming it.
- The plan-usage cache is now kept **per sign-in** rather than as one snapshot
  that was thrown away whenever the standing account changed. X-212's rule is
  unchanged and still exact — no account is ever drawn under another's name —
  but toggling between two sign-ins no longer spends a request each way, which
  it could not have afforded once the shared gate started (correctly) refusing
  a second request for a token read seconds ago.

## 3.607.0 - three doors an agent could not reach, and the one place a window changes project (B-18) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ Six pieces of code decided which project this window is on, and they did
  not agree.** The command, the quick pick, the bridge op, the Projects page's
  **Make active**, its **start a session here**, and the status bar's Clear each
  wrote `af.activeProject` themselves and then chose their own refresh — and the
  page's Make active refreshed **nothing**, so the tree and the status bar went
  on naming the old project until something else happened to repaint them.
  Writing the state and telling the window are one act, so they are now one
  function. `projects.current` and the command share it, which is what finally
  links that capability on the parity gate instead of carrying it as a gap.
- **New `console.forgetWindow`** — drops the remembered terminal window of one
  session. A window that was killed or moved leaves that memory pointing at
  nothing and the next open follows it instead of making a new one; until now
  only a person clicking the card could clear it.
- **New `projects.track.rebuild`** — re-derives a project's `Backloglog.md`
  session rows from the sessions themselves, the repair for a log that lost rows
  to a crash or was written before the transcripts it describes could be read.
  It shares its core with the page's button, so "rebuilt" cannot come to mean
  two different things.
- The gate moves with it: **370 → 373 ops on the bridge, 34 → 31 open gaps**,
  and `gapBudget` shrinks by exactly three.

## 3.606.0 - the search corpus is measured, and its prune stops blocking the window (X-131, partial) (2026-09-20)

- **The first search of every window no longer freezes it to decide there is
  nothing to prune.** The corpus' one pruning rule drops an entry whose source
  transcript is gone, and it asked that with a synchronous `existsSync` per
  remembered session — one per session that EVER ran, on the extension host's
  only thread. Measured here: **146 ms at 977 entries, and 0 of them prunable.**
