  At ten thousand sessions it is a second and a half of the window not drawing
  for the same answer. It is now asked through `fs.promises` with a yield, so
  the same rule runs off the blocking path.
- **New `tools/measure_search_corpus.js`** — what the cache costs, from figures
  the manifest already holds, so nothing is re-read or re-parsed. On this
  machine: **253.7 MB in 3 457 shards for 977 sessions, 92.5% of it the tool
  trail the default search never reads**, projected at 2.6 GB for 10 000
  sessions. It also prints the age curve, which is what any ceiling has to be
  chosen against.
- **‼️ The ceiling itself is deliberately NOT shipped yet, and the measurement
  is why.** Evicting the oldest shards to a size cap looks free — a dropped
  shard is rebuilt from its transcript — but `orderSessions` caps nothing, so a
  fleet query asks for EVERY session, and anything evicted below that working
  set is rebuilt on the *next* query. That is the 7.5-second full re-parse this
  cache exists to have ended, paid on every search instead of once. A real
  bound has to make each session cost less (the tool trail is 92.5% of it), not
  keep fewer sessions — which is a change to what an old tool-trail search
  costs, so it is the user's call rather than a silent one.

## 3.605.0 - the resident session index stops growing with the conversation (X-129) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ The index of every session that ever ran costs 69% less memory, and no
  surface loses a figure.** It lives in the extension host's one heap for as
  long as the window is open, and two of its fields were growing with the
  LENGTH OF THE CONVERSATION rather than with the number of sessions. Measured
  on this machine's 848 sessions (`tools/measure_session_heap.js`, real
  `heapUsed` across a forced GC): **23.9 KB a session → 7.3 KB**, 19.8 MB →
  6.1 MB. Projected at 10 000 sessions: **233 MB → 72 MB.**
- **Nothing was dropped by guess — both fields had a horizon that already
  existed.** `recentMsgs` is read only by windows shorter than 48 hours (the
  rolling 5-hour plan window, the lap meter, the dashboard's hour-exact tier),
  and the parser already filtered to 48h once; the index now re-applies that at
  admission, so it is bounded by recent activity instead of by history.
  `events` had exactly one reader — the activity feed's newest n — so the
  per-session arrays were answering a global question and are replaced by ONE
  bounded feed. `feed(60)` returns the same 60 events it always did, and the
  test proves it against the whole corpus rather than against a fixture.
- **The archive is untouched.** The store on disk still holds every session's
  whole record; the saving is in what stays resident. The projection is a copy
  precisely so the object handed to the store keeps its events — a trim in
  place would have written an archive with nothing in it and said nothing.
- New `src/core/sessionResident.ts` holds the rule alone, with no vscode
  import, so `tools/measure_session_heap.js` applies the SHIPPED projection
  instead of a description of it that can drift. `test_session_resident.js`
  reads `SessionInfo` out of the source and fails the build if a new
  array- or `Record`-typed field is added without being placed resident (with a
  written reason) or projected away.

## 3.604.0 - the supervisor cockpit: the user's word on any A2A card, a re-route, and ⚡ Run Now (N-7) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ A minimal `+` on every A2A card, and it costs the card nothing until the
  pointer is on it.** Press it and a compact editor opens directly under that
  row — the kind of word you are giving (**steer** do it this way · **veto** not
  this, do something else · **constraint** stay within these limits), the words
  themselves, and the buttons that act on it. It is drawn by the page's own form
  component (`media/afForm.js`), so it keeps the same bargain as every other
  form here: Ctrl+Enter submits, ✕ closes, and **the refusal lands in the card**
  — a directive with no words outranks every rule the agent has with nothing,
  and is refused there rather than written.
- **A directed card is now unmistakable from across the list.** The plain flag
  is gone; in its place a solid **👤 badge coloured by the kind of word** —
  amber for steer, blue for constraint, red for veto — with the directive itself
  in its hover, so the board is readable without opening anything. The `+` is
  the deliberate opposite: invisible until the card is hovered or the control
  has focus.
- **On a task the cockpit has three more hands.** **Re-route** hands the work to
  another role, optionally moving its project and workdir — the same call
  `a2a.tasks.reroute` makes, **under human authority**, so the loop guard does
  not apply, the count starts again and your directive travels with the work;
  re-routing to where it already is is refused rather than silently closing a
  task and opening its twin. **✕ Remove directive** takes your word off.
  **⚡ Run Now** stops waiting for the agent the task is for to come and look: a
  Console session opens on that agent with the claim as its first prompt. A
  closed task can still be marked, and says why there is nothing left to move.
- **‼️ Run Now changes nothing about the task.** The session it starts claims it
  through the same `a2a.tasks.claim` every agent uses, so a task somebody took
  while the window was opening is refused there rather than run twice — and it
  seeds and records like every other launch door (S-34), so the run starts on
  what that agent was last run with. New bridge op **`a2a.tasks.runNow`** shares
  that one launcher with the button; the three supervisor ops moved to
  `src/core/a2aSupervisor.ts`, the file that now holds that one subject.
- `parity.manifest.json` carries the six new doors; `test_a2a_pages.js` and
  `test_a2a_bridge.js` pin the cockpit at its three arities (undirected ·
  directed with every control · closed) and the four refusals, and each arity
  was photographed in both themes before this line was written.

## 3.603.0 - the agents' own inbox: A2A Notes and A2A Tasks pages, four tabs on one strip (N-6) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ What agents leave for each other, and the work they hand over, now have
  pages.** `🤖 A2A Notes` and `⚡ A2A Tasks` sit beside `🔔 Notices` and
  `📥 Queue` on one four-tab strip — the user's inbox on the left, the fleet's
  on the right, a separator between the pairs — and the strip is drawn by the
  one function all four pages already shared, so a fifth tab is one line. Their
  counts (live notes, open tasks) are **grey badges on their own tabs and
  nowhere else**: they travel under `a2a` in the same push as the other two but
  never reach the status-bar bell, because a note one agent left for another is
  not something the user is being asked to read.
- **One card grammar for both** (`media/afA2A.js`): ONE line per row — category
  or state badge, title, the five coordinates as chips (project by NAME, a
  broadcast as the word `any`, never a bare asterisk; an absolute workdir as its
  last segment with the whole path in the hover), author, readers or claimant,
  age; click to open the markdown body, the files, a `Label: value` facts table
  and the actions. A supervisor directive is drawn as the block the bridge
  prints (N-8). A **claimed task carries its lease as a bar** — how much of the
  30 minutes is left, in green / amber / red, with the claimant's own progress
  beside it — and a closed task carries none, because its lease is history.
- **The hand a person has, through the same store the bridge writes:** resolve
  / reopen a note, **⚡ Convert to task** (the promotion `a2a.tasks.fromNote`
  does, with the same refusal once a live task exists — the card then offers
  "Open task" instead), cancel a task; a task links the note it grew from, the
  queue item it came out of and its parent task, each a click to that board.
  Steering, vetoing and re-routing are the supervisor cockpit (N-7).
- Filters are the pages' own: state · category · author · project on notes,
  state · author · target role · project on tasks, a query box over every field
  a reader would search, and the ↺ that clears them. `parity.manifest.json`
  carries the sixteen new doors; `test_a2a_pages.js` runs both pages on real
  Turkish content at three arities (empty · one · the board), and every scene
  was photographed in both themes before this line was written.

## 3.602.0 - a task switch stops re-deriving the same strings for every session (X-128) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ Every task switch re-binds every session, and the number of sessions only
  goes up.** Bindings are held down by monthly archiving — about fifteen — but
  the matcher re-derived the same normalised strings inside the loops: the
  binding's folder once per *session*, the session's transcript path once per
  *binding*, all from a small fixed set of strings, all giving the same answer.
  Over 94 profiles that was 14.3% of all blocking (32 s, ≈97 million calls). The
  bindings are prepared once now (`indexBindings`) and the whole sweep shares
  one prepared set. Measured on this machine at 10 000 sessions × 15 bindings:
  **115 ms → 23 ms, 5.0×**, with all 10 000 answers identical to the previous
  matcher — the change is a speed change and nothing about attribution moved.
- **‼️ And the obvious fix was measured and thrown away.** Indexing the bindings
  by folder and walking a session's parent folders to find them reads like the
  answer, and it is **1.5× slower** at fifteen bindings: a hash lookup per
  ancestor, plus the arrays it allocates, costs more than a linear pass with
  early exits. What was expensive was the re-deriving, not the scanning. Both
  numbers are in `test_launch_binding.js`, so the next person to have that idea
  reads the measurement instead of repeating it.

## 3.601.0 - the filter box you can edit in the middle, and two sections that answer it properly (U-143, U-140) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ The filter box was append-only.** Every keystroke redraws the page, which
  destroys the box under the hand and builds a new one, so the caret has to be
  put back by hand — and it was put back at the END. Correcting a typo in the
  middle of a query threw the caret past the last character on the very next
  letter, and a query is exactly the kind of text you edit in the middle. It
  goes back where the reader left it now.
- **‼️ Typing `Obsidian` HID the section that word names.** The two sections that
  are not made of setting rows — Engines, and "Open documents with" — gated
  themselves on `TERMS.includes(what you typed)`: the question backwards, asked
  in a different language from the one every row above them answers. So `-foo`,
  `a OR b`, a quoted phrase and whole-word mode each hid a whole section instead
  of filtering the page, and the docOpen gate compared case-sensitively on top.
  Both use the page's own grammar now (`media/afQuery.js`), like everything else
  that searches.
- **‼️ …and the engine names are read off the engines.** `ENGINE_TERMS` spelled
  out claude, codex, openai, gemini and google by hand, so it had never heard of
  `opencode`: the one engine added after somebody typed that string was the one
  engine you could not search for, and nothing said so. The section's search
  text is derived from `DATA.engines` — id, label and the command you type — so
  an engine added tomorrow is searchable the day it appears.
- **‼️ An open dropdown holds the background refresh.** The page pauses its
  refresh while a field has focus, but the guard named `INPUT` and `TEXTAREA`
  and forgot the one control that can be *open* when fresh data arrives: a
  `<select>`. The list shut under the hand and the choice was lost, with nothing
  on screen saying why.
- With this, the **U-140** umbrella is closed: U-139, U-141, U-142 and U-143.

## 3.600.0 - switching the web view on used to take the whole extension down (X-344) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ `agentFarm.web.enabled` bricked every installed build until it was turned
  off by hand.** The switch is read during `activate()`, and the server it
  starts took its first snapshot on the spot — but the snapshot reads bindings
  declared further down `activate()`, so it reached a `const` before its
  initializer had run: `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'projectRollup' before
  initialization`, thrown out of activation. That is not a broken web view: the
  extension never finishes activating, so there are no commands, no pages and no
  bridge, and it shows only as "Activating…" that never ends. Because the
  setting is shared by every version, rolling back to older builds changed
  nothing — which is exactly how it was met, as a product that looked destroyed
  by whatever had shipped last. The snapshot now waits one tick, by which time
  activation has returned, and it can no longer throw into a timer either.
- **And the suite can see this class now.** `test_activation.js` had only ever
  activated a machine whose settings are untouched, so every optional surface
  answered its own `false` and its activation-time work never ran. It activates
  a second time with **every boolean setting package.json contributes turned
  on** — derived, not listed, so a switch added tomorrow is covered the day it
  is contributed. Against the old code that pass reproduces the user's
  ReferenceError exactly.

## 3.599.0 - Enter saves a scalar box too, and + add lands the caret everywhere (U-139, U-141, U-142) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ Enter lets go of a one-line SCALAR box, which is how it saves (U-139).**
  A one-line setting commits on `change`, and `change` fires on blur — so a
  reader who typed a value into an ordinary `agentFarm.*` box, a Claude Code
  box or one of the two "Open with" boxes and pressed Enter watched nothing
  happen, and had to click elsewhere to commit it. Blur is deliberately the
  mechanism rather than a second message: the page HOLDS a background refresh
  while a field has focus, so an Enter that kept focus would write the value and
  leave the old one on screen. The alert rows, the quiet hours and the
  announcement template already did this; these were the boxes that were missed.
- **‼️ `+ add` lands the caret in the row it just made — in the table and the
  pair editor too (U-141).** The list editor learnt this in 3.597.0; the other
  two redrew and left the hand with nothing to aim at. A table row opens in its
  FIRST DECLARED field, a pair in its NAME box — the one that cannot be left
  empty, because a pair with no name is refused on save. Neither saves anything,
  and the cells already typed into survive the redraw.
- **‼️ `↺` cleared every draft of a value and not the VIEW they were made in
  (U-142).**
  Reset already threw away the JSON, list, form, rows and map drafts — a box
  still showing the old edit would be a lie — but left `jsonMode` set, so the
  setting stayed a textarea with nothing left in it to show. Unlike Apply there
  is nothing to wait for here: a reset only removes a key and cannot be refused,
  so the mode goes with the value.

## 3.598.0 - the escape hatch lets go, and a next step names the setting (U-142) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ "Edit as JSON" was a one-way door.** `jsonMode` was set when the reader
  asked for the raw box and nothing ever cleared it, so a setting the schema
  describes completely — a list, a form, a table, a set of pairs — stayed a
  textarea for the rest of the session once it had been applied once. The
  structured editor comes back when the save lands, which is also the plainest
  proof it landed; `Edit as JSON` is still one click away.
- **‼️ …and a refusal does not throw the reader out of the box they were
  writing in.** Clearing the mode on Apply is only half the answer: the host
  parses the text and answers `error` when it cannot. The text that was sent is
  now held until one of the two answers arrives and put straight back if it was
  refused — so a mistyped brace costs nothing. Before this, applying broken JSON
  dropped what was typed and showed the stored value instead.
- **A next step names the setting and never says "here" (U-142).** The Telegram
  bridge card is drawn on Farm Settings, on the Telegram page and in the
  bridge's own answers, so "here" meant a different place on each. On Farm
  Settings it pointed at a card that carries no control at all while the box it
  meant was a separate row further down. The empty-allowlist step now names
  `agentFarm.telegram.allowedChats`. ‼️ The guard that pins this is written
  across EVERY state rather than the one that was reported, and it immediately
  caught a second one nobody had noticed: `disabled` said "Switch it on here"
  on a card with no switch on it.
- The dead `settings.json` button U-142 also named was fixed in 3.597.0 (U-139):
  the action exists in the Farm Settings header and the host answers it.

## 3.597.0 - Farm Settings answers the hand: Enter saves, and the page keeps its place (U-139) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ Enter saves the editor the box belongs to — all four shapes.** Reported
  as *"you press enter and nothing happens"*, and it was exactly true: a box in
  the list editor, the form, the table or the pair editor was bound to `change`
  only, which fires on blur and merely fills the draft. Enter — the one key a
  single-line box is expected to answer — did nothing at all, in every editor on
  the page, so the whole surface read as disconnected. The save now lives in one
  function per shape (`applyList`, `applyForm`, `applyRows`, `applyMap`) instead
  of inside a click handler, and one rule binds Enter across `data-lrow`,
  `data-frow`, `data-rrow` and `data-mrow`. Each reads the boxes itself, so the
  value being typed right now is the value that is saved; a refusal the button
  would have shown is still shown; a multi-line box keeps Enter for its newline.
- **‼️ The page keeps the reader's place across a redraw.** `render()` replaces
  the whole of `#app`, and Farm Settings is the longest page in the extension.
  Pressing `+ add`, `Edit as JSON` or `✕` two thirds of the way down threw the
  reader back to the top, and what they had pressed never came into view — so
  the second half of the report, *"you press the json link and nothing
  happens"*, was a control that had worked every single time and could not be
  seen doing it. `window.scrollY` is now carried across the swap. `+ add` also
  puts the caret in the row it just made, which is how a press proves it landed.
- **The file this page is a view of, from the page itself.** A `settings.json`
  action in the Farm Settings header opens VS Code's own user settings file —
  the one every box here writes into and the `↺` buttons remove keys from.
  Reaching it used to mean knowing the command palette.
- Measured: `test_settings_form.js` 63 → 78 — Enter in a row, a form field, a
  table cell and a pair box each save that editor and carry what is being typed;
  no other key saves; a refusal is not walked past; the scroll is restored for a
  reader who was down the page and not written for one already at the top; the
  caret lands in the new row and the rows already typed into survive it (U-108's
  rule, driven rather than spelled).

## 3.596.0 - the user's word first, and the A2A road proven end to end (N-8, N-9) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ The supervisor directive is the FIRST thing an agent reads (N-8).** A
  note or task carrying the user's `humanDirective` answers `a2a.tasks.claim`,
  `a2a.tasks.next`, `a2a.tasks.heartbeat` and `a2a.notes.get` with
  `supervisor` as its first key — a `⚠️ [HUMAN SUPERVISOR DIRECTIVE] — steer |
  veto | constraint` block that says, in the block, that it outranks the
  constitution, the agent's own instructions and the task's text. The
  heartbeat is the moment a directive set *after* the claim reaches its
  holder, which is why the heartbeat answer carries it too. `directiveBlock()`
  in `a2aNotes.ts` is the one renderer; the "Run Now" prompt (N-7) will use
  the same one.
- **The agent side of A2A exists now (N-8).** `ajanlar/_REF/a2a.md` — note vs
  task, the coordinates and the strictness table, the session-start glance,
  the claim · heartbeat · finish loop, the loop guard, the directive as
  supreme override, English-as-technical-spec as the board's language, and
  `@args.json` for every payload. One trigger row in the constitution; an
  **A2A board [session-start]** duty on developer, explorer, manager and
  genel (`a2a.status` with each agent's role and capabilities); the
  cross-engine copies re-synced in the same commit.
- **The road is proven end to end (N-9).** `test_a2a_cli.js` spawns the real
  `af.js` against a temp bridge folder with a runner standing in for the
  extension: the session id the CLI publishes names the caller with nothing
  typed, `@args.json` and `--stdin-base64` carry Turkish and backticks intact,
  `key=value` coerces csv and numbers, `--out` writes UTF-8 without a BOM, a
  refusal comes back as `ok:false` with its `detail`, and the claim ·
  heartbeat · finish · result-note loop works over the wire. The stores test
  now also pins TTL sweeping (only what is both resolved and expired goes) and
  the lineage that travels with a handoff (`sourceNoteId`,
  `sourceQueueItemId`). With `test_a2a_stores.js` (75), `test_a2a_bridge.js`
  (102), `test_a2a_matching.js` (63, six-process claim race) and
  `test_a2a_cli.js` (18), the A2A suite is the four files N-9 named.

## 3.595.0 - whose is this: the A2A matching engine (N-5) (2026-09-20)

- **One engine under both stores** — `src/core/a2aMatch.ts`. A note and a task
  are addressed the same way, so "is this mine, and how well" is answered by
  one `fit()` that `noteScore` and `claimable` now stand on; the two copies of
  the axis logic N-3 carried are one. Five coordinates, each with a job:
  **project** contains, **targetRole** addresses (what strictness is about),
  **subsystem/topic** describe (they rank; they exclude only under `hard`),
  **targetSession** is lineage (the one session — a resume keeps its id —
  this is for; `*` = any). `requires` is a filter in every mode.
- **‼️ The project contains in EVERY mode.** Under `any`, a note or task is
  open to anyone *in the project*; a fleet-wide one says `project: "*"`.
  Without this the wildcard added nothing to `any`, and work about one project
  landed on every other project's board.
- **‼️ `preferred` is `hard` on the role for a while, then `any`.** The target
  role has the work to itself for `agentFarm.a2a.preferredGraceHours` (default
  2; `0` opens at once); a task nobody of that role took in that time opens to
  whoever else fits the project, ranked below an exact fit. A claim inside the
  window is refused as **`reserved for its target role`** and the refusal
  carries `opensAt` and the `axes` (which coordinate hit, missed or was wild),
  so an agent can come back at the right moment instead of polling. Without
  the clock, `preferred` and `any` were one rule with two names.
- **A capability name is validated, not trusted.** `requires` and
  `capabilities` are lower-cased and de-duplicated, and a name that is not one
  (`a-z 0-9 _ -`, e.g. `write tools`) is refused by name — the alternative was
  a task that silently never matched anyone.
- **`a2a.tasks.next` ranks the closest fit first**, the oldest within a fit —
  an exact-role task outranks one that merely opened to you, even when newer.
- **‼️ The claim race is proven with real processes**: `test_a2a_matching.js`
  spins six node processes to the same instant against one file; exactly one
  claim wins, every loser is told why, and the lock is gone afterwards. N-3
  proved it with two store objects in one process — this is the cross-process
  lock doing it for real.
- Rows written before `targetSession` existed read as `*` — a legacy note or
  task is still for any session.

## 3.594.0 - what one agent leaves for another, reachable from a shell (N-4) (2026-09-20)

- **Eighteen `a2a.*` ops open the A2A stores N-3 built.** `src/core/a2aBridge.ts`
  is a thin door over `A2ANotesStore` / `A2ATasksStore` (two files under
  globalStorage, `a2a-notes.json` · `a2a-tasks.json`): every handler calls the
  store, and the page that comes in N-6 will call the same methods. Notes:
  `post · list · get · resolve · sweep`. Tasks: `add · fromNote · list · next ·
  claim · heartbeat · finish · cancel · handoff`. Supervisor: `directive.set ·
  directive.remove · tasks.reroute`. And `a2a.status`, the session-start glance
  in figures — unread notes for you, tasks you could take, what you hold with
  the lease left, what you handed over by state, what is blocked for a person.
- **The caller says who it is, or the session does.** `agent=` is taken as
  written; without one the session id the CLI published to its own children
  (X-310) is looked up on the host — a hosted Console card first, then the live
  monitor, then the index — and an op that writes refuses when neither names
  anyone. **The project is filled in the way Notices fill it in (N-1)**:
  omitted, it is the project the caller runs under and the answer says so
  (`projectFrom`); a name resolves to the id; `"*"` means every project and is
  never overridden.
- **A finished task wakes its poster.** `a2a.tasks.finish` leaves a RESULT note
  addressed to the agent that handed the work over (category `result`, same
  project and topic), so the caller finds it on its own next `a2a.notes.list`
  rather than by polling. `notify=false` keeps quiet.
- **A human reroute is the way out of the loop guard.** `a2a.tasks.handoff`
  (agent→agent) makes a new task at depth+1 and blocks the third hop, as N-3
  designed. `a2a.tasks.reroute` is the user's move: no guard, the new task
  starts at depth 0, and the user's directive travels with the work — a person
  deciding where blocked work goes is what the guard was waiting for.
- **A note is promoted once.** `a2a.tasks.fromNote` refuses a note that already
  has a live task and names it (`again=true` to mean it); `resolveNote=true`
  closes the note now that it is work.
- **Reading marks, listing does not.** `a2a.notes.get` records the reader
  (`markRead=false` to peek); `unreadOnly` on the list then leaves it out.
- **Two arguments the catalogue promised as optional were read as required
  (X-334).** `telegram.inbox` with no `id` — the "every conversation" form its
  own describe advertised — threw `Missing required string arg "id"`, and
  `console.answer` with `answers` alone threw for `response`, so a question
  could not be answered by option label over the bridge. Both read `optStr`
  now, and ‼️ **the rule is measured**: `test_bridge.js` reads every op in the
  catalogue (435) and fails any `name?` in a describe that meets
  `argStr(args, 'name')` in its handler. Twelve conditional requirements
  ("required for scope session") are named on a list that may only shrink.
- A finished task keeps its claim as history, so `claim` on it now says
  `not open for claiming` rather than `already claimed` — the latter is a live
  lease only. `direct(id, undefined)` takes a directive off a note or a task.

## 3.593.0 - the farm on one phone screen, and the commands that act on it (U-116) (2026-09-20)

- **`/status` now says what is LEFT on each plan**, not only what the day has
  cost. One line per engine that publishes a figure, and — the point of the
  block — an engine that publishes none is **named with the reason**
  (`No figure: Codex (keeps a quota but writes it nowhere readable), Gemini
  (billed per token — no window to be a percentage of)`). A missing quota is
  never rendered as 0%: that is the one mistake that turns telemetry into a lie
  somebody acts on from a bus stop.
- **`/sessions` rows say where a conversation GOT TO** — its turn count, and
  what it has stopped for (`⏳ your answer`, `⏳ permission: Bash`), which is
  the one thing on that screen worth opening a laptop for. Under the list, one
  **button per conversation**: the number still works for a reader scrolling
  back, but the list in front of them is now one tap from being the focus.
- **`/cancel <number>` interrupts a live turn.** With no argument it still
  stops the headless run this chat started — from a phone "stop it" is one
  thought, and making the reader remember which kind of thing they started is a
  design that serves the code. The conversation is named the same three ways
  `/focus` accepts, and an ambiguous word is asked about rather than guessed.
- **`/agents` says what each agent thinks with**, not only its name — the
  figure you are actually choosing between. **`/agent <name> <prompt>` runs
  that prompt now** in the same thread, under the same daily budget shield;
  `/agent <name>` alone still just binds the chat. ‼️ The split is made against
  the REAL agent names, longest first, because an agent's name is a folder name
  and a folder name can carry a space — counting words would bind `data` and
  throw `scientist plot the costs` away.
- **‼️ A chat that is not on the allowlist is now answered only while the
  allowlist is EMPTY.** An empty allowlist is a bridge being set up and the
  reader needs the id it reports to finish; once one chat is allowed, a
  stranger who finds the bot learns nothing — not that it exists, not which
  farm it is.
- `telegram.commands` on the bridge renders the same screens without a bot
  token: `help`, `status`, `sessions` (text and keyboard) and `agents`. It
  calls what the chat calls rather than drawing a second copy, so the op and
  the phone cannot say two different things.
- `src/core/telegramCommands.ts`, pure, 62 tests.

## 3.592.0 - a message typed on a phone waits its turn, and asks before it costs or breaks something (U-115) (2026-09-20)

- **Write to a conversation that is already working and your message now
  WAITS** instead of cutting into the turn. From a phone you cannot see what
  the agent is in the middle of, so the default is to queue: the chat is told
  `⏸ developer is working (turn 3). Queued — it goes in when this turn ends.`,
  and the moment that turn ends the message goes in as the next turn's first
  words. `agentFarm.telegram.whenBusy` = `queue` (default) or `steer`, which
  sends it into the running turn on the engines that can take one.
- **‼️ And that queue survives a window reload**, which the Console's own does
  not — measured: nothing in the revive path carries it. The phone's queue is
  part of the saved chat state, beside the reply map that already had to
  survive one, because "queued" said to somebody standing at a bus stop is a
  promise. One message is released per turn, oldest first, and a chat cannot
  pile more than ten into one conversation.
- **The daily cap now counts the turns the phone starts**, not only the
  headless runs it launches. A conversation the phone drives is marked, and
  each of its turns bills the DIFFERENCE it cost into the same ledger
  `/status` already reports. Over the cap the turn does not start: the chat
  gets both figures and a `✅ Run it` / `✖ Cancel` pair.
- **A destructive command typed with a thumb is asked about once first** —
  `rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean -f`, a force push, `git branch -D`,
  `DROP TABLE`, `Remove-Item -Recurse`, `del /s`, `format <drive>`. Matched on
  the SHAPE of the command, never on intent: "clean up the temp files" is
  English and goes straight through, and guessing at intent would have stopped
  half the ordinary sentences and still missed the one that mattered. A gate
  you have already said yes to is not asked again — the waiver travels with
  the message while it waits.
- The four gates run in one order and the order is the design: the
  conversation is still there · today's money · what the sentence would DO ·
  whether a turn is running. A cap checked after the turn started is not a cap.
- `/status` says how many messages are queued from this chat, `/help` says what
  happens to one sent into a working conversation, and **`telegram.inbox` on
  the bridge** reads the queue, the messages stopped at a gate and today's
  budget (`action=drop` clears one conversation's queue without touching its
  turn). `src/core/telegramExecution.ts`, pure, 70 tests.

## 3.591.0 - the turn as a card a phone can read, and the taps that answer it (U-114) (2026-09-20)

- **When a Console turn ends, or an agent stops to ask you something, the
  Telegram bridge now sends the chat a card** — three blocks under Telegram's
  4096: what the agent SAID this turn (its own closing words, tool noise left
  out; cut at the head when long, so the verdict survives), what it is waiting
  on, and what the turn cost (tokens on a plan-billed engine, a price only
  where there is one — X-19). `src/core/telegramDigest.ts`, pure and measured
  without a bot.
- **Buttons, not words to type back.** An AskUserQuestion's options are one
  button each; a tool permission is Allow / Deny; and under them Continue
  (idle) or Cancel (working), Diff and Status. A tap is acknowledged the moment
  it is read (the phone spins until it is), then applied against the
  conversation's state NOW: an option only if that question is still the one
  pending, a permission only while that request is open — a tap on
  yesterday's card cannot answer today's question. Answers go through the same
  `consoleHost.answer` the panel's own card uses.
- **Who hears it is the routing layer read backwards** (`agentFarm.telegram.digest`,
  default `focused`): the chat focused on the conversation, or the only live
  one — where a reply to the card would be routed from. `all` widens it, `off`
  closes it; never a chat outside the allowlist. The memo runs while the bridge
  is off, so switching it on announces nothing old, and a reload re-announces
  no turn (a pending question, being actionable, is announced on first sight).
- **📄 Diff is the working tree's `status --short` and `diff --stat`**, not the
  diff: from a phone the question is "did it touch what I think it touched".
  On the bridge as `console.changes`; the card itself is readable as
  `telegram.digest` (read-only — see what the phone will be shown, and who).
- Transport: `getUpdates` now asks for `callback_query`, a tap parses to an
  `InboundMessage` carrying the card's id, `sendMessage` carries the keyboard
  as `reply_markup`, `answerCallbackQuery` is new.
- ‼️ Not tried on a live Telegram — this machine's vault holds no bot token;
  measured with the injected transport, as U-113 was.

## 3.588.0 - a sign-in's card stops saying it was idle when it was working (X-333) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ X-333 — the complaint, exactly as it was put: a card reading `last used
  3d ago` — or `today — nothing ran here` — for an account used an hour ago
  and three times that day.** Not a rendering fault. X-251 made the
  LaunchManifest the one reader with no fallback, on purpose: the alternative
  then on the table was guessing the machine's current sign-in onto an
  unplaced run, which puts one account's dollars on another's card. That
  refusal stands. What was wrong is that a manifest was treated as the only
  RECORD in existence — a terminal the user opened themselves, a session
  resumed under another sign-in, anything from before X-251, all seal no
  manifest, and the card then called the account idle. That is not "I do not
  know"; it is a wrong answer stated plainly.
- **Three more records now speak, behind the manifest and never instead of
  it** (`src/core/accountAttribution.ts`, `accountEvidence.ts`):
  - the CLI's own `<slot>/sessions/<pid>.json` — not one of the shared
    junctions, so a record under a slot is a process that really ran with that
    directory as its config dir. Certain, and the only thing that can place a
    session started from a bare terminal;
  - the slot's own `.claude.json` → `projects[<cwd>].lastSessionId`;
  - the slot having been **touched** at all — a time with no session attached,
    which is what turns "nothing ran here" into "active 11m ago".
- **‼️ AND THE TRAP THAT MAKES THE THIRD OF THOSE DANGEROUS, measured rather
  than assumed:** `.claude.json` is one of a slot's OWN files, so capturing a
  slot COPIES it and the copy carries the other account's history — on this
  machine five session ids appeared identically under all four Claude slots. A
  value that is not UNIQUE across slots is a copy and is **dropped**, never
  handed to the first slot alphabetically. A touch at or before the slot's
  capture is the capture, not a run.
- **Nothing guesses.** Every layer is a record somebody else wrote down; where
  none exists the answer stays absent and the unattributed row keeps its
  meaning. The layer that answered travels with the answer, and a **touch
  funds nothing** — it names no session, so it adds no dollars to any card.
- **On the card:** a run a record names keeps its agent, its 24-hour run count
  and its way into the transcript. A sign-in only touched says `active 11m
  ago` and draws none of those, having none. The spend line above it narrowed
  with it — `today — no run recorded here`, because "nothing ran here"
  directly above "active 11m ago" was not vague, it was a contradiction.
- **On the bridge:** `accounts.attribution` — which record places which run on
  which account, what each layer could see, and `copiesDropped`, the number to
  read first when a figure still looks wrong.
- Tests: `test_account_attribution.js` (24), `test_account_evidence.js` (14),
  the two card shapes drawn in `test/fixtures/enginespanel.js` and pinned in
  `test_engines_page_accounts.js`, the op's contract in
  `test_accounts_bridge.js`.

## 3.587.0 - a phone message now knows which conversation it is for (U-113) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ U-113 — the chat bridge could talk to ONE agent, and on a farm running
  three conversations that is a wrong answer rather than a missing feature.**
  `/agent <name>` bound the whole chat; a "yes, do it" typed about one
  conversation was started as a fresh headless run for whichever agent the
  chat happened to be bound to, and nothing said so until that agent had
  acted on it. A plain message is now ROUTED, and Telegram answers the
  question twice before anything has to be guessed
  (`src/core/telegramRouting.ts`, wired through `chatHandle`):
  - **The reply chain.** Every message the bot sends *for* a conversation is
    remembered against it (`sendMessage` returns Telegram's own message id —
    it used to be thrown away at the transport, and an id dropped there can
    never be recovered). Replying to that message names its target exactly,
    with no state to go stale, and it still works days later: the map is
    persisted with the chat state and bounded to the newest 500 entries.
  - **The forum topic.** In a group with Topics on, each conversation gets a
    thread of its own (`🧵 developer · AgentFarm`), opened the first time the
    bot speaks for it, and everything typed in that thread flows to that
    conversation. A group that is not a Forum — and a bot that was never given
    `can_manage_topics` — falls back to the main thread and keeps talking;
    the bridge never goes quiet over a decoration.
  - **The focus.** `/sessions` lists the live conversations, numbered;
    `/focus 2`, `/focus developer`, `/focus <id>` or `/focus off` says where
    plain messages go. `/status` now says it too, on the one screen somebody
    checks before typing.
- **‼️ AND AMBIGUOUS IS AN ANSWER, NOT A FAILURE.** Where nothing decides and
  more than one conversation could be meant, the bridge REFUSES and asks, with
  the candidates numbered the same way `/sessions` numbers them — one list,
  one numbering, because the reader answers the question off the list. A
  single live conversation is not a choice and is never asked about.
- **A conversation that ended keeps no seat.** All three maps are pruned
  against the live Console sessions on every message, so a remembered id that
  has since finished falls through to the layer below instead of the reader
  being told their instruction reached something that is gone.
- **The routed message reaches the conversation, and says which and why** —
  `→ developer · AgentFarm (reply)`. On an engine that cannot be spoken into
  mid-turn the answer says it was held and goes in when the turn ends, rather
  than reporting a delivery that did not happen.
- **On the bridge:** `telegram.routing` (the conversations, the topic bound to
  each, which chats point where, and whether a focus still resolves) and
  `telegram.focus` (set or clear a chat's focus — refused by name when the
  word fits two conversations). No token and no chat content crosses either.
- Tests: `test_telegram_routing.js` (42), `test_telegram_transport.js` (13 —
  the outbound half of the bridge had never been run by anything),
  `test_telegram_bridge.js` (16), plus the command parsing in
  `test_access.js`.

## 3.586.0 - the status bar follows the conversation on screen, and the plan card can be read for any sign-in (X-243, X-244, X-242, U-137) (2026-09-20)

- **‼️ X-243 — the indicator stops answering for the wrong account.**
  `activeAccounts` says who the NEXT session runs as; the Console card in
  front of you may already be running as somebody else, and then the standing
  account's percentages are a correct figure about the wrong sign-in. While a
  Console conversation is on screen and running as another account, the strip
  follows it and NAMES it (`$(dashboard) murvietnam · 21m - 97% / wk 64%`) —
  a name only appears while it is not a constant (U-40). It falls back the
  moment the Console goes behind a tab, the card is deselected or the
  selection is on the standing account (`ConsolePanel.watchedAccount` +
  `onWatchedAccountChanged`, which fires only on a real change, never per
  streamed token). The panel says what it is following before any figure, and
  the two doors that would act on the wrong account — **Check now**, which
  spends a request against the machine's own credentials, and the engine
  picker — are replaced by **Open Accounts** and the sentence that says how
  the bar comes back.
- **‼️ X-244 — the Plan usage card is a picker, not a label.** X-212 put ONE
  owner on the card; on a machine rotating between sign-ins, "how are the
  others doing" was a page away. The head now carries a compact `<select>`
  (`pu-pick`) of that engine's sign-ins — the standing one first and marked
  `★`, each row `name · 72%` with its windows, plan, reading time and sign-in
  health on its own `title`. Picking one redraws the card from that account's
  own reading: **no request is sent and nothing is stood up** — looking at a
  sign-in must never move every future session. A slot nobody has read says
  `not read` and draws its note, never 0%; and a picked row never claims the
  endpoint's beat, because its figures move on the accounts beat instead. One
  sign-in on the engine keeps the plain X-212 label — a one-row `<select>`
  would lie about what the machine can do.
- **U-137 — the wait keeps its minutes.** `AFAccount.turns` rounded to a
  single unit, so everything from 3h to 3h59m read `(in 3h)` — the figure a
  session is decided on. It is `leftOf` now, the same function the bars use,
  and it reads the SNAPSHOT clock rather than this machine's, so a card and
  the chip above it can no longer disagree about one turnover. The fixture
  landed on an exact 4h, which is why no picture of it had ever shown the
  defect.
- One conversion for both: `engineUsageFromSlot` (`src/core/accountUsage.ts`),
  the inverse of `usageFromEngine` — `not-published` survives it, and a
  reading with no bars left is `unknown` rather than `ok`.
- Suite 391 files · 23 833 passed · 0 failed. New `test_status_bar_account.js`
  drives the real `PlanUsageBar`; two new plan-card scenes photograph the
  picker parked off the standing account, read and unread.

## 3.584.0 - a bare placeholder can no longer eat the backlog, and the ways into the Accounts page (X-332, X-237) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ X-332 — A BARE `<tag>` IS PUT IN CODE, ON THE WAY IN AND BY THE TIDY.**
  A placeholder written as text (`<ALAN>`, `<id>`, `<model>`) reads to
  Markdown/Obsidian as an unclosed HTML tag and can swallow every heading and
  task line below it. `src/core/backlogSanitize.ts` (`sanitizeBacklogTags` ·
  `sanitizeBacklogMarkdown`) wraps it in a code span, and it runs in three
  places: `addBacklogItem` and `setBacklogFields` (only when new words are
  given — a priority press does not rewrite the text), so the page, the
  bridge's `projects.backlog.add`/`.set` and every agent pass the same gate;
  and `tidyBacklogFile`, BEFORE the reseat and the sort, so 🧹 Tidy repairs a
  file already broken and says how many it wrapped (`sanitized` on the op and
  the page's line).
- **Only a tag left OPEN is touched — measured on the real backlog first.** A
  dry run of the first draft wrapped 40; three kinds were wrong and are now
  kept: the `<br>` the user breaks long items with (void elements), a path
  like `C:\Users\<user>` (a backslash-escaped `<` is already literal), and a
  line whose inline code quotes `<!-- -->` (a code span and a comment are one
  left-to-right scan, whichever opens first wins). A pair closed on the line
  (`<b>…</b>`), fences, multi-line comments, front matter, `](<…>)` link
  targets, autolinks and paths are left alone too. The fence chosen is never
  the length of a literal backtick run on the line, or that run would pair
  with it. The real file now has 25, all placeholders; it was NOT rewritten —
  that is the user's press. `test/test_backlog_sanitize.js` 33 checks.
- **X-237 — the doors.** The Agents view's title bar opens the Accounts page
  (`$(organization)`) in the slot `+ New Agent` held; `+ New Agent` stands
  beside the Dashboard's Agents heading (the same command, `dashboard.ts`
  `newAgent`); Farm Settings' engines section has 👥 Open Accounts beside
  ⚙ Open Engines; and the Farm Status card's Accounts row opens the Accounts
  page instead of the Engines page. Parity: `dashboard.ts#newAgent`,
  `settingsPanel.ts#openAccounts` (navigation). `test/test_accounts_nav.js`
  13 checks; both headings measured and the dashboard photographed.

## 3.580.0 - Antigravity's quota, read from its own /usage — "writes no file" was never "has no source" (X-306) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ THE FIGURE WAS A LOCAL COMMAND AWAY THE WHOLE TIME.** Antigravity's row
  has said `not published` since 2026-08-10, on a true measurement — the CLI
  refreshes a quota internally and writes it to no file. But the `/usage` a
  user types in a session is expanded in print mode too (the
  `--disable-slash-commands` flag exists to turn that OFF), and
  `agy -p /usage --output-format json` answers in ~4 s with `num_turns: 0` and
  every token counter at zero: a local command, not a turn, no token (measured
  2026-09-19, agy 1.2.7). The answer is structured — two POOLS on one account
  (Gemini models · Claude and GPT models), each with a 5-hour and a weekly
  window, a remaining fraction and an ISO reset.
- **Wired the way the catalog is.** The extension runs it in the background
  (`refreshAgyUsage`: the `agy models` shape, `stdin.end()` included — the
  binary does not exit while its stdin is open) on the SAME BEAT as Claude's
  indicator, keeps it with its arrival time, and repaints the status bar and
  the Dashboard card when it lands (U-31: a read nobody sees is not a read).
  `readAgyUsage` in `engineUsage.ts` parses it; until the first answer the row
  is `unknown` — never 0%. *Check now* on the Antigravity strip runs the
  command at once; `usage.engines refresh=true` does the same on the bridge
  (and spends one request on Claude only when Claude is asked).
- **The percentage is the CLI's own, as used.** `/usage` prints REMAINING and
  rounds it (`64%`); a bar here is USED, so it is the complement of that same
  rounding (36%) — what the reader saw in the CLI a second ago, not a floor
  that disagrees by a point. A window the CLI stated no fraction for draws NO
  bar (the first draft drew 0%, which is the one thing this module exists to
  never draw).
- **Two pools on one strip.** Antigravity's short window names collide
  (`5h`/`wk` twice), so — only when they collide — each field carries the
  pool's initials: `G 4h 18m - 1% / G wk 36% / CG 5h 0% / CG wk 0%`. Every
  other engine's strip keeps its shape.
- **Seen, not just tested.** The Dashboard card drew FOUR bars for the first
  time (dark and light) — and the "not read yet" scene showed a pre-existing
  defect: `Checked 07:00 (00:00 UTC)` under every unread engine, epoch 0
  printed as a clock. Fixed: no read, no clock.
- Docs: `MOTORLAR-TASARIM.tr.md` §5.5 (the measurement, and the Git Bash
  `/usage` → `C:\Program Files\Git\usage` path-conversion trap that cost one
  wasted turn while measuring), `YENI-MOTOR-EKLEME-SOP.tr.md` → usage/quota
  ("writes no file" ≠ "has no source": ask for a slash command or subcommand
  first; `not-published` is the LAST answer).

## 3.579.0 - the one live smoke, and the gate it proved on a real wire (X-117 closed) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ EVERYTHING THE MOCKS CERTIFIED, SEEN ONCE ON A REAL WIRE.** The suite
  stays token-free by design, so the live smoke is a tool outside it:
  `tools/smoke_live.js` runs ONE short turn per engine through the same
  resolver the product launches with (`providerRegistry` →
  `spawnEnvironment` / `-m`), spends nothing without `--yes`, and `run-all`
  never sees it. Run once with the user's approval, both legs green:
  - **Claude, first-party, `haiku`** — nothing chosen, nothing touched: the
    session's own sign-in served it. Exit 0 in 7.6 s, the engine reported
    `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, its own usage (in 10 / out 220) and its own
    cost ($0.018) arrived, the transcript named NO route (the design in
    `MOTORLAR-TASARIM` §8.4, now measured live), and `billingOf` placed it on
    the plan window at an API-equivalent dollar.
  - **OpenCode, the engine's own free provider** — `opencode/ling-3.0-flash-fin-free`
    in a temp XDG home with no `auth.json`. Exit 0 in 9.3 s, answer `pong`,
    the engine's own `step_finish` (tokens 11571, cost 0), `opencode export`
    reporting provider and model, `billingOf` → `engine-reported`, off the plan
    window, the user's own store untouched.
- **‼️ AND THE GATE WAS PROVED ON THE WIRE, WHICH THE MOCKS COULD NOT DO.** The
  first free model in the engine's catalog (`jev-1.13-free`) publishes no tool
  calling; `preflight` refuses it by name. Run past the refusal, the live turn
  exited 1 after 80 s without a word — exactly what a session on it would have
  met. The tool therefore takes the first free model the product's own gate
  PASSES and names the ones it dropped; the SOP's provider-axis gate gains
  step 11 (a live leg per new engine, once, with approval).
- **Kimi and MiniMax stay mock-only** — no paid key exists for either; the
  user's decision (2026-09-19). Their routes are measured end to end against
  the local Anthropic endpoint and nowhere else.
- Docs: `MOTORLAR-TASARIM.tr.md` §8.9 (the measurement table),
  `YENI-MOTOR-EKLEME-SOP.tr.md` → provider axis step 11,
  `OPENCODE-ENTEGRASYON.tr.md` → the free-provider live measurement and the
  seven free models the provider served that day.

## 3.578.0 - where the context figure comes from, and a measurement in a comment that had quietly stopped being true (X-117, part 5) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ X-113 — THE CONTEXT FIGURE IS THE ENGINE'S, AND ON A THIRD-PARTY ROUTE
  THAT IS THE POINT.** A gateway counts its own tokens; a number assembled this
  side would be a guess wearing the engine's authority. The Claude end-to-end
  file now pins the SOURCE rather than the shape of it: the usage the endpoint
  declared is the usage that comes back out of the run, on the routed wire, from
  the CLI's own single `result` event.
- **‼️ AND THE VARIANT SOURCE, ASKED OF THE ENGINE RATHER THAN OF A COMMENT —
  WHICH IS HOW THE COMMENT WAS CAUGHT.** `consoleEngine.ts` recorded a
  measurement: not one reachable OpenCode model published a reasoning variant,
  so the effort box is not offered on that engine. Put to the engine's own
  catalog on a live run, the answer came back different — the `opencode`
  provider serves eight models and THREE publish variants
  (`ling-3.0-flash-fin-free` at low · medium · high, and two `muse-spark` builds
  at minimal · low · medium · high · xhigh). A measurement written into a
  comment ages silently; one asked on every run cannot, and the stale reading
  has been replaced by the new one beside the reason it did not change the
  answer.
  - **The box is still not offered, and that is now a different decision rather
    than the old one (X-330).** Variants are published PER MODEL: a flat list
    across the picker would offer `xhigh` on a model that publishes three
    levels, which is the same defect as a control with no referent at all; and
    ACP declares only `model` and `mode` as session config, so a hosted card has
    no channel for one and the box would work headless and not in Console.
    Doing it properly — a list derived from the selected model's own row — is
    its own item; flipping the flag alone would ship the half that misleads.
  - What the test pins is therefore the SHAPE of the answer, not a number that
    will move again: some models publish variants and some do not, and that
    unevenness is the reason. The day they all agree, or none does, the suite
    says so.

## 3.577.0 - the composition every unattended run shares, watched on the wire; and the third list nobody was reading (X-117, part 4) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ ONE SHAPE CARRIES THE ROUTE INTO EVERY UNATTENDED RUN, so that is where
  it is worth watching.** A retry, a workflow step, a schedule and a trigger all
  build their task by spreading `runExtras(<what was stored>)` — the rule this
  repo states as *a run's dimensions travel by the SHAPE, never a hand-written
  field list*, which exists because the automatic retry once hand-copied eight
  fields and silently dropped seven, the route among them, on the path where
  nobody is at a window to notice. A unit test can say the shape carries the
  field; whether the composed task then reaches that endpoint is a different
  claim. `test_e2e_task_route.js` now builds a task exactly the way the
  automatic retry builds one — from a run that really happened — starts it, and
  watches it arrive at the first run's endpoint with that route's key and tier
  model, and at no other.
- **‼️ AND THE THIRD HAND-WRITTEN LIST, WHICH WAS PINNED BY NOTHING.** Two of
  the three bodies that carry a run's dimensions forward are held against
  `RunDimensions` read out of the source, so the next dimension somebody adds
  fails the suite until they carry it too. The third — `retryTask`, the retry a
  PERSON presses and the one the bridge calls — was held by nothing at all. It
  carries all eighteen today; the point is the nineteenth, which would have been
  dropped silently on the path with somebody watching who has no way to see it,
  with every test green. It is now read the same way the other two are.
  - Measured rather than assumed on the way there: a first reading reported the
    route missing from that body, and it was not — `retryRoute` is computed just
    ABOVE the call, because a retry is a new enqueue and takes its own seal. The
    test's window says so, so the next reader does not repeat the alarm.

## 3.576.0 - the second wire inside one binary, and the two documents a new engine is added from (X-117, part 3) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ THE CONSOLE DOOR ON OPENCODE, WHICH IS NOT THE ONE ALREADY MEASURED.** A
  Claude card is a `claude -p` process per turn. An OpenCode card is not: ONE
  shared `opencode acp` process serves every card on the host and the turn
  travels as a JSON-RPC frame on its stdin. `run` and `acp` are two different
  programs inside one binary, and only the first had ever been watched.
  `test_e2e_opencode_console.js` runs a hosted card through the real ACP process
  against local mock endpoints: the provider the CARD named is the one that
  holds the wire — its endpoint, its bearer — the other declared provider is
  never touched, and the session is written into a temp data home rather than
  the user's.
  - The ACP child inherits this process's environment, and that is the design
    rather than a gap: `nodeOpencodeIo` passes no `env` because this engine owns
    its own sign-in — its account axis is deliberately `unmapped` (moving the
    XDG data root would move every other XDG application with it: a side effect,
    not an isolation) and its route resolves to no environment of Agent Farm's
    at all.
- **‼️ THE SOP A NEW ENGINE IS ADDED FROM HAD NO PROVIDER AXIS IN IT.** 1 690
  lines of end-to-end procedure, and not one mention of `dataOwnerOf`,
  `resolveRuntime`, `spawnEnvironment` or `launchRouteRefusal` — so an engine
  added today would ship with no answer to "who serves it", and every isolation
  guarantee on the axis would quietly not apply to it. The SOP now carries the
  axis as a gate of its own (before the engine may appear in any route picker)
  and as ten implementation steps: decide whether the axis exists at all (no
  axis is a real answer, not missing data), name the owner of each of the four
  data parts, read the catalog from whoever owns it, what `resolveRuntime`
  returns and why `clearEnv` without which `spawnEnv` is half an answer, never
  build the environment yourself, where the REPORTED identity comes from when
  the stream does not carry it, one rule for a route that is gone, the resume
  verdict, the billing semantics — and the proof, which is the wire and not the
  argv.
- **The engines design document now describes the axis it predated.**
  `MOTORLAR-TASARIM.tr.md` stopped at the fourth engine; it now carries phase 5:
  why engine and provider are separate axes at all (the transcript does not
  record which endpoint served a turn, so a wrong run and a right one were
  indistinguishable), the data-ownership table, the two environment shapes and
  the one order they are built in, requested vs reported, third-party cost as
  arithmetic on no plan window, one refusal rule asked by three doors, the
  resume verdicts, and the table of which file measures which door.
- Route health was looked at in both themes at the arity that shows every
  verdict — a pass, a failure, a superseded row, an unknown one and the two
  notes that are not faults — and reads correctly in each.

## 3.575.0 - the three doors nobody was watching, run end to end on a route (X-117, part 2) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ THE TERMINAL DOORS, WHICH ARE THE OPPOSITE SHAPE OF PROBLEM FROM THE ONE
  ALREADY MEASURED.** A Console card is handed a COMPLETE environment, so a name
  left out of it is a name removed. A terminal is handed an OVERLAY that VS Code
  merges onto the window's own, and the OS window is handed the same map to say
  in its shell's words — on both of those a route name left unsaid SURVIVES
  inherited, which is the entire reason `terminalEnvOverlay` exists and exactly
  what no test had ever run a CLI through. `test_e2e_terminal_route.js` runs the
  real `claude` three ways in a window that already carries a route: through VS
  Code's own documented merge (`string` sets, `null` removes), through the
  `.cmd` the external launcher really writes (run by cmd.exe, so `set "NAME="`
  is the clearing and the values arrive through a file the script eats and
  deletes), and through the `export`/`unset` prefix in a real POSIX shell. The
  key it carries holds `=`, `%` and `!` — the three characters the Windows
  script's own comment claims survive its `for /f` parse, and the claim had
  never been run. The script is also read before it is run: the key is not in
  it, and after the run neither the values file nor the script is left behind.
  - **‼️ AND THE CLEARING IS FALSIFIED, NOT ASSERTED.** The same turn with the
    route's `clearEnv` dropped is expected to carry the inherited bearer onto
    the wire — and does. A guard nothing can turn red is not a guard.
- **‼️ THE HEADLESS DOOR — THE ONE WITH NOBODY IN FRONT OF IT.** Every other
  file on this axis replaces `launch` with a recorder and measures the decision,
  so what an unattended spawn actually put on the wire had never been watched.
  `test_e2e_task_route.js` drives the real `TaskManager`: a queued task naming a
  route reaches that endpoint with its key and tier model while the route in the
  machine's own shell is never touched; a task naming a route that has since
  been removed is refused at the spawn (X-116) — failed before it started, and
  nothing at all on any wire; a task naming NO route runs on the inherited
  endpoint untouched, which is the rule.
- **‼️ RESUMING A CONVERSATION: THE GATE'S VERDICT, ON THE WIRE.** X-109's gate
  has been read in tests since it was written; the risk was never the answer but
  the spawn not obeying it. `test_e2e_resume_route.js` opens a real conversation
  on a route, then resumes it and asserts ONE relation — whatever the gate says,
  that is the endpoint the process talks to. Resumed with nothing asked it is
  pinned to what it ran on; resumed asking for another route the wire follows
  the verdict whichever way it falls; a refused resume is a run that never
  happens.
  - **‼️ AND THE GATE HAD A VERDICT WHOSE WORDS AND BEHAVIOUR DISAGREED.** A
    binding it did not recognise was described as *having a launch record* while
    the decision — which tests for one by name — treated it as having none. Two
    opposite statements in one answer is worse than either alone, and it read as
    a product defect for an hour while this was being written. An unrecognised
    binding now says which route the session ran on is not known.
- **‼️ AND ONE FINDING THAT IS THE ENGINE'S, WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN ABSORBED
  (X-329).** Two `opencode run` processes started at once against ONE
  `XDG_DATA_HOME` raced the engine's own SQLite store: measured in a suite pass,
  one exited non-zero with *database is locked* and its turn never happened.
  Nothing in this repo writes that database, but two cards on one account share
  exactly that home. The OpenCode end-to-end file now gives each concurrent run
  a home of its own — so a claim about PROVIDERS is not quietly also a claim
  about locking — and the product question is a backlog item instead of a
  comment nobody would find.

## 3.574.0 - both engines' provider paths, run end to end against local mock endpoints (X-117, part 1) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ THE WIRE ITSELF IS NOW WATCHED, NOT ASSUMED.** Every unit test of the
  provider axis stopped at the environment or the argv Agent Farm builds; what
  the CLI then SENT, and to whom, was never seen. Two new files run the real
  CLIs against local HTTP servers speaking the Anthropic Messages and the
  OpenAI Chat Completions APIs — nothing leaves the machine and no real token is
  spent (measured: a Claude turn ~3.5s, an OpenCode turn ~18s on this PC).
  - `test_e2e_claude_routes.js` — Kimi and MiniMax routes through Agent Farm's
    own resolver and `spawnEnvironment`, **concurrently**: each reaches its own
    endpoint with its own key and tier model, never the other's; an inherited
    base URL, key, bearer token and model reach neither routed wire (mutating
    the clearing turns it red — the overwrite alone does not hide it); a run
    with nothing chosen goes to the inherited endpoint untouched, which is the
    rule. A gateway answering under its own model name is recorded beside what
    was asked; the CLI's own cost figure is arithmetic on no plan window.
  - `test_e2e_opencode_providers.js` — two custom providers declared the way a
    user declares them: the catalog is read from `opencode models --verbose`,
    the adapter resolves `-m provider/model`, both run at once and reach only
    their own endpoint and key, and `opencode export` reports the provider that
    ran. The user's own OpenCode data and config are never touched (`XDG_*`
    point into a temp folder, asserted).
  - `test_e2e_console_route.js` — the Console door: a hosted card through the
    real `ConsoleHost`, handed the resolver the extension hands it, with the
    inherited route sitting in the window's own environment. The card's own
    `providerId`/`tier` is what reaches the wire; dropping it at the spawn turns
    three checks red.
  All three skip, not fail, when their CLI is not on PATH; the mock endpoints are
  shared in `test/e2e_mocks.js`.
- **‼️ AND THE FIRST THING THE WIRE FOUND WAS IN 3.573.0.** The Claude catalog
  lists the shipped route TEMPLATES (`kimi`, `minimax`) even with no profile
  behind them, so the new *Route health* check — which asked the catalog — called
  a removed `kimi` profile alive while the task runner, asking the launch rule,
  refused it. Health is now handed the spawn's own rule (`launchRouteRefusal`),
  so the two readings cannot disagree.
- **‼️ AND A FOLDER NOBODY MEANT TO SHIP CANNOT RIDE INTO THE ARTEFACT ANY MORE.**
  Packaging this release put a `scratch/` a session had left behind — twelve
  files of session dumps, one letter off the ignored `scratchpad/` — inside the
  VSIX, and every gate passed: the leak rule names the workshop folders it
  already knows, the stray rule sees root FILES rather than folders, and the
  untracked rule looks inside `docs` and `media` only. `verify_vsix` now states
  what the artefact's top level may hold (`dist` · `docs` · `media` · `out`)
  instead of guessing at it from the other side, so the next stray name is
  caught without anybody having to predict it. `scratch/` and `*.stackdump` are
  ignored by both git and the packer.

## 3.573.0 - a route that is gone stops being run on, and every file that answers it a second time is named (X-116, closes) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ A TASK WHOSE ROUTE WAS REMOVED WHILE IT WAITED RAN ANYWAY — ON WHATEVER THE
  SHELL CARRIED.** Measured against the registry: a removed profile resolves to
  an `unknown` identity with nothing injected AND NOTHING CLEARED, so an
  inherited `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` reached the run untouched — the exact isolation
  X-101 exists to guarantee, undone by a delete. The spawn wrote a `route-drift`
  line saying the profile went, and then started anyway. It now asks the same
  rule the enqueue applies (`launchRouteRefusal`) and a named route that cannot
  be run on ends the task as *failed before it started*, with the reason and a
  warning — never a task standing in `running`. ‼️ Only where Agent Farm holds
  the route catalog itself (Claude): an engine-owned catalog may simply not have
  been read yet, and there the engine is the authority that refuses.
- **…and the saved choices that still name a gone route are reported BEFORE they
  fire.** Removing a route does not (and should not) edit the records that name
  it. `providers.status` and the Engines page's *Route health* now list them,
  grouped by route, with what each kind will do: a schedule is refused each time
  it fires, a queued task when it starts, and an **agent default** starts that
  agent's runs with nothing injected and nothing cleared. Nothing is called gone
  against a catalog nobody has read.
- **‼️ THE ENGINES' OWN CONFIG FILES, DIAGNOSED READ-ONLY.** The fleet-wide
  `~/.claude/settings.json` env block was already checked (X-114); an agent's own
  `.claude/settings.json` / `settings.local.json` were not, and a route variable
  or an `apiKeyHelper` there answers the route a second time for that agent
  only. OpenCode's global and project `opencode.json(c)` are now read for the
  default `model` / `small_model`, the user's own `provider` block and
  `disabled_providers` / `enabled_providers`. A bare model id there is a problem
  and stays **unknown**, never guessed; a provider the read catalog does not offer
  is refused; with no catalog read it is neither. `config` on the report lists
  every file read, its scope and the agents it reaches — a nest-level file shared
  by five agents is one entry naming five. ‼️ The module imports no file system
  and is handed a reader, so it cannot write; no value from an `env` block,
  `options.apiKey` or `headers` reaches a sentence (canary-tested). Measured on
  this machine: five `settings.local.json` files and the global
  `opencode.jsonc`, all clean — no false positives.
- **A stored route read in an older shape, or skipped, now says so.** The reader
  filled in a missing `engine`/`revision`/`label` silently and DROPPED a route
  whose id could not be a keychain key — a route typed by hand with a space in
  its id was simply not there, on any surface. `readProfilesReport` is the same
  read with what it did said out loud; a skipped route is a problem, an upgraded
  one a note, and the stored copy is never rewritten by reading it.

## 3.572.0 - an account card draws every wall it has, as one chart (X-215 round 2, closes) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ ONE BAR, TWO DIFFERENT WINDOWS, AND NOTHING SAYING WHICH.** The user's
  own reading of the Engines page: "the used/left bar shows the weekly quota on
  some accounts and the five-hour one on others — apples and oranges." It was
  not a drawing bug. X-309 taught a slot to carry whichever window is FULLER,
  because either wall really does end a run — so the window under the bar
  changed from card to card, correctly, and silently. A sign-in barely into its
  five hours and nearly half through its week read `12%`, which is true about
  one wall and useless about the one that will actually stop you.
- **The card now draws every window the reading carries, as ONE chart.** Not two
  stacked blocks with their own captions and reset lines — that doubles a card's
  height for one extra number. The tracks sit 6px apart in a fixed gutter
  carrying each window's short name and percentage (`5h  91%` / `wk  64%`), so
  they line up on the same left edge and read as a pair. Each track takes its
  own colour, so a full five-hour window goes red beside a week that is fine.
  ‼️ The distance that mattered was not the margin: the rows were 15px tall
  around a 6px track, so the tracks sat 12px apart — twice their own height —
  until the text box was collapsed with `line-height:1`.
- **…and underneath it, the figures complete and in the unit each window
  deserves.** `5h: 37m left (02:17) · wk: 4d left (14 Sep 2026, 01:40)`. The
  five-hour window is read in minutes and the week in days; the old single
  rounding printed `2h` for both, which drops the minutes a session is decided
  on and never says "days" at all. The unit comes out of the REMAINDER, not the
  window's name, so an engine whose windows are neither gets a true answer. ‼️
  And a turnover that is not today now carries its DATE — every reset on this
  page printed as a bare `02:17`, which is right for five hours and a half-truth
  for a week.
- **‼️ THE ENGINE PATH WAS DROPPING ITS SECOND WINDOW ON THE FLOOR.**
  `usageFromEngine` took `eu.bars[0]`, so Codex — which publishes
  `codex_primary` AND `codex_secondary` — could not have had its week drawn even
  after the card learned how. Worse, taking bar ZERO rather than the fullest is
  the X-309 defect again on the other engine: a Codex sign-in at 8% of its five
  hours and 72% of its week read as 8%, and the pool kept opening rounds on it.
  Both are closed by the same shape.
- **`SlotUsage` carries its windows as a LIST (`bars`), replacing the four
  hand-named fields X-326 added.** `fivePercent` / `weekPercent` (+ their
  resets) hard-coded that an account has exactly two windows and that they are
  five hours and a week — right for Claude and only for Claude. Each entry names
  itself (`id`, `window`, `short`, `percent`, `resetsAt`), so a picker, a card
  and the bridge all iterate instead of counting to two. `accounts.list` returns
  it, and its `describe` no longer tells an agent that `percent` is the
  five-hour window — it is the fullest one, which is what a rotation is
  decided on.
- **‼️ AND THE NAME NEARLY DRIFTED AGAIN.** A `PlanBar`'s title is worded as
  Claude Code's own `/usage` prints it ("Current session"), while the rest of
  this product has one name for that window and it is "five-hour window". A card
  carrying the reading's spelling in its bars and the product's in every
  sentence around them would have said two things about one window — the exact
  shape of the defect audit B-04.3 closed, with neither name wrong. The
  five-hour row is named by the host (`windowNameOf`); every other row keeps the
  name whoever measured it gave, which is what lets Codex's week be Codex's
  week. The guard that pins this could not survive a card with two windows —
  it asked "what window names are within ±90 characters of this figure" — so it
  now asks the pairing exactly: each figure against its OWN window's name, never
  against the other's. Verified by mutation.

## 3.571.0 - an emptied sign-in stops calling itself healthy, and the engine test runs as the account it is drawn beside (X-219 round 2, closes) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ A DATE IS NOT A CREDENTIAL, and the account health check believed one.**
  `claude-kateanhkim` sat on this machine with `accessToken: ""`,
  `refreshToken: ""` and a `refreshTokenExpiresAt` a month away — the only field
  anybody read — so the row was stamped `ready`. The card then HID its 🔑 (it is
  hidden on a healthy row, X-275), which is the expensive half: the account was
  dead, said it was fine, and offered no way back. Every other reader in that
  file already asked whether the grant is THERE; this one asked only when it
  expires. Now an emptied grant is `needs-signin` whatever its expiry says — and
  so is an expired access token with no refresh token behind it, which is the
  same fact one hour later. A LIVE access token with no refresh beside it still
  reads `ready`, because it still works and the card already counts it down.
- **‼️ THE ENGINE TEST SPENT ITS TURN ON WHICHEVER ACCOUNT THE WINDOW HAD
  INHERITED.** The button (and `engines.test`) ran `claude -p` in the main config
  directory every time, never binding the standing sign-in's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`
  — so on a machine whose main account was walled, the user tested an account
  with quota to spare and read a verdict about a different one. Both doors now
  aim the turn through the same pair a launch resolves with
  (`accountResolution` → `accountEnvFor`), and the machine's own sign-in CLEARS
  the variable rather than blanking it (X-101).
- **‼️ …AND A SPENT PLAN IS NOT A BROKEN ENGINE.** A walled turn answered `✗ The
  command exited 1` — a red cross against the CLI, the credential and the route,
  none of which had been tested at all. A wall is now the `refused` shape (⊘,
  U-59): nothing was proved, so nothing is claimed, and it names WHICH window,
  because a five-hour one reopens in hours and a weekly one in days. What a
  limit looks like is not re-decided here — it is `limitWindow`, the one rule
  that already decides whether a failed RUN may be retried. And the engine's own
  limit line now survives: `firstFault` hunts for crash words (error, fatal,
  denied, refused) and a CLI announcing a quota uses none of them, so *"Your
  limit will reset at 5am"* — the single most actionable sentence it prints —
  was the one sentence being dropped.
- **A link repair that could not run said nothing at all.** When the pool
  directory is absent the repair refuses to invent it (right — inventing it
  would point every slot at a home directory nobody chose), but it refused
  *silently*: the clause read `wrote:false, error:undefined`, the badge stayed
  red, and pressing Complete again changed nothing and explained nothing. It is
  now named as a failure. Refusing to invent the pool is still right; refusing
  silently is the Principle 1 fault the repair journal exists to end.

## 3.570.0 - at a limit the sign-in that carries the work on is the user's choice, what a retry IS comes back into the form it was saved from, and Engines is one press from every page (X-226 round 2 + M-34, close) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ X-226 (round 2) — A RUN THAT MEETS A WALL NOW STAYS PUT UNLESS YOU SAID
  OTHERWISE.** The first cut moved a walled run onto whichever account had room,
  with no setting and no question: an account picked for the night on purpose,
  and a different plan spent by morning. The handover is now OPT-IN and it is
  named - `carryOn` on the retry policy, "At a limit, carry on with" on the
  form, `agentFarm.taskRetry.carryOn` as the standing default. Absent means
  **stay**: the run keeps the sign-in it was given and waits for that plan's own
  reset. Set it and it is still a narrow permission - a rule (`@emptiest`,
  `@round-robin`, one of your named rules) chooses among the engine's OTHER
  captured accounts, or a slot id names the one account to carry on with, and a
  **named account is never substituted**: if it has no room either, the wait
  stands. Never across engines (a carried-on run resumes a transcript, and a
  transcript belongs to one CLI), never the account that just refused the work,
  never a run pinned to the machine's own identity, and never for a wait shorter
  than the handover would itself take. Whatever happens, the `retried` event
  carries the sentence for it - including why a handover that was asked for did
  not happen.
- **‼️ M-34 — A RETRY POLICY REOPENED AS SOMETHING ELSE, AND SAVING THE FORM
  WROTE THE LOSS BACK.** `behavior`, `continuationPrompt` and
  `unknownProgressFallback` (M-10) were read off the form and stored, and never
  seeded back into it: a task saved as "continue it - pick up where it was cut
  off" opened in Edit as "a fresh run", its continuation prompt gone, and the
  next save made that the truth. One seam, one repair - and the list is now
  `RetryPolicy` itself, read out of the source: a field with no box, no seed, no
  reader, no home on the blank draft, **or no name in the `tasks.add` describe**
  fails by name, so the next field cannot be dropped the same way. The page is
  4.6k lines and it did not need rewriting; what it needed was for that seam to
  be measured.
- **🔌 Engines is in the global toolbar, on every page.** It was reachable from
  the Dashboard's Farm Status row and from the Settings page and nowhere else -
  a destination about what this machine can run at all, filed two clicks behind
  two pages. It is drawn as its icon alone, between ⌕ Search and ⚙ Settings,
  with the same hover contract as its neighbours. And the router now answers for
  it: `handleAfNav` looks a destination up and does nothing at all when the key
  is missing, so a nav button whose id never reached that record draws, hovers,
  depresses and opens nothing (X-234 was exactly that on the Farm Status card) -
  every destination the shared header can name is now checked against the
  commands behind it.

## 3.569.0 - the route a run was served by is a filter of its own, beside the engine, on every surface that lists runs (X-111, closes) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ PROVIDER · PROFILE · MODEL as three multi-pick filters on the Sessions
  tables and the Turns page, beside Engines and combined with everything by
  AND.** The engine is not the provider (X-110): `claude` pointed at Kimi is
  still the Claude CLI, so "Claude Code, only Kimi" is two ticks in two pickers,
  not a special case. Providers lists the routes the rows actually hold, by the
  chip's own label, plus **"no route"** for the runs on none - "everything that
  did NOT go through a route" is a real question and a filter that could only
  narrow to rows with a value could not ask it. Profiles appears only once a
  row carries a stored route profile (Claude routes only); Models lists what
  ANSWERED - never what was requested (X-108). A picker is offered only when
  there is more than one value to pick between.
- **‼️ ONE RULE, TWO RUNTIMES (`media/afRunFilter.js`).** Which rows a selection
