  matches is decided in one file the pages run in the webview and the host runs
  for the bridge (`src/core/runFilter.ts` requires the same file, as the query
  grammar and the clock already do), so a page and an agent cannot disagree
  about which sessions ran through Kimi. The rule, stated: a turn that names
  its own provider (an OpenCode turn) is the most specific answer and wins; a
  turn that names none - **every Claude turn, for ever** - inherits its
  session's route; a session that used several providers matches when ANY of
  them is ticked, because "which runs touched Kimi" is the question the filter
  is asked with; `null` is no filter (a route that appears tomorrow is included
  by itself), `[]` is nothing.
- **The Turns page had no idea which route a turn's session ran on.** `TurnRow`
  carried only what the engine named per turn - empty on Claude - so a
  Claude-via-Kimi turn was unfindable. Every turn row now carries `providers`
  (resolved by the rule), `profile`, `route` and `routeLabel`, the hover names
  the session's route, and the identity is the SAME one the Sessions table
  draws its chip from: `sessionIdentity()` in `core/turnRuntime.ts` is now the
  one place that decides manifest · engine · external, replacing three
  hand-written copies (the table, the Turns page, and `sessionIdentityOf` in
  the host).
- **The bridge asks the same three questions.** `turns.list` and
  `sessions.recent` take `providers?` / `profiles?` / `models?` (one id,
  comma-separated, or a list; `(none)` = no route) and every row now carries
  `providers`, `route` and `profile`. `sessions.page provider=kimi` opens the
  Sessions page already narrowed to that route (`setProviderFilter` - the same
  ✕ that clears every other filter clears it), and the page's header says
  `via Kimi`.
- **The text box finds a route by name too** - "kimi" typed on the Sessions
  table matches the route's id and label the way a tick does.
- Fixture: the Turns page photographs its filter panel open, with the four
  routes and "no route" in the picker (`turns-filters`).

## 3.568.0 - a credential goes to one place, and every surface that keeps what came back is checked for it (X-115, closes) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ MEASURED LEAK, CLOSED: the OpenCode catalog was copying model options and
  headers into Agent Farm's own store.** With a canary in
  `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, `opencode models --verbose` printed a model's
  `options` and `headers` **verbatim** from the user's config - the two places
  OpenCode documents for a model's `apiKey` and an `Authorization` header - and
  the raw listing was written straight into `globalState` and restored on every
  activation. A credential OpenCode owns, copied into a store Agent Farm owns:
  the "two vaults" failure X-100 exists to prevent. The listing is now reduced
  by an **allow-list** before anything keeps it (`publicOpenCodeCatalogText`):
  the fields the readers use, reduced to their public shapes - numbers stay
  numbers, flags stay flags, a variant keeps its name and loses its settings -
  and every other field and every stray line dropped. The reduction is
  invisible downstream (rows, providers, the model list and the free-model pick
  read identically before and after), and **a copy persisted by an earlier build
  is reduced and rewritten on the first activation**, because otherwise it lives
  on in the editor's state database until a fetch that may never come.
- **A canary key through the real Claude adapter, looked for everywhere.** It
  reaches the child's environment - the one place it belongs - and nowhere
  else: not argv, not the identity, not the names to clear, not preflight, not
  the catalog, not the launch manifest or the sentence that describes it, not
  the public profile list, not `providers.status`. The official route (no
  endpoint of its own) still clears an inherited `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and key,
  and the environment the child really gets holds neither.
- **What a process says back is scrubbed of what was put into it**
  (`core/secretScrub.ts`). A task's output file and a provider test's verdict
  are artefacts Agent Farm keeps, and a CLI that quotes its own environment in
  an error is not hypothetical. On a stream a chunk boundary can cut a key in
  half, so the scrubber holds back (longest secret - 1) characters - proven at
  every possible cut point, and with multi-byte characters split across byte
  chunks. Only values injected as secrets are scrubbed (the endpoint and the
  model are public and stay readable), and **with nothing injected - almost every
  run - the raw bytes are written exactly as before**.
- **A verdict about a route nobody holds is a statement about nothing.**
  Removing a route - from the bridge or from the page, through one function -
  now empties every test record filed under it, current and superseded. An
  edited route keeps its records on purpose; they read as superseded with the
  reason.
- **The artefact and the repository are checked by CONTENT, not only by name.**
  `npm run verify` inflates every text entry of the VSIX and refuses a
  credential-shaped string by kind; the commit hook runs the same check over the
  STAGED content of every staged text file (`tools/scan_staged.js`). One list of
  shapes (`tools/credentialShapes.js`) for both, with bodies long enough that a
  doc placeholder does not match, and a planted test value marked `CANARY` told
  apart from a real key. Neither guard ever prints the value it found.
- Tests: new `test_secret_canary.js` 54. Both new guards were proven to bite -
  a synthetic VSIX with a deflated key and a throwaway repository with one
  staged - before being trusted.

## 3.567.0 - three different questions about a provider, and only one of them costs anything (X-114, closes) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ `engines.status` answers about the ENGINE, and every fault worth catching
  lives one level down.** A Claude route with no key, a tier mapped to nothing,
  an OpenCode provider the catalog stopped offering - each of those starts and
  fails on an engine the cards at the top of the Engines page call ready, and
  nothing on this machine was looking at that level. `providers.status` is the
  free verdict: everything readable without spending a token, per route, in the
  words a launch would print.
- **The three states are not a ladder, and keeping them apart is the whole
  design.** `configured` - something declares it, which says nothing about
  whether it would run. `available` - the static verdict, with **three** values,
  because `unknown` is a real answer: with no catalog read, "no" would be a lie
  and "yes" a guess. `tested` - a real turn answered, absent until somebody
  presses for it and never true on its own. A row that is available and never
  tested is the ORDINARY state of a healthy machine; painting it amber would
  send somebody to spend a turn for nothing.
- **‼️ MEASURED, AND THE ONE THING A NAIVE CHECK GETS WRONG: an OpenCode
  provider with no credential is not unhealthy.** With a completely empty
  `auth.json` the CLI still lists and runs its own connected provider - already
  written into `engines.ts`, now honoured one level down. The absence is a
  **note**, never a problem, and the row stays available.
- **‼️ A THIRD ANSWER TO THE ROUTE QUESTION, which X-101 could not reach.**
  `clearEnv` empties the inherited process environment; a route-carrying name
  sitting in the CLI's own `settings.json` `env` block is read afterwards, from
  inside the process, and no amount of clearing touches it. Agent Farm owns the
  route and still loses to it, silently. That is now an engine-wide problem with
  the name in it - said once, not once per route - while the inherited names it
  really does clear stay a note.
- **A verdict names what it proved.** Provider + model + adapter + CLI revision
  + route revision. Edit a route's endpoint, replace its key or upgrade the CLI
  and yesterday's pass is about a configuration that no longer exists - so it is
  reported as **superseded with the reason** rather than shown as current (a
  lie) or dropped (which says "never tested" about a route tested twenty minutes
  ago).
- **`providers.test` runs one real turn THROUGH one route** - the adapter
  resolves it, its environment is injected and the inherited names that would
  answer for it a second time are cleared, so the verdict is about the route that
  was named. `engines.test` cannot do this: on Claude the route IS the
  environment and its check inherits whatever the window has. Everything the free
  check already knows to be wrong refuses it before anything is spawned, because
  spending a turn to rediscover a fault that was free to read is the one outcome
  worth preventing. Three answers, never two: answered, did not answer, and
  **nothing was called** - which is read as "not tested", never as "failed".
- **‼️ NO CREDENTIAL CROSSES EITHER OP.** A key is a boolean on the way in
  (`hasSecret`) and has no field to travel out in; the credentials file is
  **counted**, never read out; what a turn injected comes back as NAMES. The same
  boundary `providers.list` and `providers.runtime` already draw.
- **Route health on the Engines page**, under Providers: the three chips side by
  side, the problems in red under the row, the notes that are not faults in grey,
  and a **Test route** button whose own tooltip says it costs a turn. A row with
  a turn in the air cannot be pressed again, in the page and in the host.
- **Found on the way: `ProviderCatalogEntry.variants` was declared and never
  filled.** Every entry answered `[]` to "what reasoning variants does this
  provider offer" - which is not "none" but "nobody ever asked the rows". Filled
  from the rows, which is what lets a row say the one thing that matters
  downstream: a hosted card cannot carry a variant at all (ACP declares only
  model and mode, and the interactive TUI takes no `--variant` flag), so a
  headless run can pick one and a card runs the model's default.
- Tests: new `test_provider_health.js` 76 and `test_engines_route_health.js` 25;
  a scene of its own in the Engines fixture carrying every state that only exists
  after something happened, looked at in both themes.

## 3.566.0 - the ceiling a model publishes for itself becomes an answer, so the fallback table stops being Claude-only (X-113, part 4, closes) (2026-09-19)

- **‼️ Measured on this machine: seven OpenCode models, every one of them
  publishing its own window, and not one of them reaching a single table.**
  `contextWindowFor` falls back to a shipped list of Claude family regexes, so
  `opencode models --verbose` could state `limit.context` on all seven -
  200 000 on `big-pickle`, 262 144 on `ling-3.0-flash-fin-free`, **1 048 576**
  on `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` - and every Sessions row, Turns row and
  Dashboard cell still drew a bare token count with no ceiling, no percentage
  and no bar. The catalog was read, cached and persisted already; nothing had
  ever handed its limits to the rule that asks.
- **Shipping seven more regexes would have been the wrong repair.** The list
  is the engine's, it changes without us, and a model added next week would
  have gone back to zero. So the host installs what a catalog published
  (`setPublishedWindows`), in the one place the catalog lands - on restore
  from `globalState` as well as on every refresh, because a window that opens
  offline still knows the ceilings it read last time.
- **And the published figure outranks the shipped table**, for the reason the
  precedence in `contextWindowOf` already gives: a list we wrote is the
  weakest evidence in the room. It is still the MODEL answer, not the engine's
  - a live OpenCode turn reports its own operational `size` and that continues
  to win, so the value/source separation this item asks for holds end to end.
- **Both spellings of a model resolve, and an ambiguous one refuses to.** A
  launch and a live card carry the engine's wire ref (`opencode/big-pickle`);
  a transcript read off disk carries the bare id (`big-pickle`) - the same two
  spellings that had `catalogRefusal` refusing every OpenCode model there is
  in part 3. A bare id two providers publish with DIFFERENT windows is dropped
  rather than resolved to whichever was read last.
- Tests: `test_ctx_window.js` 54 (+16) - the catalog round trip, the two
  spellings, the ambiguous id, the precedence against a stated window, and the
  two call sites that install it and the reader they install from, because a
  published window nobody installs is part 3's defect under another name.

## 3.565.0 - a model that cannot do what the pick asks says so while it is being picked (X-113, part 3) (2026-09-18)

- **The catalog was told what a model cannot do and threw half of it away.**
  `opencode models --verbose` publishes `attachment`, `toolcall`, `reasoning`
  and an `input` modality map on every row; the parse kept three booleans and
  dropped the map, so "this model takes no images" was a fact the engine
  stated and Agent Farm forgot. Measured on OpenCode 1.18.19: every model this
  machine reaches states `attachment: false` and `input.image: false`.
  Absent still means absent - a field the engine never mentioned does not
  become a no.
- **And the picker line stopped being an advertisement.** It listed what a
  model CAN do (`200K context`, `free`, `reasoning`) and nothing it cannot, so
  a model that takes no attachments read exactly like one that does. It now
  says `no tools` / `no attachments` / `no images` where the engine published
  the refusal, and stays silent where it published nothing.
- **‼️ The refusal reached a surface for the first time.** The adapter has
  answered "would this pick run?" since X-99 - a model the engine stopped
  offering, a tier the route does not map, a third-party endpoint with no
  stored key - and the only caller was a bridge op. So the sentence arrived as
  an engine error in a terminal after the choosing was over. The form carries
  it (`refusals`), the launcher draws it as its own row, and the Console
  composer puts it in the route panel where the pick is made. It is a WARNING,
  not a gate: the catalog can be stale and the engine is the authority on its
  own run.
- **‼️ And wiring it found the defect that proves the point: the refusal was
  refusing every OpenCode model there is.** It matched the catalog's bare
  `id` (`big-pickle`) while a launch carries the engine's wire ref
  (`opencode/big-pickle`) - the spelling that goes to `-m`. Unread for a whole
  item family, so nothing ever noticed. Both spellings now resolve to the same
  row.
- The refusal also knows the capability axis: a model that publishes no tool
  calling is refused (a session here is tool calls from its first turn), and an
  effort asked of a model that publishes no reasoning is named. Only a
  published `false` refuses; silence refuses nothing, exactly as an unread
  catalog does.
- Tests: `test_provider_catalog.js` 40 (+9), `test_launch_provider.js` 79 (+6,
  including the two doors read out of their own source). The route panel had
  never been photographed - the scene names it now (`tip: tip-route`) and its
  label says what it is for. Looked at: `console-route`.

## 3.564.0 - the live Console card gets a ceiling for the first time (X-113, part 2) (2026-09-18)

- **Measured on a running Claude session: `ctx 234.9k`, window null.** The
  card asks the engine for its window and Claude states none, so the ONE
  surface a person watches while a turn is running drew a raw token count with
  no ceiling, no percentage and no bar — while every table on the other pages
  had known the answer since X-35. The card now resolves it through the same
  rule as everything else (`contextWindowOf`), against the APPLIED model,
  which on a card that switched mid-session is not the one it was launched
  with. A Claude card reads `ctx 92.0k / 1.0M` instead of `ctx 92.0k`.
- **And the panel says which of the three the ceiling was.** Its Window line
  claimed "the capacity this session reports" for every ceiling; that is now
  only true of one of them, so it uses the shared wording (`ctxWindowIs`) —
  your override, the engine's own statement, or the model's published window.
- Tests: `test_ctx_window.js` 38 (+5, the card's resolution and its wording).
  `test_console_page.js` moves onto `lib_charts_stub` — it was the third
  hand-written `AFCharts` found by this change, and the same U-130 drift.
  The console fixture's cards carry `contextWindowSource`, and the Claude card
  that showed a bare `ctx 92.0k` was photographing a state the host can no
  longer produce. Looked at: `console.s1` — the card strip and the status line.

## 3.563.0 - one rule for "a context reading is a fraction of WHAT", and the Turns page stops dividing every engine by 200k (X-113, part 1) (2026-09-18)

- **The Turns page measured every turn of every engine against 200 000.** A
  measured Codex thread runs against 258 400 and a million-token model against
  five times that, so the hover's percentage was wrong by a third in one
  direction and by five in the other — and read as exact in both. The cell now
  takes the fraction against the ROW'S own ceiling, resolved against the turn's
  own last model rather than the session's (a session that switched models has
  turns with different ceilings).
- **When nobody stated a window there is no percentage.** 0 is a real answer
  and the panel says so — "Window: nobody stated one — no fraction to take" —
  instead of borrowing Claude's number.
- **And the ceiling now says where it came from.** `Window is:` names it:
  your own `contextWindowTokens` setting, the engine's own statement on this
  session, or the model's published window. A percentage taken against an
  override is not the same claim as one taken against a measurement, and the
  row could not tell them apart.
- **The rule itself lived in six places, in three different orders**
  (`contextWindowOf` in `core/pricing.ts` now owns it): the dashboard put the
  override first, `extension.ts` put the live host's window first on one
  branch and the session's own on another, and the session viewer let the
  CLI's printed limit beat the override. So the same session answered
  different percentages depending on which surface was asked. Precedence:
  override → what the engine stated for this session → the model's table → 0.
- **The Console's resume list showed a bare numerator on every Claude row**,
  because it asked only the session (which Claude never answers) and never the
  model table. It now gets the same ceiling every other surface gets.
- `turns.list` on the bridge carries `ctx`, `ctxWindow` and
  `ctxWindowSource`, so an agent asking how full a turn left the window is no
  longer left to assume 200 000.
- Tests: new `test_ctx_window.js` 33 — the precedence, the model table
  (including that `opus-5` is still in it), the row's two halves, and a guard
  that the hand-written `forced > 0 ? forced :` shape does not come back.
  `test_sessions_table.js` now uses `lib_charts_stub` instead of its own
  hand-written `AFCharts` (U-130's drift, caught by this change), and
  `test_dashboard_sessions.js` stubs the ceiling with the host's real rule
  instead of `() => 0`. Looked at: `turns.s2` / `turns.s3` — the panel with a
  known ceiling and the one without.

## 3.562.0 - a mission run's total and a project's rollup say when they add more than one kind of dollar (X-112, part 3 — closes) (2026-09-18)

- **A mission run's $ is its planner's and its delegates', and they need not
  be one kind.** A lead planning on the Claude plan over OpenCode delegates
  added an API-equivalent to an engine's own figure and printed one exact
  total. The host now sends `costParts` per run (planner rounds with the
  planner session's billing, each step with its own identity), and the page
  prints `$2.14 (mixed)` with the breakdown on hover — in the runs table, the
  budget line, and the finished/stopped summaries. `partsOfTotal` makes the
  parts add up to the BOOKED total: what the rounds cannot attribute (a child
  objective, a killed planner call) is `unplaced`, and a ledger that has not
  caught up invents no negative part.
- **The $ ceiling still reads the whole total, deliberately.** A mission cap
  that skipped some kinds of dollar would be the appearance of a cap; the mark
  says what the figure is, the ceiling keeps its teeth.
- **The project rollup — the project list, the dashboard's project table and
  the project row — carries `costParts`** the same way, from the same reader
  (`billingReader`), on the measured sessions it already restricted itself to.
- **Left as they are, on purpose:** the portfolio's and the phone snapshot's
  per-agent 30-day figures (glance summaries whose rows are agents, not runs),
  and the cost-anomaly report, which compares an agent's day with its own
  history and is a trend detector, not a statement of a bill.
- Tests: `test_billing.js` 62 (+4, `partsOfTotal`), `test_projects.js` 205
  (+3). Looked at: `missions.s19` — `$2.14 (mixed)` in the runs table and on
  the budget line, `$2.14 (mixed) / $5.00`.

## 3.561.0 - a total that adds a plan's API-equivalent, a key's bill and a Kimi route's arithmetic says it is mixed (X-112, part 2b) (2026-09-18)

- **One kind of dollar per run, named by the rule.** `BillingIdentity.dollar`
  is the key a sum may not cross blindly: `equivalent` (the plan), `bill` (an
  API key), `arithmetic` (a third-party route under the Claude CLI — Kimi and
  MiniMax are the same kind), `rules` (your pricing rules),
  `reported:<engine>` (one engine's own figure — two engines' own figures are
  two vendors' claims), `unplaced`.
- **`sumDollars` — a total that says what it added.** The sum is still given
  (hiding it would be the opposite lie) but it carries its parts, and `mixed`
  is what a page marks. A zero crosses no boundary; a run with no billing is
  `unplaced`, never quietly the plan. `splitWeighed` does the same for ⚖:
  "against the limit" counts only what the plan served.
- **One reader for every total.** `runBilling` is `runIdentity`'s own rule
  (the binding test is shared, not restated) without folding a single turn,
  and `billingReader` indexes the launch record once — the dashboard, the agent
  page, the project page, the fleet report and the account spend all ask it.
- **Where it shows:** the dashboard's agent comparison (`$128 (mixed)`, the
  breakdown on hover), the agent page's all-time figure, the project page's
  Money total, and the Sessions table's selection bar. The dashboard's footnote
  no longer says every cost is an API-equivalent.
- **The fleet report stopped saying "costs are API-equivalent values"** over
  Kimi runs and a key's bill. Its header says what the costs are (or that they
  are not one kind), a mixed fleet total is broken down one line per kind, the
  agent rows are marked, and ⚖ reads "N against the plan limit · M off-plan".
- Tests: `test_billing.js` (+24 — the fold, the reader, `runBilling ===
  runIdentity(...).billing`, `charts.js dollarSum === billing.ts sumDollars`,
  and the fleet report, which had no test at all), `test_sessions_table.js`
  (+3, the selection bar), `test_project_feed.js` (+3). Looked at:
  `dashboard.s1` — `$128 (mixed)` in the comparison table, row height 27px,
  table 1352 of 1384.
- Not yet: a mission run's total (its steps can run on different engines and
  its $ budget reads that total) — X-112 part 3.

## 3.560.0 - the ⚖ figure says which window it filled, and the route decides that — not a list of names (X-112, part 2a) (2026-09-18)

- **‼️ The rule was written down twice, and the two disagreed in both
  directions.** `billingOf` decided "is this the plan" from a list of provider
  NAMES this build ships; `ProviderAdapter.billingPolicy` decided the same
  thing from the profile's `baseUrl`. A name list cannot see a user's own
  profile, so a route of your own pointed at Anthropic was called third-party
  and the shipped name `anthropic` pointed at a proxy was called the plan —
  exactly backwards. `billingOf` now reads the sealed route (`identity.route`)
  and falls back to the names only for records written before the route was
  kept. `test_billing.js` holds the two readers to one answer for every
  profile, and that guard immediately caught a second defect: `billingPolicy`
  counted an **Anthropic API key** against the plan quota. Both endpoints are
  Anthropic's, but a subscription is rationed by a window and a key is metered
  per token — fixed at the source.
- **The ⚖ figure carries its own meaning.** Every surface printed "Against the
  5h limit" over every weighted count, including runs no plan served. The
  label is now the run's own (`billing.weighed`), and the cell carries a short
  mark — `⚖ 8.7k (off-plan)` — on the routes the Claude CLI did not take to
  the plan. Sessions table (row and turn table), Live Timeline, the session
  viewer, and the Console's cards, shelf rows, turn strip and step figures.
- **Another ENGINE is deliberately left unmarked.** "off-plan" said over a
  Codex run would be a new falsehood — that run is on a ChatGPT plan, just not
  on this one's window — and it wears its own badge on the same row. The panel
  still says so in full; the cell does not shout it on every row of a machine
  running two engines.
- **A dollar figure says what it is, per run.** "API-equivalent" was written
  over all four billings. The Sessions cost panel, the Timeline money panel,
  the viewer's Cost card and the Console's spend panels now print the run's own
  `…which is:` — the bill at the API tariff, an API-equivalent a plan pays
  nothing for, Anthropic-tariff arithmetic that is not that route's bill, or
  the engine's own reported figure.
- **The Console knows which run it is drawing.** `ConsoleDeps.identityFor`
  (the same reader the viewer, Timeline and Tasks use) reaches live cards and
  shelf rows, and takes the ENGINE with the ask — so a card whose first turn
  has not landed yet is not read as Claude.
- Fixtures ask the product for their billing instead of restating it, and the
  Console gained the scene the item exists for: the routed card SELECTED.
- Tests: `test_billing.js` (+16, including the two-reader guard and the mark
  rule), `test_sessions_table.js` (+6, the marked row beside the unmarked one),
  the four page tests' chart stubs now take the mark from the real `charts.js`.
  Looked at: `sessions.s1` (dark + light), `console.s1`, `console.s11`,
  `timeline.s2`; the Tokens column measured for wrap and overflow (117px, row
  height unchanged, table 1352 of 1384).

## 3.559.0 - a run through Kimi or MiniMax fills no Claude plan window, and its dollar figure is not that route's bill (X-112, part 1) (2026-09-18)

- **The rule, stated once.** `src/core/billing.ts` — `billingOf(route, engine)`
  answers who is billed and what the figures mean: the Claude plan (⚖ on the
  sign-in's five-hour window, $ an estimate at API rates), an Anthropic API key
  ($ is the bill, no window), a third-party endpoint behind the Claude CLI —
  Kimi, MiniMax, a custom route — (⚖ NOT on the window; Claude's `total_cost_usd`
  is arithmetic at the Anthropic tariff, not that route's invoice, and no
  tariff is known, so no figure is stated), another engine (its own contract),
  or unknown. Derived from the declared route, never from a model name.
- **It travels on the identity.** `RunIdentity.billing` is filled by
  `runIdentity`, so every surface that carries a provider chip carries the
  same answer, and the chip's panel ends with `Billing: …` in the host's own
  words — Console, Sessions, Turns, viewer, Live, Tasks, Missions at once.
- **The spend-by-sign-in figures refuse the wrong tokens.** `spendByAccount`
  takes a billing reader off the same manifest the account came from: a run
  the sign-in sealed onto Kimi is still its run and is counted, but its ⚖
  tokens are not added to the plan figure and Claude's dollar figure for it
  is not added as a bill; an API-key run adds its bill and no tokens. The
  account card and the analytics table carry an `off-plan` count that says
  so rather than reading quietly small. Another engine on its own sign-in
  keeps its own weighting — that row's ⚖ is that engine's.
- Tests: `test/test_billing.js` (the rule, and that a reported model name
  alone never moves a run off the plan), `test_account_spend.js` (the off-plan
  case), `test_provider_mark.js` (the panel prints the host's line, never
  derives one), the viewer measured for the line.
- Still to come in X-112: suppressing/marking the ⚖ figure itself on off-plan
  rows, OpenCode engine-reported cost kept with its provider, a guard against
  summing figures of different currencies, and the cost tooltips naming their
  source on every page.

## 3.558.0 - the Live card, the run row and the delegation row say which provider served them (X-110, part 3 — closes) (2026-09-18)

- **The last three surfaces.** A Live Timeline card, a run on the Tasks board
  and a delegation row inside a mission all named their engine and left the
  provider to be inferred from a model name — the inference this family
  forbids. Each carries the shared chip now, beside the engine badge and
  never inside it, with the component's own panel (the declared route, who
  answered when that differs, how we know, which kind of nothing a blank is).
- **One reader, three more doors.** All three are fed by `sessionIdentityOf`,
  the reader the resume gate asks: the Live card through a `identityFor` dep
  on the timeline panel, the run row through the same dep on the tasks panel
  (read off the session the run bound to — a queued run has served nobody
  yet), the delegation through the mission payload the host already resolves
  the step's session for. A row never derives it.
- **A delegation's chip is the route that ANSWERED; its provenance panel keeps
  the route it was ASKED for.** Two facts, two marks, each with its own panel —
  never worded in one place.
- Fixtures: a Kimi-routed card and a "2 providers" card on the timeline, the
  same pair on the runs board, a Kimi-served delegation beside the ≠ mark.
  `test/test_provider_chip_width.js` measures all six surfaces now and pins
  that the three new doors ask the one reader. Dark and light photographed.
- X-110 is complete: `media/afProvider.js` is the one place a provider is
  named and coloured, and every surface that names an engine names the
  provider beside it — Console, Sessions, Turns, viewer, Live, Tasks, Missions.

## 3.557.0 - a resume card's engine pill is pinned to the card's edge, whatever its title's length (K-42, round 2) (2026-09-18)

- **The defect, measured.** On every resume card with a long title the badge
  shelf was squeezed to **0px** and the engine pill drew outside it, past the
  card's right edge — the title had `min-width:0` on its shelf's account, so
  the shelf, not the title, was the half that yielded. Round 1's guard could
  not see it: the shelf's own right edge sat inside the card while the pill it
  held did not, and no scene had ever drawn a resume card at all.
- **The shelf's floor is its content, said as a grid.** A flex shelf cannot
  state "the engine pill, plus four characters of the route": an
  `overflow:hidden` child still hands its whole text to the parent's
  min-content, so with a real minimum the route pill never yielded (measured
  51px, the name cut to "goz…"). The shelf is a grid now — the engine column
  is its content, every column after it is `minmax(4ch, max-content)` — so on
  the busiest live card the route yields first and the name stays whole, and a
  shelf with one pill has one column and sits on the card's edge.
- The Console fixture has a resume scene (three titles: one that fits, one
  that does not, a pinned one with no break in it beside the widest engine
  pill). `test/test_console_identity_width.js` measures the pill as well as
  the shelf, and that every resume card pins its pill to the SAME right edge.
- `test/measure_page.js` takes its expression from a file (`@path`), so a
  measurement is never typed through the shell's quoting.

## 3.556.0 - a session's own page says which provider served it, from the record the resume gate reads (X-110, part 2) (2026-09-18)

- **The one screen with room for the whole story of a run** drew the engine
  badge, the account and a model name, and left the provider to be inferred
  from the model — the inference this family forbids. It carries the shared
  chip now, beside the engine badge and never inside it, with the component's
  own panel: the declared route and its profile revision, who ANSWERED when
  that differs, how we know, and which kind of nothing a blank is.
- **One reader, so a page and a gate cannot describe one run two ways.** The
  `runIdentity` join lived inline inside `resumeRouteFor` and nothing else
  could ask for it; it is `sessionIdentityOf` now and the gate reads it too.
  Without that, a page could say "Kimi" over a session the gate then refuses
  to resume onto Kimi — two true-looking answers about one run.
- `test/test_provider_chip_width.js` measures the viewer's chip as well, and
  pins that both sides ask the same reader.
- Still to come in X-110: the Live timeline, and task and mission rows.

## 3.555.0 - which PROVIDER served a run is a mark of its own, and the last door with no launch record has one (X-110 part 1 · X-327) (2026-09-18)

### X-110 (part 1) — the provider is a mark of its own

- **The defect.** An engine is the program on this machine; a provider is the
  endpoint that answered it, and they are two axes. Only one surface drew the
  second one at all — the Console, with a route pill it had invented for
  itself, in its own grey, on one page. Everywhere else the provider was buried
  in a hover line or left to be guessed from a model name, which is the one
  inference this family forbids: `claude-opus-5` served by Anthropic and by a
  gateway read identically.
- **`media/afProvider.js` — the mark, said once (the afEngine.js rule, one axis
  across).** A provider chip is DASHED where an engine badge is SOLID, so the
  colour can answer "which of the four" without a provider ever reading as a
  sixth engine. The four shipped Claude routes are named and coloured; anything
  else — an OpenCode native provider, a route added later — lands in one of
  five derived slots by a hash of its own id, so it is the same colour on every
  page rather than a colour that depends on where it sat in a list. Never red:
  this extension signals a fault in red, and a provider that hashed onto it
  would read as a broken route (U-49's lesson, one palette across).
- **A run that changed provider between turns is COUNTED, never named.** Saying
  "Kimi" over a run that was half Anthropic is the specific lie the component
  exists to stop; the chip says `2 providers` and the panel names them in the
  order they served.
- **Four surfaces.** The Console card's own pill is the shared chip now, and it
  is coloured by the COMPANY the profile routes to rather than by the profile,
  so two profiles on Kimi are one colour in a table and not two (new
  `ConsoleRoute.shape`, answered off the profile and never guessed from a
  name). The Sessions table draws it beside the engine badge — `Engine · Route`
  — so a machine with four routes can be SCANNED rather than hovered. The Turns
  page draws the provider the engine named for THAT turn, which is the one
  place a multi-provider run becomes legible, and the Export-MD line says
  `via <provider>` beside the model.
- The three-way "why is there nothing to show" wording (`legacy` · `external` ·
  `unknown`) had been written in two files free to disagree; it is the
  component's now, and the sessions table reads it from there.
- Guards: `test/test_provider_mark.js` (the component and the palette — no two
  shipped routes share a hue, nothing a provider can wear is the fault colour,
  a legacy run borrows no route) and `test/test_provider_chip_width.js`, which
  MEASURES the laid-out chip on both tables. That one exists because the first
  draft drew `···` where `opencode` should have been: Turns declared its Engine
  column at what a single badge needs, and every string test in the repo passed
  on it.
- Still to come in X-110: the session viewer, the Live timeline, and task and
  mission rows.

### X-327 — a task hosted in the Console has a launch record too

- **The last door with no record, named in 3.554.0 and closed here.** The
  runner skips the Console shape on purpose — "that branch hands the spawn to
  the panel, and the Console door writes its own manifest" — and for four
  releases that sentence described an intention nobody had implemented.
  `consoleTaskStart` recorded nothing, so a task with
  `interactiveTarget: console` had NO launch manifest at all and
  `sessions.resumeRoute` read its conversation back as unknown.
- **Written at the Console door, because that is where the account is a slot.**
  A task may name a rule (`@round-robin`); the door resolves it at the pick,
  and a record written on the runner's side would have named the RULE against
  a run that went to exactly one sign-in. The runner passes what set the run
  going (`launchMechanismOf`) and takes the `launchId` back, so a Console-hosted
  task carries the same link to its record every other shape carries — and a
  run a schedule started still reads as `schedule`, not as "a person opened a
  card".
- The options travel by the SHAPE (`runExtras` → `launchDimsOf`), not by a
  hand-written field list, so a dimension added to `RunDimensions` reaches this
  record without anybody remembering it here.
- Guards in `test/test_launch_manifest.js`: the mechanism travelling in and the
  id coming back, the record written after the sign-in is resolved and before
  the process is asked for, and the record naming what set the run going.

## 3.554.0 - a card started from the composer or the bridge has a launch record, so a resume can pin its route (X-109 R2) (2026-09-18)

- **Measured live, after X-109 shipped.** `sessions.resumeRoute` on two cards
  started from the Console composer today answered `binding: legacy`,
  `act: unbound` — "started before launches were recorded". They were not:
  only `startConsoleSession` (launcher, tree, profiles) wrote a launch
  manifest. The composer's own Send — the door people use most — and the
  bridge's fresh `console.start` started the card with no record, so the
  X-109 gate could never pin those conversations to the route they ran on.
- **`recordConsoleCard` — one helper, the same resolution and record as
  `startConsoleSession`** (`resolveLaunchRoute` → `recordLaunch`, mechanism
  `session`, surface `console`). The composer's Send writes it (new panel dep
  `recordConsoleLaunch`) on the SLOT that really runs — after the X-305 R2
  pick — and starts the card with its `launchId`; the bridge writes it for a
  fresh card and not for a resume, which keeps the manifest its conversation
  was started with.
- Still without a record: a task hosted in the Console (`consoleTaskStart`) —
  the runner skips the console shape so one run does not get two records, and
  nothing writes the one it should have. Left open, named in the project log.
- Guards in `test/test_launch_manifest.js`: the helper's shape, the bridge
  writing before `consoleHost.start` and only for a fresh card, the composer
  writing on the picked slot and handing the id to the card.

## 3.553.0 - Console session cards are fixed lines, and nothing jumps as a session grows (K-42) (2026-09-18)

- **The defect.** A live card's header held the name, the engine, the route,
  the token figure and the 🔖 in one wrapping line: while the figure was small
  the badges fitted beside the name, and the moment it grew the whole shelf
  fell to a second line — cards changed height mid-session and their badges
  sat top-right on one card and a line lower on the next. The sign-in pill
  was squeezed into the status line with the phase, held count, turns and
  context, and wrapped there. Resume cards put the engine pill after a long
  title on a wrapping line, so it landed bottom-LEFT on most of them.
- **A live card is four fixed lines.** (1) who + engine/route, `nowrap`, the
  name is the half that ellipsizes and the engine pill is pinned to the end;
  on a crowded line the ROUTE pill gives way first (its panel opens with the
  whole value — MIRROR) and the engine pill never does. (2) new `.h2`: the
  sign-in on the left, the token figure and the 🔖 on the right, always
  drawn, so the card's height does not depend on how far it has run.
  (3) the title. (4) the status line — phase, wait, held, turns, context,
  project — without the sign-in.
- **A resume card's engine pill is pinned to the end of its title line**
  (inside the same `.hb` group), so every card in the list wears it in the
  same corner.
- `test_console_identity_width.js` now pins the new shape (header `nowrap`,
  the `.h2` line, the sign-in off the status line, the resume pill in `.hb`)
  and MEASURES it: every one of the 68 headers in the fixture is one line
  with its badge group on that line and inside its card, and every card still
  shows its whole agent name and id.
- **`shoot_page.js` refuses a render older than the page's own media**, not
  only older than its fixture: a script or stylesheet edited after the render
  was photographed as the page before the change (measured on this item).

## 3.552.0 - a rule picked in a Console box is resolved on the spot, and never starts a session above 90% (X-305 R2) (2026-09-18)

- **‼️ The live failure.** A person opened a fresh Console card, picked
  `@round-robin` in the composer's account box and pressed Send: the card
  started on the agent's STANDING sign-in, which stood at 100%, and its first
  turn hit the limit. Picking `@round-robin` again in the live card's box
  moved it to a sign-in at 91% — under the 95% wall — and that turn hit the
  limit too, while a third sign-in sat at 21%. Every smart rule
  (`@emptiest`, `@round-robin`, `@standing`, `@pool`, `@<name>`) was
  affected, not only round-robin.
- **Root cause 1 — the composer pruned every rule.** `prunedAccount` checked
  the box's value against the engine's SLOT list only, so a rule came back as
  "nothing picked" and `accountShown` fell through to the standing slot. The
  box offered the rules (X-305) and then silently threw the choice away. A
  rule is now kept when this engine offers it (`policiesFor`), and the
  last-launch seed keeps it too.
- **Root cause 2 — the live box kept the RULE on the card.** `setAccount`
  stored `@round-robin` itself as `accountNext`; the rule was then resolved
  by the spawn seam at every re-spawn, so one conversation could be walked
  between plans, and the card could not say which sign-in it had landed on.
- **One resolver, at the moment of choice.** `ConsoleHost` takes an
  `accountPick` hook (the extension's `launchAccountPick`, the same resolver
  every other door uses) and exposes `pickAccount`: a slot or `@machine`
  passes untouched; a rule becomes ONE slot against the figures of this
  moment and commits the round-robin cursor once; a rule answering "the main
  sign-in" is stated as `@machine`; a rule that can choose nothing is a
  refusal with its reason and nothing starts. The composer resolves before
  `host.start` (a refusal is a warning, like an absent engine); the live box
  and `console.setAccount` resolve inside `setAccount`, after every other
  refusal, so a move that cannot happen never advances the rotation. The card
  keeps the SLOT and says `next message runs on <slot> (<the rule's own
  sentence>)`. The composer still REMEMBERS the rule, so the next session of
  that agent opens on the rule, not on last time's slot.
- **‼️ The default wall is 90, not 95.** 90% of the five-hour window is where
  the fleet's own agents hand over; a session started above it spends its
  first turn on a handover note or dies mid-turn. `POLICY_DEFAULT_CEILING`
  and the Engines page's fallback say 90; a rule, a step or a pool that names
  its own number keeps it. The sentry's own ceiling is unchanged.
- **`console.setAccount` knows the user's own rules** (`accountPolicies()` is
  passed to `accountRefusal`), so `@gelistirme` is no longer refused as a
  typo; its contract now says a rule is resolved into one slot on the call.
- 19 tests in `test/test_console_account.js` against the real host (a rule
  becomes one slot, commits once, `@machine` for the main sign-in, refusal
  with no slot, no resolver = refusal, the live box keeps the slot and says
  why, an impossible move does not advance the cursor, the re-spawn really
  lands on the chosen slot's directory) plus source guards on the composer,
  the constructor wiring and the bridge. `test_wiring` counts the new
  constructor argument.

## 3.551.0 - a resumed session runs on the route it ran on, and every door asks the same gate (X-109) (2026-09-18)

- **‼️ The corruption, and which door it came through.** X-101 gave every
  adapter a `resumePolicy`; X-105 refused a route change on a live card. For
  six releases NOTHING called either on a resume: the Console, the terminal,
  the bridge and a task continuing a conversation all resolved the route the
  way a fresh launch does — what was named, else the agent's STANDING route.
  A session that ran on Kimi came back on whatever the agent stood on that
  day, and no transcript could say which turns ran where (measured in August,
  the reason X-105 exists; it had only closed the live-card door).
- **`resumeRoute(adapter, binding, prior, asked, standing)` — one pure gate
  (`src/core/resumeGate.ts`).** The route a session ran on is read off its
  LAUNCH MANIFEST through the binding and re-resolved at the spawn (the
  profile at its CURRENT revision, the key from the store — nothing is copied
  out of the record). Five answers: **`pinned`** (nothing asked → the route it
  ran on, the standing route never consulted — and "ran with none" is pinned
  to NONE, which every resolver used to read as "ask the agent"), **`switch`**
  (a different route asked and the ENGINE allows it — recorded as a new run
  identity beside the earlier turns' one), **`unbound`** (nothing recorded —
  `legacy` / `external` / `unknown` binding, the same four words as
  `runIdentity` — so what was asked, else the standing route, applies and
  `why` says so), **`none`** (no provider axis), **`refuse`** with `remedy`
  (fork | new). The verdict is `adapter.resumePolicy`'s, never this file's.
- **‼️ On OpenCode the model carries the provider, and a bare id is resolved,
  never guessed.** `qualifyModelRef` reads the engine's own catalog: one
  provider serving `claude-opus-5` qualifies it, two serving `big-pickle`
  REFUSE it by name with the qualified form to use. A model naming one
  provider beside a `providerId` naming another is refused too.
- **`pinned` is a new word the resolver understands.** `resolveLaunchRoute`,
  `engineRuntimeFor`, the terminal, the ConsoleHost (`routePinned` on the init
  AND the state, so every re-spawn and the account swap stay pinned), the
  revive and the task runner (`FarmTask.routePinned`, `spawnRouteOf`) all take
  a pinned route AS IT IS, an empty providerId included. `LaunchOptions.
  routePinned` is per-launch like `resume` itself — never remembered.
- **Seven doors, one function (`resumeRouteFor`).** `console.start` (its
  `providerId=` is a DELIBERATE ask and is policed; the reply carries
  `resumeRoute`), the row's "Continue in Console", the ended card's own
  Resume (it passed NO route at all — the card said Kimi, the process talked
  to the setting), the row's terminal Resume (now handed the engine and the
  route; before, the environment was resolved for Claude off the standing
  record), `startClaudeSession` for `--resume` and `--continue` (the latter
  gated against the latest session in the folder), `sessions.start` (gated
  with its own argument, arrives `routePinned`), and a task with
  `resumeSessionId` (a refusal is a finished run with the reason; the
  verdict is a `route` event on its record). A seeded box is not an ask —
  S-45's rule applied to the route — so UI doors ask nothing and pin.
- **`sessions.resumeRoute`** — the gate, readable without spawning: the same
  function the doors use, so what it says is what they will do.
- **Out of scope, said here so it is not mistaken for done:** the mission
  planner's `--resume` runs on the spec's own route by construction (one
  route per run) and is not gated; a Console-shaped task never resumes.
- **75 tests** (`test_resume_gate.js`): the five acts per engine, the
  revision move, the bare-id ambiguity, and the WIRE — every
  `consoleHost.start` that resumes is walked by balanced braces and must
  carry `routePinned`, so a door added later is caught by shape.

## 3.550.0 - a smart account rule is a rule, not a deleted sign-in: no more "not on this machine: @emptiest" (K-41) (2026-09-18)

- **‼️ The false alarm, and where it came from.** Picking a smart policy
  (`@emptiest`, `@round-robin`, `@pool`, or a rule you named) in the Console's
  account box put that id on the card as its stated account.
  `statedAccountLabel` looked for it among the stored SLOTS, found nothing —
  because a rule is not a slot and never will be — and answered through the
  X-282 branch with `⚠ not on this machine: @emptiest`. A deleted-account
  warning, drawn over a session running perfectly on a rule the user had just
  chosen. Measured on a live card: `e45a1888`.
- **A policy reads as itself.** `statedAccountLabel` asks `isPolicyId` before it
  asks the slot list, so every surface that names a stated account — the card
  badge, the tree, the task and schedule rows, the Sessions tables — shows
  `@emptiest`. There is one producer of the missing-account mark, so one fix
  covers every one of them.
- **A rule that names nothing is still not accused here.** This function has no
  rule list, and inventing one would be the second half of the same mistake. A
  typo is refused at the door it was typed into (`policyRefusal`), which is
  where it can still be fixed.
- **‼️ And the panel no longer calls a rule a sign-in.** `Running as: @emptiest`
  would be false — the rule is what CHOSE the sign-in, and it chose when the
  process started. The card now reads `Picked by rule: @emptiest`, and a pending
  swap to a rule says `Next message picks by rule:`. The page never tests the
  `@` itself: the host answers which kind it is (`accountIsPolicy`), because the
  rule living in two places is the first half of this very bug.
- **The badge had no test at all** — that is how this shipped. It has one now,
  in every state: a sign-in, a rule, a pending swap to a rule, and a scene of
  its own (`console-card-policy`), shot dark and light.
- **‼️ Trap fixed on sight: `shoot_page.js` refuses a stale render.** It shoots
  whatever `dist/render/<name>.html` already holds, so a fixture edited without
  a re-render answers with the page as it was — and with `--scene N`, adding a
  scene shifts every number after it, so the stale file hands back a DIFFERENT
  scene under the right number. Found here: `--light` had never been
  re-rendered and photographed its neighbour (29 scenes against the dark 30).
  The fixture's mtime is now the test, and the refusal names the exact command
  including `--light`, because the two themes are two files.

## 3.549.0 - a session row says which run really produced it — and when it cannot, which kind of nothing that is (X-108) (2026-09-18)

- **‼️ `null` was three different facts sharing one blank space.** A session row
  with no launch manifest showed no setup lines at all, and that silence covered
  our own run from before the manifest existed, somebody else's transcript, and
  a route asked for with no answer. They are not the same thing and only one of
  them is worth looking at.
- **`runIdentity(manifest, engine, turns, {external})`** — the whole run on one
  object, for a row that cannot carry fifty turns: `providerId`,
  `providerLabel`, `origin`, `scope`, `providerProfileId`,
  `providerProfileRevision`, `requestedModelRef`, `reportedProviderIds`,
  `reportedModels`, `proof`, `multiProvider`, `turnScope`, `agreement` — and
  **`binding`**, which is the field to read first: `declared` · `legacy` (ours,
  older than the manifest — backfillable from evidence later, X-116) ·
  `external` (never ours; there was nothing to record) · `unknown` (asked, and
  nothing answered).
- **‼️ And NO VALUE IS INVENTED to go with it.** On the last three the route,
  the requested model and the account stay empty. Naming an absence is the
  opposite of filling it in, and filling it in from the model name is the one
  move this whole family exists to refuse.
- **An external run's origin is `external`, not `legacy-inherit`.** "Nobody was
  asked" is a statement about *our* records and is simply untrue of a run Agent
  Farm never started — it would also make the row look backfillable when there
  is nothing anywhere to backfill it from.
- **The reported half stands on its own.** An engine that named its provider has
  PROVED one even when nothing was declared (`proof: 'engine-reported'`), so the
  Sessions hover shows `Answered by: opencode` on a run with no manifest at all.
  The proof line appears only where the engine contributed evidence — "we wrote
  it down" is already what the Route line being there means.
- **All three Sessions tables** (Dashboard, agent page, Sessions page) read the
  one shared `sessionRowPool`, so the fact lands on every one of them, and the
  Engine column's `<th>` explains the states once rather than in each cell.
- **`launch.runtime` returns `identity` too**, with a describe that tells the
  caller to read `binding` first — an agent asking "what ran this" no longer has
  to fold the turn list itself.

## 3.548.0 - the provider the engine named reaches the turn index, so a multi-provider run can be told from a conflict (X-108, part 1) (2026-09-18)

- **‼️ The drop, named.** OpenCode's export states the pair — `info.model =
  { id: "big-pickle", providerID: "opencode" }` on a session, `providerID`
  beside `modelID` on every message — and only the model half was ever read. So
  the index recorded no provider at all, every later reader had to complete
  `big-pickle` back to `opencode/big-pickle` by guessing against the engine's
  published list (K-28), and a model two providers both offer could not be
  completed at all.
- **`SessionTurn.providerIds`** — the reported PROVIDER, beside `models`, which
  is the reported model. Per turn because on OpenCode the provider legitimately
  changes at a turn boundary (`session/set_config_option`), so a session-level
  answer is false the moment anybody uses that feature. **Empty on Claude for
  ever** (measured 23 Aug 2026), which is an absence and never a default.
- **‼️ And the join was structurally unable to fire.** `turnRuntimes` was called
  with `{ n, models }` at both of its call sites, so `providerConflict` and the
  multi-provider check — which read `reportedProviderIds` — could never see one
  on the only engine that publishes them. Both call sites now pass both halves,
  and the pin that certified the old shape says so.
- **‼️ `multiProvider` with `turnScope` is the feature working, not an
  incident.** `RunDrift` gains both. Several providers across a turn-scoped run
  is a legitimate multi-provider timeline and the line describes it
  (`2 providers across 4 turns — a turn-scoped run may change provider`); the
  same two inside a **session**-scoped run is the thing to go and look at. Read
  off the SCOPE, never the engine's name, so a sixth engine needs nothing added.
- **The Turns page and `turns.list` carry it** — `TurnRow.providerIds`, and the
  op returns it on every row.
- **The provider-guess guard got sharper rather than relaxed.** Reading
  `model.providerID` is the opposite of deriving a provider from a model name,
  but it reads alike on one line. The guard now STRIPS the published read and
  puts whatever is left in front of both expressions — so
  `providerId: model.providerID ? '' : model.id.split('/')[0]` is still caught,
  and four planted lines hold the narrowing honest.
- **B-25 follow-through:** `turns.list` read its `limit` with
  `typeof args.limit === 'number'`, the same silence in a different spelling —
  the CLI's `limit=50` arrives as text and was dropped for the default. It reads
  `optNum` now.

## 3.547.0 - a number sent to the bridge counts as a number: `at=1` really does put the item first (B-25) (2026-09-18)

- **‼️ The trap, named.** `optStr` answers `''` for anything that is not a
  string, so `Number(optStr(args, 'at'))` was `0` for every number a caller
  sent — and `0` means "no position asked for". Four items opened with
  `at:1…4` on 2026-09-17 all landed at the BOTTOM of the queue under an
  `ok: true` response, and had to be moved by hand. Nothing errored; there was
  nothing to read.
- **Numbers are read with `optNum`, which takes either form.** A JSON request
  carries `1`, the CLI's `at=1` shorthand coerces to `1`, a hand-written arg is
  `"1"` — all three now count. Five sites carried the broken shape:
  `projects.backlog.add`'s `at`, `studio.assets`' and `toolbox.servers`' `limit`,
  and `studio.render`'s `fps` / `clipSeconds`.
- **‼️ And the shape is banned from the source, so it cannot come back.**
  `test_bridge.js` scans every `src/**/*.ts` line (comments excluded — they are
  prose about the trap) for `Number|parseInt|parseFloat(optStr|argStr(` and
  fails by file and line number. It reports 5 hits against the previous commit.
- **An `at` that cannot be honoured is said out loud.** `at: "top"` no longer
  disappears: the response's `note` reads `at="top" is not a queue position
  (1 is the top), so the item queued where a new one normally would`. Silence is
  what let the original bug live.
- **The stand-in that certified the bug reads the arg the way the op does.**
  The dispatch test's mirror handler read `a.at` straight, so it was green on a
  number the shipped op threw away. It goes through the real `optNum` now, and
  the number form, the text form and the unusable form each have a test.

## 3.546.0 - the Console account box is live: 5h and weekly figures apart, refreshed in place, never under an open menu (X-326) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ Option A — the two windows, named.** An account row reads
  `name · 5h: 12% / wk: 40%` (one of them alone when only one is reported,
  `—` when nothing has been read), so a weekly 40% and a five-hour 12% are never
  the same bare number in one list. `SlotUsage` carries `fivePercent` /
  `weekPercent` (+ their resets) beside the binding bar it already had.
- **‼️ The figures are refreshed in place.** The host pushes `accounts` to an
  open Console on every fresh reading (`accountUsage.onRead`), on hover of an
  account box (mouseenter, no delay), when a card is opened or `+` pressed, and
  every 30 seconds; the page refills `#c-account` / `#c-account-live` where they
  stand and re-syncs their hover panels — no full repaint, no lost focus.
  **A box that is the active element is left alone**: replacing the options of
  an open list closes it and moves the choice.
- **One account list, wherever it is drawn.** The composer's box, a live card's
  box and the refresh all build through `accountAxisSpec` (root row first,
  slots as the component draws them, rules in their own group) and fill through
  `axisBoxBody` — the same option body the shell draws, so a refresh cannot
  differ from a render. Page message `getAccounts` is on the parity manifest
  (`accounts.list`).

## 3.545.0 - a saved setup starts its own agent, whatever row the Agents tree has selected (S-65) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ The profile's own agent is absolute.** `Start Session…` (the panel
  icon) opens on the saved setups, and a setup saved for `developer` could
  start `psikolog`: the Agents tree keeps its last clicked row selected, VS Code
  hands that row to the command as its argument, and `known ?? profile` let it
  outrank the profile — with no way to deselect a tree row, the trap was
  permanent. A profile that names an agent now starts THAT agent (present, or
  gone and asked for once, as before); the caller's agent is the answer only for
  a setup that names nobody (S-48 — a row's own menu pressing a legacy profile
  still starts that row), and with neither it asks. The decision is one pure
  function (`pressedSetupStarts`), run in `test_launch_profiles`.
- **The saved-setup list always says who each row starts** — it used to hide
  the agent whenever one was "known", which was hiding the one fact that
  decided what happened.

## 3.544.0 - continue from handover, one click from the card that stopped; the note is seen the moment it is written (S-64, closes) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ "Continue from handover" on the Console card.** A card that was told
  CONTEXT HANDOVER, or whose handover note has been found, now carries the law's
  next step beside "Open transcript": the button opens the composer on that
  agent with the card's whole setup — engine, model, effort, permission mode,
  superpowers, route, sign-in, project — and the host's first message already in
  the box (the note's path, the reading that fired, and the protocol the fresh
  run is bound to). It does not press Send: a run that stopped on its five-hour
  window is the one whose account you change first. The conversation on the
  card is never resumed. MIRROR: the tooltip opens with the state the card is
  in. Drawn on no quiet card — a card at CONVERGE is still working.
- **‼️ The note is seen at the write, not at the next search.** The guard used
  to learn "handed over" only when the sentry listed the answer folders after a
  round; a Console session that handed over by hand sat on the card as "not
  yet". The live hook already sees every Write and Edit, so the write of a file
  under the canonical name, by the session the eight characters in it belong
  to, marks the record on the spot (`handoverNoteWrittenBy`) — a note written
  for another session is that session's fact and is ignored.
- **The same door for an agent: `console.continueFromHandover id=<console id>`**
  — `open=true` is the button's path (composer only); the default starts the
  fresh session at once through `console.start`, with every refusal that door
  has. A quiet card is refused by name. `handoverContinueFor` in the host runs
  the one search the sentry uses (`findHandover`) on the click, never on a
  render, and writes the paragraph (`handoverContinuePrompt`).
- S-64 closes: signal (1) · words on the surfaces (2) · retry's smart continue
  (3) · rounds, lanes and the lead (4) · the fresh run itself (5).

## 3.543.0 - a handed-over conversation is not resumed by a task's next round, a mission lane, or the lead (S-64, 4/n) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ A round is never sent into a conversation that was handed over.** A
  round is a reply, so it resumes the conversation that was answered — except
  the one the context guard told to hand over (or a note closed): the law sends
  the next run into a FRESH session. The round still runs; it starts fresh, and
  its prompt says why (the session, the reading that fired), where the work now
  lives (the handover note, or `af.js sessions.read id=<sid>` when none has been
  found) and then carries the round's own instruction whole. Both places a round
  resumes are covered: `openNextRound` for a run already bound, and
  `releaseRounds` for a held round whose conversation binds afterwards. The
  record says it: "round N starts a fresh session — <sid> was told to hand over
  at 41% …".
- **‼️ A mission lane whose last session was handed over is a `handoff`,
  whatever the engine could do.** The message records `handedOver {pct, note}`,
  the speaker is told its last session was handed over (with the reading and the
  note to read), and the lead's round line reads `Ada(done,handoff after
  handover at 43%)` — so a re-told lane is not mistaken for an engine that
  cannot resume.
- **‼️ The lead's own planning conversation is not resumed past the line.** The
  planner has no write tools, so it cannot write the note the sentence asks
  for; its note is the ledger. A handed-over lead session is dropped and the
  next call is seeded the way the resume-fallback seeds one — briefing, ledger,
  guidance, the round that just came back — under a "Why this is a fresh
  session" heading, and the ledger records the handover.
- One answer for all of them: `handoverEvidenceOf` in the host (the guard's
  record — told HANDOVER, or closed by a note), read by the retry, the rounds
  and the missions alike.

## 3.542.0 - the bridge guard is seen, not trusted, and says which engines it holds on (B-23, closes) (2026-09-17)

- **The card shows what the guard stopped.** A Console session whose search for
  a session id was refused carries `guard N` on its status strip, beside the
  window figure; its AFTip opens with the long form ("Bridge guard — N searches
  for a session id stopped"), lists the newest five as `when: tool · id`, says
  how many it left out, and names the call that answers and the way out. Nothing
  is drawn while there were none — on a guarded engine that silence is the
  honest answer, and a `0` on every card would be noise. The words are the
  host's (`bridgeGuardView`), never re-derived on the page.
- **‼️ The refusals survive a reload.** They lived in memory, so a window reload
  set the count back to zero and the card would have said "held" about a run
  that was stopped an hour earlier. `core/bridgeGuardLog.ts` keeps them in
  `bridge-guard.json` (capped at 500, oldest dropped, a torn file read as empty).
- **‼️ Which engines the rule is held on, per engine.** A guard that silently
  covers two engines out of five reads as covering all of them.
  `bridgeGuardCoverage` answers for each: **Claude** — its PreToolUse hook;
  **Codex** — the PreToolUse hook in the `hooks.json` the fleet writes. Codex is
  there on measurement, not analogy: codex-cli 0.149.0 parses
  `permissionDecision` on PreToolUse, refuses only `ask` and `allow`, prints
  "Command blocked by PreToolUse hook: <reason>", and names its shell tool
  `Bash` — the name the guard already reads — so the same listener answer
  already stops it, while that wire is installed and trusted. **Gemini,
  Antigravity, OpenCode** — no hook Agent Farm wires; each says so, with the
  reason, and that there the rule is only written.
- An argv-shaped command (`["rg", "-l", <id>]`) is read as the command it is.
- **`sessions.bridgeGuard`** now returns `engines` (the coverage above) and takes
  `session=<id>` for one session's refusals; the setting's description names the
  engines it holds on.
- Console fixture: two scenes (one refusal, seven refusals), drawn and looked at
  in both themes.

## 3.541.0 - a session id is not hunted for on disk: the bridge rule is held by the hook (B-23, 1/n) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ MEASURED: a written rule with nothing watching it is not a rule.** Agent
  Farm data — sessions, transcripts, turns, tasks, missions, projects — is asked
  of the bridge first. On 2026-09-17 two runs went hunting for a session id
  through the file system and guessing the engine's layout, one of them for over
  ten minutes, while `af.js sessions.find q=<id>` answers in one call.
- **`core/bridgeGuard.ts`** refuses that call at the hook. A `PreToolUse` on a
  SEARCH tool (Grep, Glob, or a shell `find`/`grep`/`rg`/`ls`/`dir`/
  `Get-ChildItem`/`Select-String`) carrying a full session id — or a short id
  this machine knows — is answered with the CLI's deny shape, and the agent
  reads one line instead: what the string is, that the layout belongs to the
  engine and changes, `sessions.find q=<id>` for the file and `sessions.read
  id=<id>` for the conversation, and the way out.
- **‼️ NARROW ON PURPOSE, because this sits in front of every tool call every
  agent here makes.** An Edit, a Write, a Read of a named path is never touched;
  a shell command is only a search when its VERB is one; a call already using
  the bridge is never refused; and the SHORT form is refused only when the index
  knows it — an 8-character hex string is also every abbreviated git hash there
  is, and `git log <sha>` must not be collateral. `af:allow-id` anywhere in the
  command always runs, because a legitimate file operation on a transcript
  exists and a refusal with no escape teaches an agent to fight the guard.
- **The channel is the same listener, in a second shape.** `contextSignal`
  (S-64) ADDS to the model's context; this STOPS the call, and it outranks the
  signal on `PreToolUse` — a call that is not going to run has no next step to
  be told anything before. A guard that throws still leaves the hook intact.
- **`agentFarm.bridgeGuard`** (default on) switches it off; `sessions.bridgeGuard`
  reports the setting, the escape token, how many ids are known and every
  refusal it has made, so the rule's own health is read rather than trusted.

## 3.540.0 - a conversation that was told to stop is never the one a retry resumes (S-64, 3/n) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ MEASURED: smart continue would have resumed the one run it must not.**
  `behavior: "smart"` resumes an interrupted run's own conversation rather than
  repeating its prompt — right for work that was cut off, and wrong for exactly
  one run: the one whose context window had reached the handover line. The law
  is explicit ("the next run is always a fresh session that starts from the
  note, never a resume of the saturated one"), and resuming it puts the new turn
  into a window that was already full — walking straight back into the wall the
  retry was sent to escape.
- **`retryDecision` takes the guard's evidence** (`handover: {told, pct, note}`)
  and refuses the continuation on it: the retry still happens, with the original
  prompt, and the row says which rule stopped the continuation and at what
  reading. `simple` policies are untouched — they never continued anything.
  The `unknown` branch is deliberately unchanged: knowing the window was full
  says nothing about whether the work landed.
- **The loop closes where the note is found.** The handover search that serves
  both the sentry and the bridge now records its hit against the session it
  closed (`markHandedOver`), so "handed over" is a measured fact on every
  surface — and the retry above has something to read. A handover on the OTHER
  trigger (the 5-hour quota) is recorded too, on a session that crossed no line
  here: the fact kept is that the conversation is closed and its work continues
  elsewhere, which is true however it ended.
- **The sentry diagnosis gains a third wall.** A run told to hand over that
  wrote no note is `wall-context` — a discipline failure with a name — instead
  of `wall-unfinished`, "the session ended on its own", which it did not. And a
  crossing on an engine whose hooks carry no channel is `wall-context-blind`:
  the run was never asked, so the missing note is the wiring and not the agent.
  `CONVERGE` is not a wall; a note still beats both.
- **`sentry.prompt`** accepts `context: {level, pct, delivered}` — the law's
  second trigger beside `quotaPercent`'s first, straight out of
  `sessions.contextGuard`.

## 3.539.0 - the card says whether the run was TOLD, and whether the sentence ever reached it (S-64, 2/n) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ MEASURED GAP: the signal went out and nothing on screen said so.** A
  card drew `ctx 410.0k / 1.0M · 41%` and stopped there, which reads as a run
  that was told to hand over and carried on working. On an engine whose hooks
  carry no `additionalContext` that reading is a charge against an agent
  nobody ever spoke to: the guard had recorded `undelivered` since 3.538.0 and
  no surface drew it.
- **`contextSignalView` (`core/contextGuard.ts`) is the words, derived ONCE.**
  Three states — `quiet` (no line crossed: nothing is drawn, because silence is
  the honest answer there), `delivered`, and `undelivered` — each with a chip
  for a dense strip and one fact per line for the panel: which word went out at
  what percent, through which hook, whether the earlier converge had gone out
  before it, whether a handover note has closed the loop, and the two lines in
  force. The host builds it and every surface renders it, so two pages cannot
  word the same state differently.
- **The Console status strip** carries the chip beside the window figure —
  `ctx 410.0k / 1.0M · 41% · HANDOVER` — in the warning colour at the converge
  line, the error colour at the handover line, and `HANDOVER ✕` when the
  crossing never reached the run. SHORTHAND: the chip drops the word `CONTEXT`
  that the `ctx` figure already says, and the AFTip opens with the law's full
  wording. An order that was obeyed (`✓ handed over`) stops shouting — the loud
  colours are kept for the states somebody may still have to act on.
- **A session's own page** says the same thing under its "Context now" gauge,
  from the same view (`ViewerDeps.contextSignalFor`), so a finished run can be
  read after the fact: told, or never reachable.
- **`sessions.contextGuard id=<sid>`** now answers `view` alongside the record,
  so an agent asking the bridge reads exactly what a human watching the run
  reads.
- **First fixture for the session viewer** (`test/fixtures/sessionviewer.js`,
  4 scenes) — the page had never been photographed. Console gains three scenes
  for the three signal states, because the whole point of the states is that
  they must not look like each other.

## 3.538.0 - a running agent is told when its window reaches the converge and the handover line (S-64, 1/n) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ MEASURED: the handover law binds a run to the context window at 35%
  (start nothing new) and 40% (stop and hand over), and an agent cannot see
  its own fill** — the quota it can probe, the window it cannot. A rule with
  no feedback is not a rule; on an unlimited plan it would be the only brake.
- **`core/contextGuard.ts`** decides WHEN to say the law's two words, ONCE per
  line per window: `CONTEXT CONVERGE <pct>% — …` at the converge line,
  `CONTEXT HANDOVER <pct>% — …` at the handover line (the higher wins and
  contains the lower). A window that empties again (compaction) re-arms both.
  The measurement is not rewritten: the reading comes from the Console host's
  live stream, else the transcript the hook payload itself names (its last
  real call, read from the tail), else the session index; the window is the
  session's own where stated, else the model's known window through the
  same `agentFarm.contextWindowTokens` override the viewer honours. No
  reading, no window, a reading over the window — no percentage, no sentence.
- **The channel is the live hook's own answer.** Every account's Claude
  settings already POST each tool call to the listener and print its answer;
  the listener used to answer `{}` to everything. It now answers a due
  session's `PostToolUse` / `UserPromptSubmit` with
  `{ hookSpecificOutput: { additionalContext } }`, which Claude Code puts
  into the model's context before its next step — no new process, no
  polling, and never on a hook that does not read the field. A guard that
  throws still answers `{}` and 200: a tool call is never broken by it.
- **An engine with no channel is said, not faked.** A crossing on a Codex
  session is recorded as `undelivered` with the reason; nothing is sent.
- **Thresholds are settings** — `agentFarm.contextConvergePct` (35),
  `agentFarm.contextHandoverPct` (40), 0 = off, a converge line above the
  handover line folds down onto it — **read and written from the bridge:**
  `sessions.contextGuard` (the thresholds, every session's record; with
  `id` one session's record AND its window reading right now) and
  `sessions.contextGuard.set`. `console.sessions` rows carry
  `contextSignal`. Records survive a reload (`context-guard.json`).
- Still open on the item (next steps): the session card and the viewer
  showing whether the signal went and whether the run handed over after it;
  the clean continuation — `retry.ts`'s smart path and `taskRounds.ts` not
  resuming a conversation past the handover line but opening a new session
  from the handover note; the sentry diagnosis carrying the fill; a mission
  role's handover known to the lead; the interactive card's "continue from
  handover" option.
- Tests: `test_context_guard` (65) — thresholds, the sentence, the hook
  answer shape, the transcript tail, the guard's once-per-level/re-arm/no-
  channel rules, the host wiring, and the listener end to end over HTTP.

## 3.537.0 - the mission form can say which endpoint serves each member and the planner (X-107, closes) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ MEASURED: the spec had carried a route per member and per planner since
  3.534.0 and the form could not say either** — the dimension was reachable
  from the bridge only. A person starting a mission from the page had no box
  for the one fact no transcript preserves (X-98).
- **Each team row carries a Route box and, under a route that serves tiers, a
  Tier box** (`pr-`/`tr-`), in the Tasks form's own words (`ntRouteRows`): the
  label is the bare value, the meaning is the hover, the MIRROR line opens
  with what the box holds. Drawn only where the engine has routes at all; on
  an engine with none the slot is held by a `—` that says why (B-02.2), so
  the rows stay columns — measured in the laid-out DOM, three rows on the
  same edges.
- **The tier belongs to its route.** Moving the route drops the tier under it
  on the spot and the row says so (`tier opus cleared — it belonged to the
  route this row was on`): unlike a model the engine no longer offers (U-101
  asks), a tier without its route has no meaning at all (X-101). Moving the
  ENGINE goes through the same ask-first plan as the model and the effort,
  with `lostRoute`/`lostTier` beside them — and the strip now names a lost
  sign-in too, which it had been leaving out.
- **The Orchestrator block carries its own pair** (`f-planner-route`,
  `f-planner-tier`) beside the planner's sign-in: one long-lived headless
  claude, not a delegation, and the workers' route says nothing about it.
- **Apply profile writes both onto every included row.** The profile's tier
  list is the profile's route's own — with the route left on "don't change"
  the rows may be on different routes, so only keep/clear is offered. A kept
  route the profile's engine cannot take, or a tier the route does not serve,
  refuses the press before any row is touched (X-123).
- **No mission-wide route box on the form**, for the reason U-101 removed the
  mission-wide engine box: a level the rows cannot see is a form disagreeing
  with itself. `MissionSpec.providerId` stays for the bridge and for
  inheritance, exactly as `engine` and `account` do.
- What the item's list still named — task templates carry the route through
  `RunDimensions` (X-106), a pool member and the adaptive delegate resolve
  through `resolveDelegateRun` (3.534.0), a delegation is made with its
  dimensions by the shape, a rerun or a resume runs the spec's own route,
  a task retry is a new enqueue that seals itself. There is no mission
  template entity to carry one.
- Host: the missions page receives `routes` from `engineRouteMatrix`, the
  same matrix the Tasks form reads. Fixture: a `form-routes` scene (a member
  on Kimi/opus beside one on OpenCode, the planner on Kimi). Tests:
  `test_team_row_columns` +3 (two more axes, each placeholder naming its
  own), `test_missions_webview` +14 (boxes, payload, route move, profile).

## 3.536.0 - an agent reads what a session said through the bridge, in one shape for every engine (B-24) (2026-09-17)
