- **‼️ MEASURED: the bridge could say where a transcript is and could not hand
  it over.** `sessions.find` gives the file, `search.transcripts` finds words
  across all of them, and nothing returned ONE conversation. So an agent
  opened the raw file and had to know each engine's format — and a Console
  snapshot calls the model's reply `agent` and a tool's answer `result`. A
  filter written for Claude's `assistant` came back empty and an agent
  reported "nothing there" about a session that was full (2026-09-17).
- **`sessions.read`** answers with the session's messages in the transcript
  page's own vocabulary — `user | assistant | tool | toolResult | system` for
  every engine. It goes through the viewer's own `buildData`, with the page's
  message ceiling lifted, so an agent and the viewer read one thing; nobody
  parses a transcript of their own.
- **Which session is meant is never guessed** (`core/sessionRead.ts`): an
  exact id, a unique id prefix or the transcript path. A prefix that fits
  several sessions is refused with their ids; an unknown id points at
  `sessions.find`.
- **Pages honestly:** `roles` (default user,assistant; `all`; an engine's own
  `agent`/`result` accepted on the way in, an unknown word refused rather than
  dropped), `turn`, `sidechain`, `from`/`limit` with `next` (negative `from`
  counts from the end), `maxChars` with a `clipped` full length on every cut
  step. Numbers are read with `optNum`, never through `optStr` (B-25).
- Tests: `test_session_read` (34) — roles, aliases, paging, clipping,
  reference resolution, the op's wiring, and a Console snapshot read end to
  end through the page's parse.

## 3.535.0 - the provenance panel says which endpoint served the work, and whose plan paid (X-107) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ MEASURED: the panel that exists to answer "why did it run like that" was
  silent about two of its dimensions.** `provLines` prints one row per entry of
  the page's own `DIMS` list, and that list was written out by hand with five
  entries. X-225 put an `account` on the resolver's record months ago and this
  never printed it — so the one dimension a reader chases when a bill looks
  wrong was missing from the only surface that could have said it, and the
  route would have gone the same way.
- **Route and Sign-in are on the list now.** The tier prints UNDER its route
  (`kimi-work/opus`), never as a line of its own: alone the word says nothing,
  because it means a different model on every endpoint (X-101).
- **The row chip carries the route and leaves the sign-in to the panel.** That
  is a judgement about the reader, not about width: the chip answers "what did
  this work run as", and the endpoint that served it is the one part of that
  answer no transcript preserves (X-98). Which plan was billed is a question
  about the invoice and has its own line one hover away (ONE SUBJECT).
- Neither reports an `applied` reading, which is correct rather than missing —
  no engine states the route or the sign-in it ran under, so nothing is
  compared and no row can wear a false `≠`.
- Fixture: the delegate scene now carries a route and a sign-in; panel and
  chip both measured in the laid-out DOM. Tests: `test_mission_route` +4
  (37 total). Suite 366 files / 22345 green.

## 3.534.0 - a mission says which endpoint carries its workers and which carries its planner (X-107) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ X-107 (1/n) — MEASURED: a mission could not state a route anywhere.**
  Every other run dimension a cast member states travels down to the
  delegation — engine (X-18), permission mode (M-14), effort (M-18), sign-in
  (X-225). The ROUTE did not, so "these delegations go through the Kimi
  endpoint, the orchestrator stays on Anthropic's" could not be said at all,
  and every participant took whichever standing route its agent happened to
  have at 3 a.m.
- **Two axes, because they are two questions.** `MissionSpec.providerId` /
  `.tier` is the route every delegation is served by; a member (or a pool
  member) overrides it with its own. `MissionSpec.plannerProviderId` /
  `.plannerTier` is the ORCHESTRATOR's own — one long-lived headless `claude`
  carrying the run from round to round, and the most expensive thing a mission
  does. Same shape `plannerAccount` (X-225) already has.
- **‼️ THE TIER COMES FROM WHICHEVER RUNG NAMED THE ROUTE.** `opus` is
  `kimi-k2-thinking` on one endpoint and `MiniMax-M2` on another (X-101), so a
  member's tier is never applied to the MISSION's route, and a tier with no
  route at all is dropped rather than stored as a word with no referent.
  Under the mission there is no third rung on purpose: `resolveLaunchRoute`
  already falls through to the agent's standing record at the spawn, and
  answering one question twice is how two answers start disagreeing.
- **The planner now spawns through its route.** That call passed `undefined`
  where the runtime layer belongs, so the longest-lived call a mission makes
  ran on whatever the window was holding while every delegate beside it could
  be pointed anywhere.
- **‼️ AND THE DELEGATION IS MADE WITH ITS DIMENSIONS, BY THE SHAPE.** They
  were written onto the row `addTask` had already returned — the dimensions
  are part of MAKING a task, and since X-106 one arriving a line later is one
  the enqueue's route seal never saw. `runExtras` now carries the lot, so the
  next dimension travels without that seam knowing it exists.
- **Two silent drops found and fixed on the way.** `bridgeMissionInput` copied
  a cast member field by field and BOTH its team and its pool mapping had lost
  X-225's `account`: a caller could set it over the bridge, get no refusal and
  watch every delegation run on the standing sign-in. And the preview's
  `memberView` took its own field list, so the draft card reported every
  account as unset while the wave ran on it. Both take the member's own shape
  now, measured against `MissionTeamMember` read out of the source.
- **One refusal, four doors.** `launchRouteRefusal` is asked by the automation
  door (`runDims`), by the planner box, by the mission-wide box and by every
  member box — before the mission exists, not once per planning call for the
  rest of the run. A member's is judged against the engine THAT member lands
  on, exactly as its account is.
- Readable back: `missions.list` gives each member's `account`, `providerId`
  and `tier` (falling back to the mission's), plus `plannerProviderId` /
  `plannerTier`; the run note and `step.ran` carry `route <id>/<tier>`.
- Tests: new `test_mission_route` (33), `test_bridge` +1, and four source
  guards updated to the new shape. Suite 366 files / 22341 green.
- **Still open on X-107:** the missions form has no route boxes yet (the
  dimension is reachable over the bridge only), and mission templates,
  adaptive suggestions and resume inheritance are not wired.

## 3.533.0 - a queued run remembers what its route MEANT when somebody chose it (X-106) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ X-106 step (1) — MEASURED: a task could not tell a route that stayed
  put from one that was edited underneath it.** A task states its route when
  it is WRITTEN and runs hours later. The profile behind that route is a
  setting: it can be edited, re-keyed or pointed at another endpoint while the
  row waits in the queue. The spawn then resolved the same name to a different
  answer and the manifest recorded THAT — correctly, which is the problem.
  Both readings of "which endpoint served the nightly batch" were one sentence
  written twice, and the change between them was nowhere at all.
- **The seal, at the enqueue.** `FarmTask.routeSeal` holds what the named
  route resolved to at the moment somebody chose it: the redacted
  `ProviderIdentity` (profile id + revision, endpoint, base url, auth KIND —
  never a credential) and the catalog revision. Written in `addTask`, where
  the project is already stamped, because that is the one moment a dozen call
  sites share. It is a RECORD, not a dimension: not in `RunDimensions`, not
  carried by `runExtras`, and a seal handed in on the shape is dropped — a
  retry is a new enqueue and seals itself.
- **‼️ ONLY WHERE A ROUTE WAS NAMED.** With nothing chosen the agent's own
  standing record decides at the spawn; sealing that would report drift the
  first time the user changed their standing route, about a run that never
  named one.
- **And the spawn says when it moved.** `startTask` asks the SAME symbol
  (`sealRoute` → `resolveLaunchRoute`, the resolver the terminal, the Console
  and the manifest all go through) and writes a new kind of event on the run's
  own record — `route-drift`, drawn as "route moved under it" — naming what
  changed: profile, revision, endpoint, base url, auth kind, model, catalog.
  It does NOT hold the run back: an edited profile is a changed answer to the
  same question, not a different question. What came BACK (`reportedModels`,
  the proof) is never drift, which a deep equality would have reported on
  every run that answered.
- **The manifest states its catalog revision too.** X-102 declared the field
  and nothing ever filled it, so the other half of the comparison was blank
  for six releases. `recordLaunch` now resolves it at the one point every
  launch door passes through. Empty on a Claude route is correct: that catalog
  is derived from the profiles, and each profile's revision is in the identity.
- **The retry names its route at the enqueue** instead of writing it onto the
  returned row — a route patched on afterwards is a route the seal never saw,
  and the run's own history would start blank.
- Read it with `tasks.get` → `routeSeal` (null = no route was named, which is
  not the same as a route that did not move).
- Tests: `test_task_route` (+16: the drift sentence field by field, the two
  moments against a real `TaskManager`, one resolver asked exactly twice, the
  seal kept out of the dimensions, both halves of the manifest comparison);
  fixture scene on the scheduled run, its timeline measured in the laid-out
  DOM.

## 3.532.0 - every sign-in on its own quota beat, in the background, with a switch (X-239, X-240, X-241) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ THE USER'S RULE:** "five accounts, two of them working — those two on
  the active interval (60 s), the other three on the idle one (5 min), smart,
  and never all at once." Until this, the only timer calling the account
  usage service's `beat()` was the Engines page's own — no page open, no
  reading, and a rule such as `@emptiest` chose on figures nobody had read
  since the last time somebody looked; and the TTL was one fleet-wide figure,
  so one running turn put all five sign-ins on the fast beat.
- **X-240 — the TTL is each slot's own.** `AccountUsageOptions.ttlMs(slot?)`
  is asked with the slot in hand; the host answers `refreshMs(slotActive(id),
  minutes, seconds)`. A slot is "working" when a live turn (`working`/`tool`,
  never an idle open session) is placed on it by its LAUNCH MANIFEST
  (`sessionAccountOf`, the one reader every surface uses); a live turn no
  manifest places counts for the engine's standing sign-in. A TTL of 0 (the
  minutes setting at 0) now makes a beat owe that slot nothing — measured
  before: 0 made every slot due on every tick, so "automatic refresh off"
  read the endpoint every five seconds while the Engines page was open.
- **X-239 — the beat runs whether or not a page is open.** A background timer
  at the request floor (5 s) asks the service; the service decides whether
  any slot is due, whether the switch is on, whether the endpoint is backing
  off, and reads at most one slot per tick — five accounts are never asked at
  once, and a 429 still pauses the fleet. Off costs a timer and nothing else.
- **X-241 — the switch.** `agentFarm.accountsAutoRefresh` (default on), read
  by the service (`autoBeat`) before anything, file walks included; a
  person's ⟳, "all engines" and the turn-boundary read still work. The
  Engines page's Accounts head wears `⚡ Auto-refresh: ON/OFF` (lit / grey),
  its AFTip MIRROR first ("Now: on — 1 of 5 on the fast beat") and then EVERY
  sign-in's own beat with why (DENSITY: a fact a reader would otherwise infer
  card by card). Bridge: `accounts.autoRefresh` (read, or `on` to write) —
  the op and the button call ONE function; `accounts.list` carries the state.
- Tests: `test_account_usage` (+12: two working slots read at 60 s while the
  idle one waits its five minutes; the switch spends nothing and leaves ⟳
  and the edge alone; TTL 0 owes nothing; the host wiring read from source),
  `test_engines_page_accounts` (+11, ON and OFF scenes), `test_bridge` (+4),
  parity manifest entry; fixture scene `enginesautooff`, photographed, the
  button measured on the head row.

## 3.531.0 - a named rule may be the emptiest of the sign-ins it lists, and a task handed to the Console keeps its route, its sign-in and its discipline (X-324, X-106) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ X-106 step (2) — MEASURED: a task with `interactiveTarget: 'console'`
  opened on the agent's defaults.** The gate from the task runner into the
  Console (`startConsoleTask` in `extension.ts`) was a hand-written field
  list — engine · model · effort · permissionMode · projectId — so
  `providerId`, `tier`, `account` and `superpowers` fell out between the task
  and `consoleHost.start`, which accepts all four. The gate now spreads
  `runExtras(task)` (the shape, so the next dimension travels without the
  seam knowing) and the door reads the route, resolves the task's **account
  once** through `launchAccountFor` (a rule such as `@emptiest` or `@Night`
  becomes a slot against this moment's figures, `commit` lets `@round-robin`
  advance; a rule that can choose nothing is a warning and a failed task,
  never the main sign-in — the same answer an absent engine gives), and
  falls superpowers to the agent's default the way the headless spawn does
  (a hosted fresh start reads absent as OFF, so the default has to be said).
  `test_task_route` (+16) reads `RunDimensions` out of the source and
  requires every field the Console can use at the door, the exemptions
  named (`cli`, the interactive target/close, the finish sound, `workDir`
  which arrives as `cwd`, and the queue's own `priority` · `rounds` ·
  `ignoreBudget` · `retry`). Step (1) — sealing the profile revision at
  enqueue — is still open.

- **‼️ THE GAP THE USER NAMED.** "Of my five sign-ins, start on whichever of
  THESE three has the most room" could not be said: the built-in `@emptiest`
  scans every slot of the engine, `@pool` needs a sentry campaign running,
  and a named rule walks its steps as a CHAIN — step 1 carries every launch
  until it is walled, so work never spreads across the accounts the user
  chose. And the wall is a launch-time filter, not a mid-session switch, so
  the choice has to be right at the start.
- **A rule now has a `strategy`**: `chain` (the default, unchanged) or
  `emptiest` — the listed accounts are a pool of their own, compared at the
  launch on the figures of that moment, and the one with the most room starts.
  The ranking is `roomOrder`, the very function the engine-wide `@emptiest`
  runs on (most room first, a measured slot before an unread one) — no second
  copy. A step's own wall and model filter mean the same in both strategies;
  a step the host says is not stored is out of the pool; every listed slot
  walled is a REFUSAL naming each with its figure and the first reset, never
  the main sign-in. A chain may still step through an emptiest rule.
- **‼️ The lock, and why.** A step naming a RULE has no single figure to
  compare, so a list holding one can only be walked as a chain. The core
  refuses to store `emptiest` over such a list (`policyShapeRefusal`, the
  sentence naming each rule step); the Engines form holds its Strategy switch
  on chain while a rule step is in the draft — the emptiest row disabled, the
  label reading "locked", the AFTip saying which step did it — and keeping a
  rule step in an emptiest draft flips it to chain on the draft itself, so
  Save posts what the drawing shows. Deciding this at the RULE rather than as
  a new "pool of accounts" step kind keeps the step list flat: a step is still
  an account or a rule, and how the list is read is one switch on the card.
- Engines page: a strategy chip on every rule card (`→ chain` / `⚖ emptiest`,
  AFTip with the definition); an emptiest card sets its steps beside each
  other (`·`) rather than walking them (`→`). Bridge: `policies.save` takes
  `strategy`; `policies.list` describes an emptiest rule by what it compares.
  `agentFarm.accountPolicies` schema carries the enum.
- Tests: `test_account_policies` (+22: the pool, per-step walls, the model
  filter, unstored and unread slots, the refusal, the shape lock, a chain
  through an emptiest rule), `test_engines_policies` (+20: the chip, the
  switch, the lock on keep, the posted draft, the free switch after the rule
  step is removed), `test_bridge` (+3); fixture rule `@Ucu_Birden` (emptiest
  over three slots, resolving to the LAST listed) + two form scenes (free,
  locked), both photographed and the chip measured.

## 3.530.0 - the sentry's warnings reach the user as warnings (X-309) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ MEASURED ON THE FIRE DRILL (scenario 2).** The failure brake fired and
  posted its notice — but as a routine **update**. Both sentry notices
  ("Sentry stopped", "the leader has stopped waking") were posted with
  `type: 'alert'`, which is not a notice type; `NoticeInput.type` is a loose
  string and an unknown word becomes `update` without a sound. Both are
  `warning` now.
- `test/test_notices.js` (+2) reads every literal type the host posts out of
  `src/extension.ts` and requires each to be a real `NOTICE_TYPES` entry

## 3.529.0 - the third fire drill's three findings: a run is told its own id, a file is not a handover note because the session wrote it, and a round is told how to close its item (X-321, X-322, X-323) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ MEASURED ON THE THIRD FIRE DRILL** (X-309 scenario 1 run 3, campaign
  `sc-mu4w20b2`, `basit` · haiku · `bypassPermissions`). X-320 held — the first
  round's words carried `P-1` — and the round wrote the file correctly. Then it
  went wrong three ways at once.
- **X-321 — back-to-back runs in one folder never learnt their session id.**
  A campaign opens its rounds one after another in the same agent folder, and
  `bindSession`'s 120 s of slack put the second round's transcript inside all
  three rounds' windows; the binding was refused as ambiguous and never made.
  That round's row kept no session, no progress and no cost, and the third round
  opened on "The previous session () ended…" with nothing measured behind it.
  A fresh headless Claude run is now **told** its id at the spawn
  (`--session-id <uuid>`, measured on 2.1.269 with `-p` — the transcript is
  written under exactly that name), the row carries it the moment the process
  exists (`spawnSessionId`, and `runSessionId` so a run killed a second later can
  still be resumed), and the launch binding publishes it as a declaration, which
  `bindSession` already trusts before any clock. A resumed run is not given one.
- **X-322 — a file was a "handover note" because the session wrote it.**
  Authorship scores +3 and the default threshold is 3, so every markdown file a
  session wrote passed on its own: the round's deliverable
  `10_Notes/sentry_hello.md` was adopted at 4 and the next round was told to
  "read the handover note FIRST and carry on from exactly where it stopped".
  Adoption now also needs something that speaks of a handover — the session id
  in the name, `devir`/`handover`, the canonical pattern, or the word *note*
  (so X-189's `gece-notu.md` is still found). The file stays identified and
  ranked; the evidence names it and says why it was passed over.
- **…and the evidence stopped being a wall.** The same words recited the 27
  other sessions' notes in the shared folder — twice, because the folder is
  reached through two sources. Near misses are now counted per file name, and
  past three they are one line: "27 handover notes of other sessions were passed
  over (… among them)".
- **X-323 — a round was told to close its item but not how.** The haiku round
  searched its TOOL list for `projects.backlog.check`, found nothing (it is a
  bridge op, reached through a command), and wrote "P-1 closed" — the item stayed
  open. The item line now carries the exact command, with the staged helper's
  real path (forward slashes) and the project filled in, says it is a shell
  command and not a tool, and says "closed" may be said only once it answers ok.
  With no helper path, or a value a one-line command cannot quote safely, no
  command is invented; an opening that already names the op is left alone.
- `test/test_task_session_id.js` (new, 13), `test/test_handover_discovery.js`
  (+9), `test/test_sentry_driver.js` (+9).

## 3.528.0 - and the FIRST round is a round: the opening words carry the item too (X-320) (2026-09-17)

- **‼️ X-319 FIXED ROUNDS 2+ AND LEFT ROUND 1 AS BLIND AS THE FIVE THAT FAILED
  THE DRILL.** `sentryStep` only builds words when a session has finished
  (`words = fin && diagnosis ? buildNextPrompt(…)`), so the first round of every
  campaign has no verdict at all and opens on `i.opening` — the sentence the
  user typed when starting the campaign, **written before anybody knew which
  item the backlog would hand out**. The round takes the item (`taken: P-1`) and
  is never told what it says.
- **The same hole sat on two more paths.** The leader's own sentence REPLACES
  the built template and so never passed through the item attachment; and a tick
  that wakes from a sleep whose carried sentence no longer fits drops it and
  falls back to the opening, which was equally bare.
- **So the attachment moved to where every path passes** — `withItem` is now the
  exported `withItemLine` and the driver runs the prompt it is about to send
  through it, whatever produced that prompt. `fresh` still follows the verdict,
  so `clean-handover` keeps naming the item without the "this is the work" line.
- **‼️ AN EMPTY OPENING STAYS EMPTY.** A campaign started with no words is
  refused by the planner (`no-prompt`) rather than opening an empty session; an
  item line appended to nothing would make that emptiness look like words and
  send a paid round out on a sentence nobody wrote.
- `test/test_sentry_driver.js` (+6) pins the itemless opening, the opening that
  already names the code, the empty opening's refusal, the leader sentence and
  the dropped carry.

## 3.527.0 - a round that takes an item is told what the item says, whichever verdict fired (X-319) (2026-09-16)

- **‼️ MEASURED ON THE SECOND FIRE DRILL** (X-309 scenario 1 run 2, campaign
  `sc-mu403dqa`, `basit` · haiku · `bypassPermissions`, pool
  `wmmuratvural, murvietnam` tiered): the weekly wall was skipped correctly and
  no retry escaped the pool — and then **five rounds in a row took `P-1` and
  every one of them ended having done nothing**, until the failure brake
  stopped the campaign.
- **The round was taking real work off the backlog and was never told what it
  was.** Of the five built-in templates only `item-done` and
  `nothing-to-continue` name the item; `hit-the-wall` and the `*` fallback hand
  the round the DIAGNOSIS of the previous session and nothing else. A model
  given an instruction with a hole in it fills the hole: one round decided the
  item "was already closed" without looking (zero tool calls), another read the
  diagnosis as a file-naming problem and **renamed a file in the vault nobody
  had asked it to touch**.
- **So the item is now attached where the words are built** (`buildNextPrompt`),
  not in the templates. The templates are the USER'S to write — that is the
  whole point of the file — and a rule every block has to remember is a rule the
  next block forgets. A template that already names the code is left exactly as
  it is, and a round that took no item is given no item line.
- **`clean-handover` is the one verdict this must not fight.** There IS a trace
  to carry on from and the block deliberately says not to restart the item, so
  the item is NAMED there without the "this is the work" line — knowing which
  item the note is about is not the same as being told to start it over.
- `test/test_sentry_prompt.js` (+10) pins every verdict including the catch-all,
  a block the user wrote, the no-double-naming rule and the empty-backlog case.

## 3.526.0 - what is inside backticks is quoted text, not a field: closing an item no longer rewrites the sentence it was quoted in (X-318) (2026-09-16)

- **‼️ MEASURED ON THE VERY NEXT WRITE.** X-312's own backlog line quoted
  `` `[closed:: 2145c0a0#3]` `` as the evidence of the bug it was describing.
  Closing that item read the quote as the item's `closed` FIELD, and
  `stampBacklogClosed` — the one function whose whole promise is that nothing
  else on the line is touched — replaced it where it stood. The user's sentence
  silently named a different session, and the real stamp was never appended at
  all. Two of the three things a closure is supposed to do went wrong, and
  neither of them was visible in the reply.
- **An inline field is something Agent Farm wrote; a backtick span is something
  the person wrote**, and to a regex they are identical. So every field is now
  read from the line with its backtick runs blanked out (same length, so an
  index found in the mask is the index in the real line), and the stamp writer
  splices by POSITION rather than calling `replace` — which rewrote every match
  on the line, quoted or not.
- **And the quote survives into the text the reader is shown.** `displayText`
  strips fields, icons and tags to leave the words; it was deleting the quoted
  example too, so the sentence making a point of it arrived with a hole in it.
  Stripping now runs over the un-quoted parts only. A field REBUILD
  (`setBacklogFields`) is correct by construction once that is true, since it
  rebuilds the line out of those words.
- The item that was damaged has been repaired in place: the quote is back to
  what it said, and the real `[closed:: …]` is where it belongs.
- `test/test_project_backlog.js` (+10) pins it from both ends — a quoted
  `[closed:: …]` and a quoted `[effort:: …]` beating neither the parse nor the
  real field, the stamp appended rather than swapped, clearing taking only the
  real one, and a field rebuild carrying the quote through byte for byte.

## 3.525.0 - a sentry round is reopened by its campaign and by nothing else, and the ledger is stamped with the session that actually closed the item (X-312) (2026-09-16)

- **‼️ MEASURED ON THE SAME FIRE DRILL** (X-309 scenario 1, campaign
  `sc-mu3psbkz`): a round walled on a pool account ended `failed`, and the task
  layer then retried it by itself — *"Sentry R1 · P-1 (retry 1)"*. The retry
  escaped the campaign in both directions at once, and neither half was
  visible from the other.
- **OUT OF THE POOL.** The retry's account came from `carryOnAccount`, which
  ranks every sign-in captured on the machine and has never heard of a campaign
  pool. So the work carried on to an account the user had deliberately fenced
  OUT of it — the one plan the pool exists to protect — and spent it all night.
- **OFF THE LEDGER.** `runExtras` carries a run's DIMENSIONS and not its
  lineage, so the retry was born without `sentryOf`: invisible to the campaign,
  which went on counting two rounds, saw nothing come out of them and stopped
  on the failure brake — while the retry it could not see was writing files,
  committing and closing backlog items.
- **The whole reopening decision goes back to the one place that owns it.**
  A sentry round is no longer retried by the retry policy at all; the
  campaign's own next round IS the retry, and it is a fresh reading of the
  backlog on an account `campaignPick` chose. This is exactly the rule the
  watchdog already stated for a round that goes quiet (X-178), asked now of
  every ending rather than one of them. Narrowing the handover to the pool
  would have fixed the first half and left the second. The round's own record
  says which rule stopped the retry, so nothing is refused in silence.
- **The gate is narrow.** An ordinary headless run that meets the same wall is
  retried exactly as before and still carries on to a sign-in with room —
  X-226 is untouched.
- **‼️ AND WHOSE TURN CLOSED THE ITEM IS ASKED OF THE CALLER, not guessed.**
  The escaped retry closed `P-1` through `projects.backlog.check` and the stamp
  landed on a DIFFERENT session of the same agent (`[closed:: 2145c0a0#3]`),
  pointing a reader at a transcript where nothing of the sort happened:
  `attributeTrack` ranks the agent's live sessions and takes the freshest,
  which is a coin toss whenever two are alive — and the wrong row looks exactly
  as certain as a right one. The caller already says who it is; X-310 put
  `from.sessionId` in every bridge envelope, read from what the CLI published
  to its own children. Both doors into the ledger (`projects.backlog.check`,
  `projects.track`) were throwing it away and now read it. An explicit
  `session` argument still wins, and an engine that publishes nothing still
  falls through to the ranking, stamped `uncertain` as before.
- `test/test_sentry_retry.js` (14) pins all of it — including `runExtras`
  dropping the lineage, so a later change there cannot quietly make this
  reasoning obsolete without failing.

## 3.524.0 - the fire drill's first finding: a weekly wall was invisible to the pool, and the brake blamed permissions for it (X-309, scenario 1 run 1) (2026-09-16)

- **‼️ MEASURED ON THE FIRST FIRE DRILL** (campaign `sc-mu3psbkz`, `basit` ·
  haiku · `bypassPermissions` · pool `aicozums, wmmuratvural` tiered): round 1
  opened on `wmmuratvural` — correctly past `aicozums` at 100% of its five
  hours — and died in one line: *You've hit your weekly limit · resets 7pm*.
  Round 2 opened on the SAME account and died the same way. The brake stopped
  the campaign after two, saying the rounds "produced nothing … usually a
  permission or a working-directory mismatch". The permission mode was already
  `bypassPermissions`; the account was at 100% of its WEEK.
- **The slot read `0% · ok`.** `usageFrom` took the `five_hour` bar out of the
  snapshot and dropped the `seven_day` one that was sitting beside it, so a
  weekly wall was invisible to `slotIsUsable`, to the pool's rotation and to
  `@emptiest` alike — the account looked like the emptiest on the machine.
  **A slot now carries whichever window is FULLER** (`bindingBar`), names it
  when it is the week (`window: 'Current week (all models)'` — the card already
  says "of its current week", X-215 taught it for Codex), and carries THAT
  window's reset, which is what the campaign's sleep has to wait for. A tie or
  a fuller five-hour window reads exactly as before. The per-model weekly bars
  are not folded in: whether they bind depends on the launch's model.
- **A round that ended `failed` on the account's own wall is not barren.**
  `barren()` counted every `failed` row; a `wall-limit` diagnosis now exempts it
  the way X-307 already exempted a `done` one — the plan window being spent is
  the account's fault, answered by the rotation and the sleep, never by the
  brake. And the brake's permissions hint is written for `wall-unfinished` only,
  so a spent window is no longer explained as a cwd mismatch.
- The drill is still open: run 1 is the finding, not the pass. `test_account_usage`
  pins the drill's exact case (0% of five hours, 100% of the week → not usable);
  `test_sentry_driver` pins a `failed` wall-limit round at streak 0 through
  `failLimit + 1` repetitions.

## 3.523.0 - a rule can be written by hand: the Engines page grows an Account policies section with a chain editor — the last half of X-305 (2026-09-16)

- **‼️ THE ONE SURFACE A HAND COULD NOT REACH.** Steps 1–3 made a rule
  choosable everywhere an account is taken and gave it a bridge; a named rule
  could still only be WRITTEN by editing `agentFarm.accountPolicies` in a JSON
  file or calling `policies.save`. The Engines page — already the page for
  "which sign-ins does this machine hold" — now carries **Account policies**
  between Accounts (what a rule chooses among) and Providers.
- **The built-in four are a table, not cards.** One row per rule, one chip per
  engine that holds a captured slot, and the chip is what the rule comes to
  RIGHT NOW (`→ personal@gmail`, `→ Main account`) or that it cannot choose
  (`nothing right now`, in the palette's yellow for *your move* — never red,
  because a rule walled at 11:02 is the right answer at 14:50). The hover opens
  with the figure that decided it and puts the rule's standing description under
  it (MIRROR). They are not editable because they are not stored anywhere to
  edit; the vocabulary a named rule is written in needs no buttons.
- **A named rule is a card**: its chips, its engine pill (`any engine` or the
  one it is pinned to), its wall (`≤ 60%`, or the default with the hover saying
  so), its note and its chain read as numbered steps — `1. spare@gmail →
  2. @emptiest → 3. work@studio (haiku, sonnet)` — with Edit and Delete. ‼️ A
  chip names its engine only where nothing beside it does: a table column or a
  pinned rule's pill already says it, and saying it twice is the DENSITY fault.
- **The form is the `AFForm` card, and the chain is an `F.list` acting on the
  DRAFT.** Name (a stat when editing — a rename is a new rule), engine (a
  redraw field, because it changes which accounts a step can name), wall, note,
  then the steps with `↑ ↓ edit ✕`, and ONE step open at a time in a nested
  editor: kind (a rule | a fixed account — a redraw field), the value box drawn
  from that half (built-ins + the OTHER named rules, or the engine's slots),
  its own wall and a model filter. Reordering and removing post nothing; Save
  posts the whole draft, and a step still open when Save is pressed is kept
  rather than lost to a press one button over.
- **‼️ SAME FUNCTIONS AS THE BRIDGE.** `policies.save` and `policies.delete` had
  their logic inline; it now lives in `savePolicy` / `deletePolicy` in
  `extension.ts`, and the op, the page's `policySave` / `policyDelete` handlers
  and the deps are all calls to those two — the parity gate derives the shared
  symbol rather than trusting the claim. The page hands over a FORM, which
  `policyFromForm` reads through an allow-list (a field the page invented is
  dropped; an empty ceiling is ABSENT, not 0) before the core judges the shape.
  A refusal lands in the form; an empty `pol-msg` closes it. Both capabilities
  are in `parity.manifest.json` in this commit.
- **Looked at, not assumed.** Three new fixture scenes — zero rules (the default,
  the smallest arity), one rule, three rules (a chain, one walled right now, one
  stepping through another) — and a fourth that PRESSES Edit and opens step 3 in
  the nested editor. The fixture asks `resolvePolicy` for what each rule comes to
  rather than typing it. Both themes photographed; the DOM measured: table 331px
  (not stretched), no chip under 88px, every card head one line, the step
  editor's four controls 319px each. `test_engines_policies.js` (84) drives the
  real page through open → step → reorder → remove → refuse → close.

## 3.522.0 - every account picker now offers the rules, and a rule can be written, read and removed without touching a settings file — steps 3 and most of 4 of X-305 (2026-09-16)

- **‼️ TWO KINDS OF ANSWER, DRAWN AS TWO GROUPS.** A slot is an answer that was
  true when somebody picked it; a rule is re-decided at every launch. A flat
  list makes them look like the same kind of choice, so every account picker now
  draws **Smart policies — decided at each launch** above **Fixed accounts —
  this one, every time**. The headings live in `media/afAccount.js` beside the
  row body, for the reason the row body is there: three pages spelling a group
  differently is three pages the reader has to learn separately.
- **‼️ AND EVERY PICKER MEANS EVERY PICKER** — the Console composer, a live
  card's account box, the Missions delegation row, the Tasks step card, the
  Tasks run form and the Queue's fourth box. That is the failure
  `_REF/agentfarm-dev.md` names by name (added to the composer, forgotten
  everywhere else), so the gate DERIVES the list from the pages: any file that
  still called the ungrouped `AFAccount.options` fails it.
- **A rule reads as the rule AND what it comes to** — `@emptiest → aicozums`,
  and `@pool · nothing to pick right now` when it can choose nothing. ‼️ **A rule
  that cannot choose is still offered**: "right now" is not "at launch", and a
  rule walled at 11:02 may be the only thing that can answer at 14:50 when the
  first window turns over. The panel opens with the rule's own reason for this
  moment and puts its standing description under it (MIRROR).
- **The Console's box needed one structural change.** `axisBox` wrapped every
  list in a single `<optgroup>` named after the axis, and HTML has no nested
  `<optgroup>` — so a box may now pass `groups` instead, which replaces that one
  heading. The axis is already the heading of the box's own panel, so the one
  grouping level is spent on the distinction that is said nowhere else. Every
  other box passes no `groups` and is drawn exactly as before.
- **`agentFarm.accountPolicies` is now a real setting** with its full schema, and
  three bridge ops make it reachable without editing JSON: **`policies.list`**
  (every rule with what it comes to this second, its deciding figure, and its
  refusal), **`policies.save`** (refused by `policyShapeRefusal` if the rule
  could never choose — checked against the OTHER rules, so one can be rewritten)
  and **`policies.delete`** (refused while another rule steps through it, and it
  says out loud that anything still naming the rule is then REFUSED at launch
  rather than quietly taking the main sign-in).
- **Looked at, not assumed.** A new fixture scene sets the account box TO a rule
  — the state that can only go wrong in a picture — and the DOM was measured:
  two groups in the right order, all four policy shapes drawing correctly
  (`→ slot`, `→ Main account`, `· nothing to pick right now`, a named rule), the
  rule selected, box 111px. The label clips to `@emptiest → per` at strip width,
  which is SHORTHAND working as intended: the rule is the stable identity and
  the resolved slot is in the panel.
- **Gate:** `test_af_account.js` +10 on the component, `test_bridge.js` +12 on
  the three ops, `test_account_policy_wire.js` now 57. **What remains** (the
  rest of step 4): the Engines page CRUD — the rules are fully usable from the
  bridge and the settings file, but not yet written from a panel.

## 3.521.0 - the rule now reaches the spawn: a launch really asks it, and a rule that can choose nothing refuses instead of spending the main sign-in — step 2 of X-305 (2026-09-16)

- **‼️ ONE RESOLVER, AND EVERY DOOR IS ALREADY BEHIND IT.** `launchAccountPick`
  is the single place an account box becomes an answer: a stated slot passes
  straight through, a stated rule is walked by `resolvePolicy` against
  `policyWorldFor` — the live usage snapshot, what the standing layers answer,
  the running campaign's pool, the round-robin cursor and the user's own rules.
  `launchAccountFor`, `launchAccountSlot` and `launchAccountEnv` all resolve
  through it, so the account a door SHOWS and the account a process GETS cannot
  differ. No door had to be taught anything: the seam was already singular
  (X-169), which is the whole return on having built it that way.
- **‼️ A REFUSAL IS A THROW, NEVER AN EMPTY STRING.** `''` on this seam means
  "inject no variable", and no variable means the machine's main sign-in — so a
  rule that answered `''` would spend exactly the plan it was written to protect,
  on a launch nobody was watching (X-302). `launchAccountEnv` refuses the spawn
  **before** it looks the slot up, and `launchAccountRefusal` asks the rule at
  the DOOR as well, so "every sign-in is walled, the first is back at 14:49" is
  said where the box was typed rather than thrown at the spawn. It also now
  hands the named rules to `accountRefusal`, so `@nihgt` is a typo and `@night`
  is a rule.
- **‼️ THE ROTATION MOVES ONLY WHERE A LAUNCH IS REAL.** `@round-robin`'s cursor
  is remembered in `workspaceState` by the three doors that really start a
  process and by `launchAccountEnv` — never by `launchAccountPick` itself, so a
  page that merely describes a setup cannot advance the rotation every time it
  is drawn. The Console door also stopped resolving the account **twice**, which
  a rule makes wrong as well as wasteful: two calls, two different slots, and
  the card keeps the second.
- **‼️ THE DOOR AND THE SPAWN ASK THE SAME QUESTION.** A named rule may carry a
  model-filtered step, so a `launchAccountRefusal` that checked without the
  model was guarding a launch it had not described — the door would pass and the
  spawn throw, or it would refuse something that would have worked. Every door
  with a launch shape in hand now hands the model over, and the gate names the
  four of them one by one.
- **The pickers speak rules.** `accountRowsFor` offers the built-ins and the
  user's named rules above the stored slots, each row saying what it would pick
  **right now** or why it cannot (MIRROR); `accountRowLabel` prints
  `@emptiest → Work` rather than today's answer alone, so a standing rule and a
  slot somebody typed can be told apart. The profile editor stopped printing
  `@emptiest (not on this machine)` — it asks the same label. Both bridge
  session doors document the rules in their `account?` describe.
- **Gate:** `test_account_policy_wire.js`, 41 assertions, and it measures the
  WIRE rather than the core (A-02.10): the seam is singular, the refusal comes
  before the slot lookup, the commit sites are exactly the doors that spawn —
  and `PolicyWorld` is read out of the core's own source so **every** field of
  it must be supplied by `policyWorldFor`, with one named exemption (`now`,
  which is the real clock). Mutation-checked. **What remains** (steps 3–4):
  `media/afAccount.js` gaining the two groups, the Engines page CRUD,
  `agentFarm.accountPolicies` and `policies.list/save/delete`.

## 3.520.0 - an account chosen at launch by a rule, against the figures of that moment — the core, step 1 of X-305 (2026-09-15)

- **‼️ THE POLICY CORE, PURE AND PROVEN — NOT YET WIRED.** `src/core/accountPolicy.ts`
  turns a stated `@emptiest` / `@pool` / `@standing` / `@round-robin`, or one of
  the user's own named rules (`@Night`), into a slot against the usage figures
  it is handed — never a disk, never a clock of its own. `@emptiest` is
  `roomOrder`'s head for the launch's engine; `@pool` walks the running
  campaign's pool exactly as the sentry does (`accountOrder`, its order, its
  rotation, its ceiling); `@standing` is the layered answer a launch stating
  nothing gets, said out loud; `@round-robin` takes the next usable slot after
  the one handed back as `cursor`. A named rule is a chain of steps — a slot or
  a policy, each with its own wall and an optional model filter — walked top to
  bottom, refusing loops at depth five.
- **‼️ A POLICY THAT FINDS NOTHING REFUSES; IT NEVER FALLS TO THE MAIN SIGN-IN**
  (X-302's lesson, applied at the spawn seam): the refusal names every slot with
  its figure and the first reset. **And a wall is 95 here, not 100** — a policy
  chooses where to START a session, and a slot with five per cent left is the
  one that ends it ten minutes in.
- `accountRefusal` no longer calls `@emptiest` a forgotten slot: a policy id is
  checked against the built-ins and the named rules (`policyRefusal`), so a typo
  is refused at the door and a real policy passes to the seam. `policyShapeRefusal`
  refuses a rule on its way in (no name, untypeable name, a built-in's name, an
  empty chain, a step with neither or both, a step pointing at itself or at
  nothing, a ceiling outside 1–100).
- **Gate:** `test_account_policies.js`, 63 assertions over the four policies,
  named chains (model filter, per-step wall, engine mismatch, loop, nothing
  usable, a step naming an unstored slot), the door's refusal and the shape
  check. **What remains** (steps 2–4 of X-305): the seam (`launchAccountFor`
  resolves a policy with `accountUsage.current()`, the campaign pool, the
  standing layers and a persisted round-robin cursor; `launchAccountRefusal`
  passes the named rules), `media/afAccount.js` gaining the two groups, the
  Engines page CRUD, `agentFarm.accountPolicies` and `policies.list/save/delete`.

## 3.519.0 - the headless Chrome the tests drive no longer fills the system drive (X-311) (2026-09-15)

- **‼️ THE LEAK WAS THE THROWAWAY PROFILE ITSELF.** `shoot_page.js`,
  `measure_page.js` and `test_shot_height.js` each launched Chrome with a fresh
  `--user-data-dir` — right, the user's own browser is never touched — but a
  profile Chrome has never seen is one it installs the machine's EXTERNAL
  extensions into on every launch (the registry names Adobe Acrobat twice and
  the IDM integration module here): the CRX lands in `%TEMP%\<guid>.tmp`, is
  unpacked into `%TEMP%\scoped_dir<pid>_<n>`, and `--dump-dom` finishing kills
  the process before the install completes, so nothing is ever cleaned up.
  Measured 2026-09-15: 2,584 folders and 4,145 CRX files, **15.5 GB, the system
  drive at ZERO and a VSIX install failing with ENOSPC**; today's leftovers
  arrived in four bursts, each at the exact minutes a full suite was running,
  ~40 per run. Neither the MCP browsers nor a schedule was the source.
- **Measured fix, three rounds each against the installed Chrome:** the old
  list left 1 `scoped_dir` per launch every time; **`--disable-extensions`
  left none** every time; `--disable-component-update` alone left 1 (it is an
  extension, not a component). The flags now live in ONE file,
  `test/headless_chrome.js` (`headlessFlags(profile)`), with
  `--disable-component-update` and `--disable-background-networking` behind
  the one that mattered — a longer page gives the component updater time to
  start downloads that end the same way.
- **And a sweeper for what is already there.** `sweepAndReport()` runs in every
  launch's `finally` and once more at the end of `run-all.js`: it takes only
  the leak's exact shape older than two hours — an empty or manifest-holding
  `scoped_dir<pid>_<n>`, a `<guid>.tmp` whose first bytes are the CRX magic
  `Cr24` — and leaves alone anything fresh, anything of another shape and
  anything the OS holds locked. First run on this machine: 60 folders and 100
  CRX files, 521.8 MB. `node test/headless_chrome.js --sweep [--hours N]` by
  hand.
- **Gate:** `test_headless_chrome.js` — a fourth hand-written flag list
  anywhere under `test/` or `tools/` fails by shape (a quoted `--headless=new`
  followed by a comma), the three sites are checked for `headlessFlags` and a
  sweep in their `finally`, the sweeper is proved on a fixture of eleven
  shapes, and the browser half launches the real Chrome with the flags and
  counts what appeared in `%TEMP%`. Mutations: the bare list put back into
  `measure_page.js` → 2 named failures; `--disable-extensions` removed → the
  live launch leaves 1 folder and the assertion says so.

## 3.518.0 - a restart waits for the turns that did not ask for it, and speaks only into the one that did (X-310) (2026-09-15)

- **‼️ ONLY THE TURN THAT ASKED CONSENTED TO DYING.** X-232 exempted every
  session the engine had named from blocking a `resume:true` restart, on the
  reading that a resume takes it up again so it is not a loss. An idle card is
  no blocker at all (A-02.4), so that exemption only ever reached sessions IN
  FLIGHT — and for those the reading is false: the revive marks them `midTurn`
  precisely because the answer they were writing is gone. Measured 2026-09-15:
  one session asked for a restart to load a build and a second one, on another
  card and mid file-write, was taken down with it having agreed to nothing.
  The exemption is now the **asker's alone** (`askedBy`); every other turn in
  flight blocks, the plan arms behind it, and it fires by itself when the last
  one is done.
- **‼️ AND THE "CARRY ON" PROMPT GOES TO THAT SEAT AND NO OTHER.** B-03.7
  narrowed the revive nudge from every seat to every *mid-turn* seat, which is
  one step short: being mid-turn says a turn was cut, not that this seat wanted
  it cut. Both sessions above were handed the same "carry on from where you
  were", and the one that had consented to nothing woke up and acted on guesses
  about a conversation whose last exchange had been destroyed under it. A
  session cut without asking now comes back whole — seat live, scrollback
  restored, **nothing spoken into it** — and its card says so in the note above
  the conversation (`REVIVE_HELD`), so the next word in it is the user's.
- **The asker is a fact the request carries, not one we guess.** `af.js` writes
  the caller's own session id into the request envelope (`from`), read from the
  environment the CLI already publishes to its children
  (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, or `AGENT_FARM_SESSION` for a terminal Agent Farm
  opened) — nothing is spawned, injected or remembered to make it true. It is a
  claim and never a credential: it rides on the envelope so an op's own
  `sessionId` argument can never be read as the caller, and **an unknown asker
  exempts nobody** — the plan simply arms and waits, which is slower and never
  destructive.
- Gates: `test_self_restart.js` (the bystander blocks, the asker does not, an
  unnamed asker exempts nobody, an armed plan remembers who asked, and the
  wiring from the op down to the stamp), `test_console_revive.js` (the nudge's
  two conditions, matched on the engine session id rather than the seat id a
  restart does not survive), `test_bridge.js` (the envelope is read back off
  the file `af.js` really wrote, under three different environments).

## 3.517.0 - the composer's boxes and the host's doors are counted against the dimension list — step 4 of 4 (X-152) (2026-09-15)

- **‼️ X-148's FAILURE NOW FAILS THE BUILD.** `providerId` and `tier` were once
  added to `LaunchOptions`, wired into the launcher, and simply never given a
  box in the Console composer — and nothing went red, because nothing counted.
  `test_console_intent.js` now reads the page's `askIntent` fields out of
  `media/console.js` and the host's `applyIntent` arms out of
  `src/panels/consolePanel.ts` and compares both against
  `LAUNCH_DIMENSIONS`: a box the host does not answer, a door no box reaches,
  and a user-answered dimension arriving with neither are each a separate red
  line. The five dimensions that are deliberately not in the strip (`name`,
  `prompt`, `resume`, `continueLast`, `cli`) are named with their reason and
  the exemption is itself checked, so it cannot quietly cover a sixth.
- **S-50 on the page, not only on the host.** A cold page — no saved state of
  its own, and a stale one from the build before this item — is booted through
  `lib_page_dom` and every box is read out of the markup: the engine, the
  model, the effort, the permission mode, the agent, the sign-in and the
  Superpowers chip all come from the bootstrap `composerIntent`, and nothing a
  previous build left in `afConsole` is drawn. And the page's convergence is
  measured from the page's own side: a box changed posts one `setIntent` and
  draws nothing meanwhile, and when the host's answer refuses the pick the
  page draws the ANSWER rather than keeping the value the hand chose.
- The four names `media/console.js` stripped out of a saved state by hand are
  now the dimension list itself (`AFDimensions.ids()` + the agent), so a
  dimension the page must never keep a copy of is covered by arriving.

## 3.516.0 - the composer's one-at-a-time fields and per-field messages are gone — step 3 of 4 (X-152) (2026-09-15)

- **‼️ ONE STATEMENT OF THE SETUP ON THE WIRE, AND ONE DOOR INTO IT.** The host
  no longer pushes `engine`, `composerPick`, `composerAccount`,
  `superpowersChoice`, `composerLaunch`, `defaults` or `presetAgent`, and the
  agent rows no longer carry `lastLaunch`/`engineDefaults` (the host reads
  both itself when the engine moves — `moveEngine`). `composerIntent` +
  `composerAgent` + `composerPrompt` are the whole of what the page is told
  about the next session. `setEngine`, `setRoute`, `setAccount` and
  `setSuperpowers` are not doors any more: a message by one of those names
  changes nothing (measured), `setIntent` is the one message, and the parity
  manifest lost the four entries.
- `composerLaunch` (the one-shot setup record) is reduced to what it really
  was for: `composerPrompt`, the first prompt a launcher handed over, into the
  draft once per seed and let go on the next start. A plain door (an agent
  row) leaves no prompt pending. The `presetAgent` one-shot is gone with it —
  the record is stated on every push, so the cold-open failure it caused
  (S-50: a payload dropped on the way could never be said again) has no
  mechanism left to happen through.
- Gates: `test_console_intent.js` (the retired names are not doors; the
  one-at-a-time fields are off the wire), `test_console_cold_open.js` (S-50
  reads the record and the prompt; the agent is stated again on the next
  refresh, not spent), `test_console_agent_default.js` §5, `test_launch_parity.js`,
  `test_parity.js`; fixtures carry only the record. Step 4 adds the S-50/S-51
  gates on the record and the dimension matrix.

## 3.515.0 - the Console composer is a pure view of the host's record — step 2 of 4 (X-152) (2026-09-15)

- **‼️ THE PAGE KEEPS NO COPY OF THE NEXT SESSION'S SETUP.** `media/console.js`
  no longer holds `agentId`, `model`, `effort` or `permissionMode` in its own
  state (a saved state that still carries them is stripped on load); every box
  on the strip is drawn from `DATA.composerIntent` + `DATA.composerAgent`, and
  every change — agent, engine, model, effort, permission mode, route, tier,
  sign-in, the Superpowers chip — is ONE message, `setIntent { field, value }`,
  posted through `askIntent`. There is no reconcile on the page any more
  (`reconcileComposer`, `memoryOn` and the engine handler's memory/Settings
  lookup are gone — the host's `narrowComposer` and `moveEngine` are the one
  rule), no local echo, and no half-answer drawn while the host thinks.
- **‼️ S-51 IS THE ECHO, DRAWN THE MOMENT IT LANDS.** `askedHost` lets the
  host's answer through M-33 with the hand still on the picker, and the box the
  rebuild replaced gets focus back (`refocus`) — an arrow-key walk through the
  engine list keeps its place. M-33 itself is untouched: a rebuild nobody asked
  for still waits for `focusout`. And the boxes MIRROR the record on every
  pass, not only on a rebuild: a value the host narrowed away is corrected in
  the control, never left as the hand's pick over a different truth.
- **Send carries content only** (`start { text, attach }`): the host starts from
  `composerAgent` and `composerIntent` — model/effort from the record, then the
  agent's own Settings row, then the fleet; the discipline from the record's
  third answer (`undefined` = the agent's own default, resolved host-side now).
  `resume` reads the boxes off the record too. The first prompt a door handed
  over is the one part of a setup that is content, and it travels as
  `composerPrompt` into the draft, once per seed.
- Fixtures carry `composerIntent`/`composerAgent` (`intentOf`); the
  engine-switch scene photographs the host's answer rather than pressing a
  picker into a harness with nobody to answer it. Gates repointed:
  `test_console_page.js` (S-49 · S-51 · route · account read the record and
  measure `setIntent`), `test_console_agent_default.js` (`startWith` sets the
  record the way the page does), `test_launch_parity.js`, `test_resume_dims.js`,
  `test_console.js`. Step 3 retires `setEngine/setRoute/setAccount/
  setSuperpowers` and the one-at-a-time fields on the host; step 4 adds the
  S-50/S-51 gates on the record.

## 3.514.0 - a saved setup that names no agent is given one ONCE and keeps it; Edit has an Agent row (X-180) (2026-09-15)

- **‼️ "PRESSING A SETUP IS THE START" WAS NOT TRUE OF A SETUP WITH A QUESTION

- The user's three "Developer …" profiles were pinned to `developer` through

## 3.513.0 - the composer's intent has one owner, the host — step 1 of 4 (X-152) (2026-09-15)

- **‼️ ONE RECORD FOR THE NEXT SESSION.** The strip's answers lived in two
  places with five rules between them: the engine, the route, the sign-in and
  the discipline on the host (each its own field, each pruned by its own
  handler), the model, the effort and the permission mode in the page's own
  state (narrowed there, seeded from a one-shot record the page had to notice),
  and Send stitched the halves back together. Every race this family is named
  after — the cold open losing the setup (S-50), the boxes answering only when
  the hand let go (S-51) — was that seam. `ConsolePanel.composerIntent` is the
  seam closed: every dimension in one `LaunchIntent`, held on the host, narrowed
  there by the one rule (`core/aflaunch.ts` = `media/afLaunch.js`, X-149),
  changed by one message (`setIntent { field, value }`), pushed to the page
  whole (`composerIntent` + `composerAgent`). The four old fields are accessors
  over it; the doors seed it (`seedIntent`); moving the engine re-answers the
  three under it on the host (`moveEngine`: memory → the agent's own setting →
  narrowed). `setIntent` is on the parity manifest beside `setRoute`.
- **Nothing on screen changes in this step.** The page still reads the older
  one-at-a-time fields and keeps its own copy; step 2 makes it a pure view
  (reads `composerIntent`, posts `setIntent`, keeps only the draft and the
  attachments), step 3 retires the per-field messages, step 4 adds the S-50/S-51
  gates. The plan with all four steps is in the project's X-148 plan note, §6.
- Gate: `test_console_intent.js` — the whole intent is in the bootstrap payload
  narrowed; `setIntent` changes one field and ignores a dimension the record
  does not hold; moving the engine re-answers model/effort/permission from THIS
  agent's row for the new engine and drops the old engine's route; a hand-picked
  model takes its own default effort, an unknown one drops to Default; a plain
  door seeds memory → own setting → fleet; after Send the route, the sign-in and
  the discipline clear while the engine and the boxes stay.

## 3.512.0 - the Start Session… icon opens ON your saved setups — no agent question first, one press is the start (X-180) (2026-09-15)

- **‼️ THE LIST STILL CAME SECOND.** 3.511.0 put the saved setups on the right
  door but still asked the agent first, and the item said the opposite in as
  many words: *press the icon and the profiles appear*. The reason it could not
  be first was structural — a profile did not know who it was for.
- **A profile now knows its agent.** The launcher is opened for one agent, so
  **Save** and **Replace** write `agentId` into the profile (the bridge's
  `launch.profile.save` takes `agentId?` too). Pressing the **Start Session…**
  icon opens straight on the saved setups; each row says *who · where*; pressing
  one **is** the start — no agent question, no second confirmation. A setup
  saved before profiles carried an agent asks for one, once, and says so when
  the agent it named has left the fleet.
- The first row, `Full setup…`, is the old flow untouched: the agent, then the
  dialog. Nothing saved → no list. A door that already knows the agent (a row's
  own Start Session… menu, the agent page, the portfolio) starts that agent on
  the pressed setup. The inline ▶ is untouched.
- Gates: `test_run_surface.js` measures the layer in front of `resolveAgent`
  and the profile's agent taking precedence; `test_launch_profiles.js` — Save
  stores the agent, Replace stores the one in front of the user and keeps the
  row's when it does not know, a profile that never named one stays that way,
  and `agentId` is not a dimension a load applies or a match compares.

## 3.511.0 - the saved-setup list is on the door it was asked for, ▶ is itself again, and a Console card starts on Dialog (X-180 · K-40) (2026-09-15)

- **‼️ X-180 HAD BEEN BUILT ON THE WRONG DOOR.** The item named the panel's
  **Start Session…** icon and the row's Start Session… menu — `agentfarm.launchSession`,
  the door that opens the full launcher — and the discovery note said so by name,
  with a warning not to confuse it with the inline ▶. 3.510.0 put the layer on the
  ▶ (`agentfarm.startSession`) anyway: the icon the user pressed did not change at
  all, and the one-click ▶ gained a profile list it had never asked for. Both
  undone in one move — **▶ is byte-for-byte what it was before 3.510.0**, and the
  saved-setup list now sits in front of the full launcher, where it belongs:
  agent known → your saved setups, first row `Full setup…` opens the dialog
  exactly as before, pressing a setup **is** the start. Nothing saved → no list.
  A caller that already names a surface (the agent page's Launch button) goes
  straight to the dialog, as before.
- The gate in `test_run_surface.js` now measures the right door — the layer in
  front of `runLauncher`, and **▶ carrying none of it** — and the two windows
  that had been widened to make room for the misplaced prose are back to size.
- **‼️ K-40 — A NEW CONSOLE CARD SOMETIMES OPENED ON "EVERYTHING".** K-38 kept
  ONE value — the last `show` anybody set on any card — and a panel opening cold
  seeded every unfiltered card from it, so one "everything" on one card put every
  session that arrived afterwards on everything: K-21's defect again, one
  panel-open later. Now **every card starts on Dialog**, and the panel default is
  not a memory. What K-38 was really asked for — *the filter I chose survives the
  panel closing* — is kept, and kept better: the reading is filed by the host
  **under the card's own CLI session id** (the one thing about a card that
  survives a reload; the Console's `cs…` ids do not), bounded to the newest
  hundred, and the same session comes back on it — the card beside it does not.
  The picker says so on itself. `sessionViewer`'s widening on a deep link that
  Dialog would hide (S-4) is deliberate and untouched.
- Gates: `test_console_show.js` (the memory is per session, a later push finds
  its record, the page's own answer wins, the earlier build's panel-wide
  `null` is not honoured; host side measured on the source), `test_console_tail.js`
  seeds its filter on the card.

## 3.510.0 - Start Session offers the setups you already saved, and pressing one IS the start (X-180) (2026-09-14)

- **‼️ THE COMMON PRESS WAS THE LONGEST PATH.** Pressing ▶ opened the full
  launcher — the right surface for building a NEW setup or assembling a one-off,
  and the wrong one for "open the setup I already keep". Reaching a saved
  profile meant walking down into the profile rows, loading one, then coming
  back up to Start: three moves for an answer that was already written down.
- **The saved setups are now offered the moment the agent is known**, and
  pressing one **is** the launch — no second confirmation. The full dialog is
  the first row of that list (`Full setup…`) and **nothing about it changed**:
  every step, every row, save/load/edit, all exactly as before, simply behind
  one keypress.
- **‼️ WITH NOTHING SAVED THE LAYER DOES NOT EXIST.** An empty profile list
  falls straight through to the dialog and draws nothing — a person who keeps no
  profiles must not pay a keypress for a list with one row in it, and that is
  also the state every machine starts in.
- **The setup is reproduced through the launcher's own two functions**
  (`profileAccountGone` then `applyProfile`), never a hand-built object: a
  dimension the profile stores and this path forgot would be a session quietly
  running as something else, which is the exact defect A-11 and X-103 were
  written for. A sign-in that has since left the machine is dropped **and said**
  (X-253), and the account is otherwise resolved by `launchAccountFor` (X-169).
- **A profile that never stored a surface is ASKED, not guessed.** Every profile
  saved before A-11 says nothing about where it runs, and the two answers are
  not interchangeable — a terminal spawns the CLI now, the Console opens a
  composer that spawns on the first message. Picking one for the reader would be
  the same silent substitution the account guard refuses.
- The Console arm keeps K-34 (it opens its composer and does not spawn; Send is
  the launch and Send records it); the terminal arm records with the one shared
  recorder like every other door.
- Guarded by six new gates in `test_run_surface.js`. Two windows in that file
  were widened rather than trimmed: it measures the source with fixed character
  slices, so the reason written in front of a measured line reads exactly like
  the line having been deleted — the trap its own comment names.

## 3.509.0 - When nobody set a vault folder, Obsidian is asked — and when it cannot answer, it SAYS so (X-308) (2026-09-14)

- **‼️ THE DEFECT WAS THE SILENCE, NOT THE LAW.** `agentFarm.vaultDir` had never
  been set on the measured machine, so `${vault}` resolved to nothing and X-188's
  law — an unresolved variable CANCELS the path — skipped every path setting that
  used it. That is the correct behaviour. What was wrong is that **no surface
  said a word**: a handover folder, a sentry template pool and an answer folder
  were all being silently passed over, and the only way to find out was to read
  the resolver. It was seen live during X-307's evidence round.
- **Obsidian already knows.** Its own registry (`%APPDATA%/obsidian/obsidian.json`
  on Windows, the platform equivalents elsewhere) lists every vault with an
  `open` flag. When the setting is empty and **exactly one** vault is open, that
  folder now answers `${vault}` — and the value is marked as DERIVED everywhere
  it is shown, because it can change under the user without anybody editing a
  setting.
- **‼️ THE SETTING ALWAYS WINS.** This is a fallback, never an override. A person
  who typed a folder has answered the question, and an extension that quietly
  prefers its own guess over their answer is worse than one that never guesses.
- **‼️ AND IT REFUSES TO GUESS BETWEEN TWO.** More than one vault can be open at
  once — measured in `docopen.ts`, on this same machine, in the sibling problem
  of which vault a URI lands in. Two open vaults, or none, or no Obsidian at all
  are each a **refusal with a sentence**: the variable stays unresolved exactly
  as before, and the reason names what it could not choose between. A wrong
  vault would file the work somewhere nobody looks; that is worse than the
  silence this replaces.
- **Three surfaces, one fact.** `farm.health` gains a `vault` block (value,
  `ok`, `source`, `why`, how many vaults are known and how many are open), the
  Settings page's variable legend draws the vault chip as derived and opens its
  panel on the value → the reason → the meaning, and `settings.paths` carries
  the same `source`/`note` because all three read the one shared function.
- **One registry, one path function.** `docopen.ts` had its own copy of the
  per-platform `obsidian.json` location; it now calls the new module's, so the
  two readers of that file cannot drift apart.
- Guarded by `test_vault_discovery.js` (27 checks) — including **this machine's
  real registry replayed as a fixture**: four vaults, exactly one open, landing
  on the vault every agent actually writes to. Two new scenes on the settings
  fixture draw the derived value and the two-open refusal, both with the panel
  really open.

## 3.508.0 - On a narrow panel the composer's WORDS go short, and every box stays a box (U-136) (2026-09-14)

- **‼️ THE BOXES WERE NOT THE PROBLEM — THE RIGHT-HAND GROUP WAS.** Measured on
  the console fixture at a 900px panel (row 530px): the four live pickers
  (model · effort · account · permission) were laid out at **ZERO pixels** each,
  and the row *still* ran **73px past the panel**, which put Send outside it.
  So crushing the boxes bought nothing: it destroyed the controls and did not
  stop the overflow. The width was going to `#c-live`, which is `flex:none` and
  took **309px of 530** on its own — `3 held` + `drop all` + `Send after turn` +
  `⎋ Interrupt +2`.
- **The words give way, not the controls.** Each label in that group is now a
  long form and a short one (`Send after turn` → `⏭`, `drop all` → `⨯`,
  `⎋ Interrupt +2` → `⎋ +2`, `3 held` → `3⏸`), and the stylesheet picks between
  them with a **container query on `.composer`** — so a wide window with a
  narrow composer is still narrow. The long form is the first line of the
  button's own title, which is the SHORTHAND rule this repo already runs on.
  Two thresholds, because a held message adds two controls: 780px with them,
  680px without.
- **And a floor under every picker.** `.crow .axisw` keeps `min-width:28px` —
  the width of a closed select's arrow. The reader may lose the *value* at a
  narrow width, never the *box*: it still opens, and its AFTip reads it out.
  Nothing is dropped from the row at any width.
- **Below a 520px composer the row wraps** instead of overflowing: at that width
  the fixed load alone (agent + engine + show + the right-hand group + Send,
  none of which shrink) is 382px against a 288px row, so no box is small enough
  to make it fit. The wrap is fenced *inside* the container query on purpose —
  turned on for every width it pushed 21 of 46 rows onto a second line at
  1200px, because a wrapped flex item does not shrink to avoid its own wrap.
- **The gaps go before any box does**, at 3px under 780px: eleven children are
  ten gaps, and a gap holds no information.
- **Measured after, at every width** (console fixture, all 46 rows, 560→1400px):
  overflow **0 everywhere**, no box below its floor, nothing dropped, and
  1200/1400px byte-for-byte the row it already was — long labels, one line.
  Guarded by three new gates in `test_console_identity_width.js` that read the
  laid-out DOM: no picker crushed, nothing past the panel with Send inside it,
  and the long/short swap actually happening.
- **The overlap gate was wrong about its own subject.** It compared a `<button>`
  with the `<span>` *inside* it and called the containment a 40-80px collision.
  A control that carries its own wording always encloses what it draws, so the
  scan now skips pairs where one contains the other.

## 3.507.0 - The campaign that reopened the same nothing four times now stops (X-307) (2026-09-14)

- **‼️ A ROUND THAT ANSWERS AND LEAVES NOTHING IS NOW A BARREN ROUND.**
  Measured on a live campaign (`sc-mu15qwp8`, four rounds, all on `P-1`,
  ~$0.08 each): the sessions ran with `acceptEdits` in an agent folder while
  their target was in the vault, so each one took exactly one turn — a
  sentence saying a write permission was needed — and ended `done` having
  written nothing. That is not `nothing-to-continue` (something *was*
  attempted), so it reached `hit-the-wall`, which the failure brake did not
  count. The leader diagnosed the same item, reopened the same round, and
  would have run until morning. `failLimit` was 2 and never fired.
- **The verdict now carries `left`** (`something` | `nothing` | `unknown`):
  did the session leave a trace anywhere — an item touched, an uncommitted
  path, a handover note. All three must have been really measured; an
  unmeasured fact reads `unknown` and never brakes a campaign, which is the
  same law the rest of `sessionDiagnosis` already states.
- **One outcome, two walls.** `hit-the-wall` splits its rule into
  `wall-limit` (the engine said the plan window was spent — not the
  campaign's fault, and it reopens by itself) and `wall-unfinished` (the
  session ended on its own). Only the second can be barren.
- **`sentry.status` says what each round actually said** — `lastText`, the
  session's closing sentence on one line, capped at 200 characters with a
  leading `…` when it was cut, so a short answer reads as short. Four rounds
  saying the same thing is the whole diagnosis; before this it cost one
  `tasks.get` per round to find out.
- **And the trap is named where it is set** — `sentry.start`'s
  `permissionMode` and the campaign form's Permissions tooltip now say the
  measured half out loud: `acceptEdits` approves writes inside the round's
  own working folder and nothing outside it, so an unattended round whose
  target is elsewhere needs `bypassPermissions`.

## 3.506.0 - Stop reaches the commands the turn left running behind it (S-62) (2026-09-14)

- **‼️ "I STOPPED IT AND IT WENT ON" — THE SECOND WAY, MEASURED AND CLOSED.**
  S-54 closed the first (a message queued into the turn). This is the other: a
  Bash call the model backgrounded (`run_in_background`) survives Interrupt,
  and when it finishes the CLI writes `task_notification` and — with nobody
  typing — opens a NEW turn on its own to hand the model the result, which
  then carries on with the original work. Measured with `tools/probe_background.js`
  against claude-cli 2.1.269: Stop at 11 s, the process finished at 18 s, a
  new `system/init` and a new turn followed within 100 ms. `cancel_queued`
  cannot reach it: the notification does not exist yet when the interrupt is
  answered.
- **The CLI owns those processes and lists them itself** —
  `system/background_tasks_changed` is its whole live list, replaced on every
  change — **and offers `stop_task` for exactly this** (its own schema: a
  consumer without a per-task stop is meant to have Interrupt kill them, and
  this build measured as not doing so for a backgrounded shell). Interrupt now
  asks the CLI to stop EACH listed task before it aborts the turn. A task
  stopped that way notifies as `stopped`, which measured opens no turn, in
  either order.
- **The strip says what is still out there — one chip per process, with a ✕.**
  `⏳ Start the dev server on po… ✕` while the turn runs (and the button reads
  `⎋ Interrupt +2`, its tooltip naming what else it ends) AND after the turn
  is over, beside "your turn now" — which is the arity the reader actually
  meets and the one with no Interrupt button to press, so the ✕ is the only
  way to end the process. The panel carries the long form, how long it has run
  and what the CLI will do when it ends. A task that finishes on its own is a
  system row saying a new turn is being opened, so the turn that appears has
  a visible cause; a refused stop is an error row naming the command.
- **Bridge:** `console.stopTask { id, taskId }`; `console.sessions` rows carry
  `backgroundTasks`; `console.interrupt` reports `backgroundStopped`.
- The list is never derived by counting tool calls, and it OUTLIVES the turn on
  purpose. Reducer, host, page and fixture (three scenes: two running · one
  after the turn · none) are each pinned.

## 3.505.0 - Which sign-in ran cheap and which ran expensive, over a month (X-252 b) (2026-09-14)

- **‼️ EVERY HEADER BUTTON ON THE ENGINES PAGE WAS DEAD.** `AFHeader.wire(vscode,
  hooks)` takes the API first; `media/engines.js` handed it only the hooks, so
  the hooks object sat in the `vscode` slot and all 16 nav buttons called
  `postMessage` on something that has none — measured on the page harness:
  `vscode.postMessage is not a function`, `posted: []`. The header's own ⟳ fell
  through to the same dead call. Nothing could see it: both arguments are
  optional to the type checker, the page renders perfectly, every string test
  passes, and a photograph shows a row of buttons that look exactly like
  buttons. A press that silently does nothing is indistinguishable from one
  that is thinking. `test_wiring.js` now reads that call site on every page.
- **Task Analytics gains "Spend by sign-in (30d)"** — which plan paid for the
  month, what a run on each one usually costs, and the weighted tokens beside
  the money. ‼️ The ENGINE stays a COLUMN rather than being replaced: an account
  is under one engine, and dropping the coarser split would have thrown away the
  answer people already read.
- **The part of the month that belongs to nobody is a ROW, not a footnote.** A
  session this farm did not start carries no launch manifest, so no sign-in can
  be named for it without inventing one — and a reader adding the money column
  up has to be able to see why it falls short.
- **The way in is the figure itself.** The Engines card's `today …` line is the
  door to the breakdown and its panel says so; nothing was added beside it, and
  the resting card is drawn exactly as it was. The Dashboard's `Cost today`
  tile, which answered to no page at all, now names the one that explains it.
- The page had **no fixture** until now, which is how a section could be added
  to it and never looked at. It has one, with the arities that read differently:
  a fully priced sign-in, one part-priced, one where every run was on an engine
  that states no price, nothing attributed at all, and a host that cannot answer
  (where the section is absent rather than empty).

## 3.504.0 - A sign-in says what it spent, and the card is really handed what it draws (X-252 a/c/d) (2026-09-14)

- **‼️ FOUR FIELDS OF X-255 AND X-258 WERE NEVER REACHING THE PAGE.** The Engines
  page's `accounts()` dep forwarded a HAND-WRITTEN LIST of fields, and the list
  had stopped at X-269 — so `standingAgents` and `pinnedAgents` (X-255) and
  `onIt` and `line` (X-258) were built by the host, typed on the panel, drawn by
  `media/engines.js`, supplied by the fixture, and invisible on the real
  machine. Both items shipped green, were photographed and were closed, because
  every test and every photograph reads the fixture and **the fixture is not the
  wire**. Measured against the bridge, which forwards the same row whole and had
  all four. The dep now hands `publicAccount`'s row over by the SHAPE, and
  `test_engines_account_wire.js` refuses both halves of the mistake: a field
  list here, and a field the card is typed for that nothing builds.
- **A sign-in's card now says what it SPENT today** — `today $4.31 · ⚖ 1.8M ·
  7 runs` — under the percentage that only ever said how close the wall was.
  Cost was split by ENGINE and by nothing else; with five sign-ins under one
  engine, "what did this account cost today, whose window did that burn" had no
  answer anywhere after the fact, which is the whole economics of running more
  than one.
- **‼️ And it refuses three easy answers, each one out loud.** A run is placed on
  a sign-in by its own LAUNCH MANIFEST, so a session this farm did not start is
  counted nowhere rather than guessed onto whichever account the machine holds.
  An engine that publishes no price gets no money figure at all — its 0 is a
  missing figure, not a free day. A conversation that crossed midnight on an
  engine writing no per-day totals is left out of today rather than sliced by a
  ratio nobody measured; each refusal is a COUNT on the card's own panel. And a
  row whose host sent no figure draws **no line**, exactly as an unread window
  draws no bar.
- **A price change now invalidates the figures it invalidates.** The external
  scan remembered each parse against `size:mtimeMs` — the transcript's own file
  and nothing else — while every cost and weighted total in that parse comes
  from the price table and the quota weights. Editing either rebuilt the engine,
